content:
Wheel Hub Bearing & ABS Sensor Wholesale for Hyundai Kia

Wheel hub bearings and ABS wheel speed sensors are among the highest-turnover chassis parts in the Hyundai-Kia aftermarket. Every vehicle has four hub bearings and four ABS sensors, and they wear out on a predictable schedule — typically 80,000 to 120,000 km for bearings and 60,000 to 100,000 km for sensors in hot, dusty, or rough-road markets. This guide covers the five products in our Guangzhou warehouse, their OE reference numbers, pricing tiers, quality grades, and the technical details that procurement managers need when sourcing for distribution in Africa, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

Kingmay Auto Parts supplies hub bearings in Gen 2 (press-in) and Gen 3 (bolt-on) formats, ABS sensors in both Hall-effect active and magnetic passive types, and application-specific variants for the Hyundai Elantra/Cerato platform and the Tucson/Sportage SUV platform. All products carry ISO/TS 16949 certification and ship with 12-month warranty terms.

Product Catalog: Hub Bearings & ABS Sensors

The catalog spans 13 distinct OE reference numbers across five SKUs. The Elantra/Cerato hub (id=187) and Tucson/Sportage hub (id=188) are platform-specific, while the universal wheel bearing (id=68) and hub assembly (id=69) cover a wider range of Asian and Western vehicles. The ABS sensor (id=80) is cross-compatible with Hyundai, Kia, Toyota, Honda, Ford, and Audi applications.

Hub Bearing Generations: Gen 1 vs Gen 2 vs Gen 3

Hyundai and Kia vehicles use three generations of wheel hub bearing designs, and procurement managers must know which type fits their market's vehicle fleet. Ordering the wrong generation means the part cannot be installed without a hydraulic press and shop tooling that most aftermarket garages in developing markets do not have.

Generation Design Installation Typical Hyundai Kia Years ABS Ring
Gen 1 Tapered roller bearing pair (inner + outer), separable Press-in, requires hydraulic press Pre-2005 (Accent, Elantra HD, Sonata NF) External tone ring on CV joint
Gen 2 Double-row angular contact, unitized, press-in Press into steering knuckle 2005-2015 (Elantra MD, Cerato YD, Tucson LM) Integrated magnetic encoder
Gen 3 Flanged hub unit, bolt-on, pre-loaded Bolt directly to knuckle (no press needed) 2015+ (Elantra AD, Cerato BD, Tucson TL, Sportage QL) Integrated magnetic encoder

Our id=68 (Wheel Bearing) covers all three generations, while id=69 (Hub Bearing Assembly) focuses on Gen 2 and Gen 3 bolt-on units. The application-specific id=187 (Elantra/Cerato) and id=188 (Tucson/Sportage) are Gen 2 double-row angular contact bearings with integrated ABS encoder rings — the most common replacement type in markets where 2010-2020 Hyundai-Kia vehicles dominate the fleet.

ABS Wheel Speed Sensor: Technical Specifications

The ABS wheel speed sensor (id=80) is the electronic component that reads the magnetic encoder ring on the hub bearing and transmits wheel rotational speed data to the ABS/ESC control module. When a hub bearing is replaced, the ABS sensor is often damaged or contaminated during disassembly — which is why we recommend ordering sensors alongside bearings in a paired replacement strategy.

Specification Active (Hall-effect) Passive (Inductive)
Output Signal Digital square wave Analog sine wave
Operating Voltage 12V DC (vehicle supply) Self-generating (no supply)
Min Detectable Speed 0 km/h (static) ~3 km/h
Air Gap 0.5–1.3 mm (OEM spec) 0.5–1.3 mm (OEM spec)
Connector 2-pin sealed 2-pin
Cable Length OEM-matched (450–900 mm) OEM-matched (450–900 mm)
Temperature Range -40°C to +140°C -40°C to +150°C

Post-2010 Hyundai-Kia vehicles predominantly use active Hall-effect sensors because they can detect wheel speed at near-zero velocity, enabling hill-start assist, auto-hold braking, and more precise traction control. Passive inductive sensors are found on pre-2010 models and are cheaper but cannot detect speeds below 3 km/h. We supply both types with OEM-matched connectors and cable lengths.

Pricing Tiers & Wholesale Structure

Our FOB Guangzhou pricing follows a three-tier structure based on order quantity. All prices are in USD and include standard export packing (anti-corrosion oil + vacuum-sealed bag + carton). Prices do not include freight, insurance, or destination-country import duties.

Failure Diagnosis: When to Replace Hub Bearings & ABS Sensors

Hub bearing failure follows a predictable pattern. The first symptom is usually a humming or droning noise at speeds above 60 km/h that increases with vehicle speed. As the bearing degrades further, the noise becomes a grinding or growling sound, and vibration can be felt through the steering wheel or floor pan. In the final stage, the wheel develops play — detectable by jacking up the vehicle and rocking the wheel at the 12 and 6 o'clock positions.

ABS sensor failure is harder to diagnose because the sensor itself does not make noise. The most common symptom is an illuminated ABS warning light on the dashboard, accompanied by a stored trouble code (C1201-C1299 on Hyundai-Kia vehicles). Other indicators include: traction control activating unexpectedly on dry roads, speedometer fluctuations at low speed, and transmission harshness (some Hyundai-Kia 6-speed automatics use the rear ABS sensor for output shaft speed calculation).

The critical pairing issue: when a Gen 2 or Gen 3 hub bearing with an integrated ABS encoder ring is replaced, the old ABS sensor must be removed from the old bearing and reinstalled in the new one. During this process, the sensor tip can be contaminated with metallic debris from the worn bearing, causing immediate ABS light illumination after the repair. We recommend replacing the ABS sensor whenever the hub bearing is replaced on vehicles with over 100,000 km — the $12-$48 sensor cost is small compared to the labor cost of redoing the job.

Quality Grades: OEM vs OES vs Aftermarket

We supply three quality grades for hub bearings and ABS sensors. The grade selection depends on the target market's price sensitivity and the buyer's warranty policy.

OEM Grade — Manufactured by the same Tier 1 suppliers that supply Hyundai-Kia assembly lines (ILJIN, SCHAEFFLER/FAG, NSK, NTN). These bearings carry the OEM part number stamped on the outer race and come in original packaging. Prices are at th e top of the range ($65-$85 for universal, $30-$38 for application-specific). Best for buyers who serve dealership networks or offer 24-month warranties.

OES Grade — Manufactured to OEM specifications by Tier 2 suppliers with ISO/TS 16949 certification. These use the same bearing steel (SUJ2 / 100Cr6), same seal design, and same grease specification as OEM, but may use a slightly different cage material or surface finish. Prices are 30-40% below OEM. This is our best-selling grade for distributors in Nigeria, Kenya, and the UAE who want OEM-level reliability at a competitive price point.

Aftermarket Economy — Manufactured to dimensional specifications but with standard-grade bearing steel and commercial-grade seals. Prices are 50-60% below OEM. Suitable for markets where the average vehicle age exceeds 12 years and the buyer prioritizes low cost over long service life. We do not recommend this grade for ABS sensors because the Hall-effect IC quality varies significantly between suppliers.

Container Loading & Shipping from Guangzhou

Hub bearings and ABS sensors are dense, compact parts that pack efficiently. A standard 20-foot container can hold approximately 4,000-5,000 hub bearing cartons and 6,000-8,000 ABS sensor boxes, depending on the SKU mix. All products are individually boxed with anti-corrosion treatment (VCI paper + desiccant) and then packed in 5-ply export cartons with foam dividers.

Shipping options from Guangzhou:

  • Sea freight (LCL): 15-25 days to Mombasa, 18-28 days to Lagos, 12-18 days to Dubai, 10-15 days to Manila. Minimum order $2,000. Ideal for first-time buyers testing the market.
  • Sea freight (FCL 20ft): Same transit times, lower per-unit cost. Minimum order $15,000. Recommended for established distributors.
  • Air freight: 3-7 days worldwide. Cost is $4-$8/kg for bearings (heavy) and $2-$4/kg for sensors (light). Used for emergency restocking.
  • Courier (DHL/FedEx): 3-5 days. Used for samples and small orders under 30 kg.

Export documentation includes commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin (FORM A for GSP-eligible destinations), and ISO/TS 16949 certificate copy. HS code for hub bearings: 8482.10.00; for ABS sensors: 9031.80.90.

FAQ: Hyundai Kia Hub Bearing & ABS Sensor Wholesale

How long do Hyundai Kia wheel hub bearings last?

OEM-grade hub bearings typically last 100,000-150,000 km under normal driving conditions. In markets with poor road surfaces (unpaved roads, potholes), high ambient temperatures (Middle East, Africa), and heavy vehicle loading (taxis, ride-share), the service life drops to 60,000-90,000 km. Gen 3 bolt-on bearings tend to last longer than Gen 2 press-in bearings because the factory-set preload eliminates installation error. We recommend inspecting hub bearings at every tire rotation (10,000 km) and replacing them at the first sign of noise — continuing to drive on a failed bearing can damage the CV joint, steering knuckle, and ABS sensor tone ring.

What are the symptoms of a failing ABS wheel speed sensor?

The most common symptom is an illuminated ABS warning light with a stored trouble code (C1201-C1299 on Hyundai-Kia). Other signs include: intermittent traction control activation on dry roads, speedometer needle fluctuation at low speeds (below 20 km/h), transmission harshness or delayed shifting (on Hyundai-Kia 6-speed automatics that use the rear wheel speed sensor for output sha ft speed), and disabled hill-start assist. To diagnose, use an OBD-II scanner to read the ABS module codes, then check the suspect sensor's resistance (passive: 1,000-2,500 ohms; active: 12V supply with digital output) and inspect the sensor tip for metallic debris contamination from a worn hub bearing.

Should I replace the ABS sensor when replacing the hub bearing?

Yes, for vehicles over 100,000 km. The ABS sensor sits inside the hub bearing's magnetic encoder ring, and when the bearing wears, metallic debris from the worn race and balls contaminates the sensor tip. Removing the sensor from the old bearing and reinstalling it in the new one often results in immediate ABS light illumination because the debris cannot be fully cleaned from the Hall-effect IC. The sensor costs $12-$48 (depending on grade and quantity) versus $15-$85 for the bearing — replacing both at the same time saves the labor cost of a second disassembly and ensures the ABS system functions correctly after the repair.

What is the difference between 51720-1G000 and 51720-2H000?

Both are front wheel hub bearings for the Hyundai Elantra / Kia Cerato platform, but they fit different model years. 51720-1G000 is for the Hyundai Elantra YD/HD (2006-2010) and Kia Cerato TD (2006-2011) with 4-bolt pattern (4×100). 51720-2H000 is for the Hyundai Elantra MD (2011-2015) and Kia Cerato YD (2012-2016) with 5-bolt pattern (5×114.3). 51720-A7000 is the latest version for the Elantra AD (2016-2020) and Cerato BD (2017-2021). All three use a Gen 2 double-row angular contact bearing with integrated ABS encoder ring, but the bolt pattern, hub diameter, and tone ring polarity differ — they are not interchangeable.

What is the minimum order quantity for hub bearings?

MOQ is 10 pieces per SKU for the universal wheel bearing (id=68) and hub assembly (id=69), and 20 pieces per SKU for the application-specific Elantra (id=187) and Tucson (id=188) variants. ABS sensors (id=80) have a 20-piece MOQ. Sample orders of 1-9 pieces are accepted at the sample-tier price (top of the range). For new distributors, we recommend starting with a 50-piece mixed order (10 pcs × 5 SKUs) to test market demand, then scaling to container orders once sell-through is confirmed.

Do you provide warranty on hub bearings and ABS sensors?

Yes. All products carry a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects (bearing race cracking, ball spalling, seal failure, sensor IC malfunction). The warranty starts from the bill of lading date and covers replacement of the defective part — it does not cover labor costs for removal and reinstallation. OEM-grade bearings from ILJIN/FAG/NSK carry an extended 24-month warranty when purchased in quantities of 50+ per SKU. Warranty claims require photos of the defective part, the lot number stamped on the outer race or sensor housing, and the original commercial invoice.

The Dolphin undercuts the MG4 by $5,092, which matters in price-first markets like Nigeria, but the MG4 EV's 170 hp vs the Dolphin's 95 hp is a 79% power difference — a major factor for highway driving and fleet resale value. The MG ZS EV sits alone in the comparison — no other Chinese brand offers a 440 km LFP compact SUV at under $20,000 FOB, which is why fleet operators in Thailand and Australia order it in volume.

Charging, Battery & Real-World Range

Both MG models use LFP (lithium iron phosphate) chemistry — the same thermal-stability profile as BYD's Blade Battery, without the nickel-cobalt supply-chain cost. LFP cells tolerate higher operating temperatures (safe up to 60°C cell surface), which suits Middle East and African climates where summer cabin temperatures can exceed 55°C. Cycle life is 2,000+ full charges to 80% capacity, roughly 400,000-500,000 km of usable battery life.

DC fast charging: the MG4 EV charges 30-80% in about 26 minutes on a 117 kW charger; the ZS EV takes about 36 minutes on its 88 kW limit. Home charging on a 7 kW wallbox: the MG4 EV (51 kWh) takes about 7.5 hours for 0-100%; the ZS EV takes 7.3 hours. For importers in markets without public DC networks, every MG EV ships with the Type 2 CCS2 charging port (EU standard) — verify your market's charging standard before ordering, because the CCS2-combo inlet cannot be field-converted to CHAdeMO or GB/T.

Real-world range depends on driving style and climate. In warm-climate city driving (25-35 km/h average), the MG4 EV delivers 320-340 km per charge; highway driving at 120 km/h cuts this to 260-280 km. The ZS EV's larger pack and SUV aero profile return 390-410 km city / 310-330 km highway. Buyers planning daily routes over 300 km should choose the ZS EV or the higher-capacity 64 kWh MG4 EV variant (available on request).

United Kingdom: The MG4 EV's home export market. MG has UK dealer coverage in 140+ locations and the MG4 EV was the best-selling Chinese EV in the UK in 2024-2025. Import duty on Chinese-built EVs to the UK is currently 10% (MFN rate; no anti-dumping duty applies as of August 2026, but UK TTP reviews are ongoing — confirm the duty rate with your broker at booking time). VAT is 20%.

Australia: Zero import duty under the China-Australia FTA, 10% GST, and established MG dealer network. The ZS EV is the volume seller; the MG4 EV appeals to private buyers and fleets wanting a sport hatchback. The main cost is ocean freight from Nansha to Sydney or Melbourne ($1,200-$1,400/unit).

UAE and Saudi Arabia: 5% import duty plus 5% VAT (UAE) or 15% VAT (Saudi). Summer heat favors LFP chemistry. The UAE's EV registration incentives (free Salik tags, priority parking) push MG4 EV demand in Dubai, where the 351 km WLTP range is more than enough for daily commutes.

Kenya and Nigeria: Kenya applies 0% import duty on pure EVs (2024 waiver) — the cheapest African landing point at $21,918 landed. Nigeria has no EV duty waiver; standard 20% duty plus 7.5% VAT applies. In both markets, the lack of public fast charging makes the ZS EV's 440 km range and LFP battery the stronger proposition.

Thailand: BOI-registered EV imports enter at 0% duty. The Thai government's EV 3.5 scheme requires approved importers to assemble or source locally in later years — new importers should partner with an existing BOI licensee or accept the standard 60% duty for direct imports. MG has a factory in Thailand (SAIC-CP, Chonburi), so check whether import duty is avoidable by sourcing locally built units.

Brazil: Chinese EV imports face 18% import duty plus state ICMS (~18%). The federal government's 2026 EV incentive program provides a temporary PIS/COFINS exemption for EVs priced under R$250,000, which the MG4 EV qualifies for — verify the program is still active at import time. MG's Brazilian dealer network is expanding and offers strong residual values.

FAQ: 2026 MG4 EV & MG ZS EV Export from China

What is the FOB price of the MG4 EV and MG ZS EV?

The MG4 EV 51kWh Luxury is USD $17,800 FOB Nansha at single-unit pricing, dropping to $17,400 at 5+ units and $17,000 at 20+. The MG ZS EV 51kWh is $19,800 FOB, $19,400 at 5+, and $19,000 at 20+. Prices include CCC certificate, UN38.3 battery documentation, MIIT files, standard export packing, and pre-shipment inspection. A 64 kWh MG4 EV long-range variant is available on request at a $2,500 premium.

Are MG4 EV and MG ZS EV made in China or Europe?

Export units from our Nansha warehouse are built by SAIC Motor's Nanjing and Zhengzhou plants in China. MG also assembles some models at its Chonburi, Thailand plant (SAIC-CP) and has announced a European assembly operation for 2027, but current export volume to the UK, Australia, and Africa ships from Chinese plants. Buyers sourcing for Thailand should ask whether locally assembled units qualify for the BOI duty exemption.

What is the real-world driving range of the MG4 EV?

The MG4 EV 51kWh has a WLTP-certified range of 351 km. In warm city driving expect 320-340 km per charge; at 120 km/h highway speed expect 260-280 km. The figure is WLTP, not CLTC — Chinese-market CLTC ratings run 10-15% higher than real driving, so WLTP numbers are the conservative, reliable ones for export buyers.

How does the MG4 EV compare to the BYD Dolphin?

The MG4 EV is $5,092 more expensive than the BYD Dolphin 410km ($17,800 vs $12,708 FCA) but offers 79% more power (170 vs 95 hp), rear-wheel drive, a 2,705 mm wheelbase versus 2,700 mm, and WLTP range certification. The Dolphin wins on price; the MG4 wins on driving dynamics, power, and fleet resale appeal in Europe and Australia. Choose the Dolphin for price-first emerging markets, the MG4 EV for markets where the buyer values performance and RWD.

What warranty does the MG4 EV and MG ZS EV carry for export?

Both models carry a 7-year / 150,000 km vehicle warranty and a 7-year / 150,000 km battery warranty on LFP packs (whichever comes first), honored through MG's global dealer network in most markets. Export buyers should confirm warranty transferability with their destination country's MG distributor — in markets without an MG dealer, Globalucar provides a 12-month exporter warranty covering battery and drivetrain defects, with claims processed through our Guangzhou service center.

Can I mix MG EVs and petrol MG5 sedans in one container?

Yes. A 40ft HQ container fits 2 EVs + 2 MG5 sedans (mixed load), which spreads container cost across units. Mixed loads are a practical way for first-time importers to test both the EV and petrol markets in one shipment.

Why Body & Lighting Parts Drive Collision Repair Sales

Body and lighting parts are the highest-volume, fastest-turning category in the global collision repair aftermarket. Every minor front-end impact on a Toyota Corolla, Honda Civic, or Hyundai Elantra creates an order for at least one headlight, one bumper cover, and often a fender and grille. In markets where traffic density is high and road conditions are rough — Nigeria, Kenya, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Thailand, and the Philippines — front-end and side-impact damage is the single most common insurance claim, and repair shops restock these parts every week rather than every month.

For importers, body and lighting parts behave differently from mechanical parts. They are bulky (bumpers and fenders consume container space), finish-dependent (parts ship primed and are painted locally, so paint code matching is a local job), and highly model-specific (a 2019 Toyota Corolla front bumper will not fit a 2016 model). The buyers who succeed in this category are those who standardize on a narrow set of high-volume platforms and stock the four fastest-moving part groups: bumper covers, fenders, headlights, and tail lamps. This guide covers all four for the Toyota Corolla/Camry/RAV4, Honda Civic/CR-V, and Hyundai Elantra/Kia Sportage platform families — the vehicles that dominate used-car fleets across emerging markets.

Kingmay Auto Parts ships primed bumper covers, stamped steel fenders, and halogen-to-LED headlight assemblies from our Guangzhou warehouse with export packing designed for sea freight. All parts carry ISO 9001 / IATF 16949 factory certification and a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects, excluding paint (parts ship primed, unpainted) and damage caused in transit.

Headlight Types: Halogen vs Projector vs Full LED

Headlights are the single most expensive item in most collision repair orders, and the technology varies widely by model year and trim. Ordering the wrong type means the assembly will not plug in, will not match the vehicle's wiring, or will fail a roadworthiness inspection. Three types cover nearly all Toyota, Honda, and Hyundai-Kia vehicles from 2015 to 2024:

The critical compatibility rule: full LED assemblies on 2018+ Toyota Camry and RAV4 require the vehicle's CAN-bus lighting module and sometimes a beam-height sensor calibration. Installing a full LED assembly on a car originally built with a halogen setup usually triggers a dashboard error or leaves the LED DRL inoperative. Before ordering, buyers should provide the VIN of the target vehicle so our technical team can confirm the correct connector, DRL wiring, and any module requirements.

Steel vs Plastic Fenders: Application Guide

Fenders are the second most replaced body panel after bumper covers, and the material choice matters more than most importers realize. Chinese factories produce both stamped steel fenders and PP/ABS plastic fenders for the same vehicle platforms, and the right choice depends on the market's repair culture and cost structure.

For Toyota Corolla and Camry, the factory-installed fender is always stamped steel, so OEM-matched repairs use steel. Plastic fenders are an aftermarket economy option that reduces weight and cost but does not match the original part's stiffness or structural behavior in the wheel arch. In markets where the buyer is a body shop competing on repair price, plastic fenders are common; in markets where the buyer is an insurer or fleet operator requiring original-equivalent repairs, steel is the standard. We stock both and price them separately so distributors can serve both segments from one container.

Quality Grades: Genuine vs OEM-Grade vs Aftermarket

Body and lighting parts are available in three quality grades, and the differences matter for warranty exposure and customer satisfaction in collision repair:

Genuine (Genuine Toyota / Honda Genuine / MOBIS) — Produced by the OEM or its licensed supplier, sold in OEM packaging with the maker's part number and 12-month factory warranty. Prices run 2-3x the OEM-grade equivalent. Used by dealership networks and insurer-mandated repairs. For most independent body shops, genuine parts price a repair out of the market.

OEM-Grade — Produced in IATF 16949-certified Chinese factories on OEM tooling or reverse-engineered to OEM dimensions, from OEM-grade PP (bumpers) or stamped steel from OEM-spec coils (fenders). Dimensional accuracy is within OEM tolerance, so fit-up is direct with no drilling or shimming. This is our recommended grade for distributors serving independent body shops: the fit is right, the price is 40-60% below genuine, and the 12-month warranty covers manufacturing defects. Headlight assemblies use branded LED modules (Osram, Lumileds, Samsung) and OEM-matched connectors.

Aftermarket Economy — Produced to nominal dimensions from lower-grade PP or thinner steel. Fit may require adjustment (oversized bolt holes, flexing the panel), and LED modules may come from unbranded suppliers with shorter life. Prices run 60-70% below genuine. Suitable only for markets where the buyer's customer explicitly chooses the cheapest repair and accepts the fit risk. We recommend one test-fit per part number before committing to container quantities.

To verify grade, request the factory's IATF 16949 certificate, the material test report (PP melt-flow index for bumpers, steel gauge and tensile for fenders), and a sample for test-fit. A reliable supplier will offer a sample order at the sample tier before any container commitment — treat any supplier that refuses samples or demands full payment before shipment as a red flag.

Container Loading & Shipping Strategy

Body and lighting parts are bulky, so container planning is the difference between a profitable shipment and a costly one. Bumpers and fenders are load-bearing on their own surfaces: they ship primed and must be separated with foam sheets and bubble wrap so the panels do not scuff each other during transit. Headlights and tail lamps ship in individual cartons with foam corner protectors.

Our standard packing specification:

  • Bumper covers — stacked flat with foam interleaving, 8-10 per crate, crates banded to pallets
  • Fenders — nested pairs with foam separators, 12-16 per crate
  • Headlight / tail lamp assemblies — individual cartons with foam corner protectors, 20-24 per master carton
  • All parts — primed surfaces wrapped in anti-static film; hardware (bolts, brackets) bagged and labeled per part

Shipping options from Guangzhou:

  • Sea freight (LCL): 15-25 days to Mombasa, 18-28 days to Lagos, 12-18 days to Dubai, 10-15 days to Manila, 14-20 days to Bangkok. Minimum order $2,000.
  • Sea freight (FCL 20ft): same transit times at lower per-unit cost. Minimum order $15,000. A 20ft container of mixed body parts typically invoices $14,000-$20,000 FOB.
  • Air freight: 3-7 days worldwide at $5-$9/kg — viable for headlights and tail lamps (small, high value) but not for bumpers and fenders (bulky).
  • Courier (DHL/FedEx): 3-5 days for samples and small orders under 30 kg.

Export documentation: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin (FORM A for GSP-eligible destinations), and IATF 16949 certificate copy. HS codes: bumpers and parts thereof 8708.10.00; lighting equipment 8512.20.00; body stampings 8708.29.00.

FAQ: Body & Lighting Parts Wholesale from China

What is the minimum order quantity for body parts from China?

MOQ is 5 pieces per part number at the wholesale tier for bumpers, fenders, headlights, and tail lamps. Sample orders of 1-4 pieces are accepted at the sample tier price. For a mixed container, we recommend a first order of 150-200 pieces across the seven platform families we stock — 60 bumpers, 50 fenders, 40 headlights, and 40 tail lamps — which covers the most common repair scenarios in African and Middle Eastern markets while keeping initial working capital around $12,000-$15,000 FOB Guangzhou.

Do bumpers and fenders come painted or primed?

All bumpers and fenders ship primed (grey or black E-coat / primer), not painted. Paint is applied locally to match the vehicle's paint code, because color-matching requires the actual vehicle present and varies by market (Saudi beige, UAE white, Nigerian silver are the highest-demand codes). Primed parts are cheaper to ship (no paint logistics) and avoid the risk of paint damage in transit. Headlight and tail lamp assemblies ship with clear UV-coated housings, ready to install.

How do I know which headlight type fits my customer's Toyota or Honda?

Send us the VIN of the target vehicle. We match the VIN against our application database to confirm the connector type, DRL wiring, beam height, and any CAN-bus module requirements. As a rule: pre-2016 models use halogen reflectors; 2016-2021 Corolla, Civic, and Elantra use projector + LED DRL; 2018+ Camry, 2019+ RAV4, and high-trim CR-V use full LED. Full LED assemblies often require the vehicle's lighting module and auto-leveling calibration — installing them on a car originally built with halogen triggers dashboard errors.

What is the difference between genuine, OEM-grade, and aftermarket body parts?

Genuine parts are produced by the OEM or licensed suppliers, cost 2-3x more, and carry the maker's warranty — they are used by dealerships and insurer-mandated repairs. OEM-grade parts are made in IATF 16949-certified Chinese factories to OEM dimensions and material specs, cost 40-60% less, and fit without modification; this is the grade most distributors stock. Aftermarket economy parts cost 60-70% less but may require fit adjustment and use lower-grade materials — acceptable for price-first markets with older vehicles. Always verify grade with the factory certificate, material test report, and a test-fit sample.

Do you offer a warranty on body and lighting parts?

Yes. All parts carry a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects: cracking or warping of bumper covers, poor steel stamping on fenders, LED module failure, or seal failure on headlight assemblies. The warranty excludes paint (parts ship primed) and transit damage. Claims require photos of the defective part, the part number stamped on the panel or housing, and the original commercial invoice. For container orders of 50+ per part number, we offer a pre-shipment inspection with photo and measurement report before loading.

Can I mix bumper, fender, headlight, and tail lamp parts from different brands in one container?

Yes — in fact this is the recommended strategy. A single 20ft container can carry a mix of Toyota, Honda, and Hyundai-Kia body and lighting parts, which lets you serve the whole local fleet with one shipment and spreads freight cost. The example mix of 60 bumpers, 50 fenders, 40 headlights, and 40 tail lamps across seven platforms invoices around $12,000-$15,000 FOB Guangzhou. We produce a packing list and loading plan per SKU so your customs broker and warehouse can verify the shipment on arrival.

Why the BYD Shark 6 Is the First PHEV Pickup Worth Exporting

The 2026 BYD Shark 6 is the first plug-in hybrid (PHEV) pickup truck to enter the export market from China, and it is built on BYD's dedicated DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) platform — the same architecture that underpins the Fang Cheng Bao Leopard 5. For export buyers, the Shark 6 answers the question that has blocked electric pickups in desert and rural markets for years: how do you get EV running costs in a vehicle that still needs to haul, tow, and cross terrain where charging stations do not exist?

BYD answered it with a hybrid system that pairs a 1.5-liter turbocharged petrol engine with two electric motors, delivering a combined 430 hp and 650 Nm of torque. The truck runs up to 100 km on battery alone, then switches to hybrid mode for a combined range of roughly 840 km on a full tank and charge. That is the specification set that Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Nigeria, Kenya and Australia all want — a workhorse that saves fuel on daily commutes and still crosses a desert in one tank.

This guide covers the export versions available from our Nansha, Guangzhou warehouse. The Shark 6 ships with full CCC certification, UN38.3 battery compliance, and MIIT export documentation. FOB pricing starts at USD $31,800 for the 1.5T DMO Premium and $36,500 for the 2.0T Performance, with volume tiers at 5+ and 20+ units. We keep the petrol and DM-i models in the same container plan for importers who want to mix pickups, SUVs and sedans in one shipment.

BYD Shark 6 Full Specifications: DMO Platform Deep Dive

The DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) platform is BYD's dedicated body-on-frame hybrid pickup architecture. Unlike car-platform EVs that were adapted into trucks, DMO was designed from the start for utility: a ladder frame, longitudinal engine layout, double-wishbone front and rear suspension, and an electric drive system integrated into the frame rails. This gives the Shark 6 the durability profile of a traditional pickup with the efficiency of a hybrid.

For most African and Middle Eastern buyers, the 1.5T Premium is the right trade-off between price, fuel economy and capability.

Powertrain Breakdown: 430 hp, 650 Nm & Battery System

The Shark 6's hybrid system combines three power sources through a single AWD drivetrain:

  • 1.5-liter turbocharged engine — a longitudinal four-cylinder producing 143 kW (192 hp), designed for high-efficiency cruise and battery charging on the highway.
  • Front electric motor — 170 kW / 310 Nm, handling launch torque and front-axle drive.
  • Rear electric motor — 150 kW / 340 Nm, driving the rear axle independently, which gives the truck real torque-vectoring off-road.

Combined output is 321 kW (430 hp) and 650 Nm, with the two motors contributing the majority of low-speed torque — this is why the Shark 6 accelerates 0-100 km/h in 5.7 seconds, faster than any diesel pickup in its class. The system uses a CVT-style e-CVT transmission, and the powertrain control unit blends engine and motor output automatically; in Sand and Mud modes the rear motor is biased on to mimic a locked rear differential.

The battery is a 29.58 kWh Blade LFP pack mounted between the frame rails. The Blade Battery's thermal stability is the same chemistry BYD uses across its passenger EV line — cells survive nail penetration tests without thermal runaway — which matters in markets where cabin temperatures exceed 50°C. Charging: 55 kW DC fast charging takes the pack from 30-80% in about 30 minutes; an 7 kW AC wallbox charges 0-100% in roughly 4.5 hours. The truck also carries 6 kW Vehicle-to-Load (V2L), turning the pickup into a mobile generator for tools, camping gear, or a 240V supply for a worksite — a feature African and Middle Eastern contractors value highly.

Real-world fuel economy: in EV mode, daily commutes under 80 km cost near zero fuel; in hybrid mode, expect 7.9-9.0 L/100 km depending on load and terrain — roughly 35-40% less than a comparable diesel Hilux or Ranger on the same route. On a 60 L tank plus a full charge, the claimed 840 km combined range translates to 750-780 km of practical range in mixed use.

The Shark 6's advantages are power, fuel economy, and technology: 430 hp vs 204 hp is a 110% power advantage, and the 7.9 L/100 km hybrid figure undercuts both diesels by 10-20% in daily use. For the Saudi market specifically, BYD priced the Shark 6 at SAR 165,900 (≈ $44,200) — under the Hilux GR and Ranger Wildtrak V6 that dominate the premium end of the segment — while delivering more power and half the daily fuel cost.

The honest positioning for export buyers: the Shark 6 is not a 1-ton commercial workhorse replacement — choose the Hilux/Ranger for that role at the same price point. The Shark 6 is the premium lifestyle-plus-fleet pickup: the fastest and most efficient double cab in the market, aimed at private owners, government fleets, and contractors whose daily driving is under 100 km and whose fuel bill is the main operating cost. FAQ: 2026 BYD Shark 6 Export from China

What is the FOB price of the BYD Shark 6?

The 1.5T DMO Premium is USD $31,800 FOB Nansha at single-unit pricing, dropping to $31,200 at 5+ units and $30,500 at 20+. The 2.0T Performance is $36,500 FOB, $35,900 at 5+, and $35,200 at 20+. Prices include CCC certificate, UN38.3 battery documentation, MIIT files, standard export packing, and pre-shipment inspection.

Is the BYD Shark 6 available for export from China?

Yes. Export units from our Nansha warehouse are factory-fresh Chinese-spec vehicles with full CCC certification and UN38.3 battery compliance. The Shark 6 is also sold through BYD distributors in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Australia, South Africa, Thailand, and Egypt — but those are retail channels. Export pricing from China is lower because it excludes local distributor margin, taxes, and dealer setup. We handle the complete export chain: purchase, MIIT registration, export documents, ocean freight, and delivery to your destination port.

How far can the BYD Shark 6 drive on battery alone?

The 29.58 kWh Blade Battery delivers up to 100 km of EV-only range in mild driving (WLTC-adjacent), and roughly 80-90 km in real mixed city use. Combined range on a full 60 L tank plus a full charge is claimed at 840 km; expect 750-780 km in practical mixed driving. Daily commutes under 80 km can run almost entirely on battery, which is the fuel-saving case that makes the truck popular in Dubai and Riyadh.

How does the BYD Shark 6 compare to the Toyota Hilux and Ford Ranger?

The Shark 6 produces 430 hp and 650 Nm versus 204 hp / 500 Nm for the Hilux 2.8 GD-6 and 210 hp / 500 Nm for the Ranger 2.0 Bi-Turbo — roughly double the power of both diesels. It accelerates 0-100 km/h in 5.7 seconds (vs 10.0 and 9.5 seconds) and uses 7.9 L/100 km (vs 8.5-10 L/100 km). The diesels retain the payload edge (1,000-1,050 kg vs 835 kg) and higher braked towing (3,500 kg vs 2,500 kg). Buyers who haul 1-ton loads daily should pick the Hilux or Ranger; buyers who want the fastest, most efficient double cab should pick the Shark 6.

Can I tow with the BYD Shark 6?

Yes. The 1.5T Premium tows up to 2,500 kg braked (750 kg unbraked); the 2.0T Performance tows up to 3,500 kg braked — the same figure as V6 diesel Hilux and Ranger models. Towing at maximum reduces EV range and increases hybrid fuel consumption to roughly 10-11 L/100 km, so plan routes and charging accordingly. The trailer harness and tow hook are included on export units.

What warranty does the BYD Shark 6 carry for export?

Both trims carry a 5-year / 100,000 km vehicle warranty and an 8-year / 200,000 km battery warranty (whichever comes first), aligned with BYD's global standard. Export buyers should confirm warranty transferability with their destination market's BYD distributor. In markets without an active BYD dealer, Globalucar provides a 12-month exporter warranty covering the hybrid system, battery, and drivetrain defects, with claims processed through our Guangzhou service center.

Why Engine & Transmission Mounts Drive NVH Repair Revenue

Engine mounts and transmission mounts are the lowest-visibility but highest-frequency wear parts on any high-mileage sedan or SUV. While brake pads and filters turn over monthly, mounts turn over quarterly to annually, but every replacement is a higher-ticket job. A taxi-driven Toyota Corolla, Hyundai Elantra or Kia Sportage will typically need two engine mounts and one transmission mount between 80,000 and 140,000 km — and the same vehicle returns every 12-18 months for the next replacement. That is why workshops in Lagos, Mombasa, Dubai, Riyadh and Manila keep a standing inventory of at least one mount per popular platform in the workshop, and wholesalers in those markets move 40-80 mount sets per month for the four platform families covered in this guide.

NVH (Noise, Vibration, Harshness) complaints from mounts are the second most common drivability complaint after engine misfire. Symptoms are distinctive: a vibration felt through the steering wheel at idle that disappears when the clutch is pressed, a clunk on hard acceleration or gear selection, an engine that visibly rocks under throttle, or a vibration that worsens with the AC compressor cycling. These symptoms are often misdiagnosed as engine, transmission or wheel-balance problems, which is why the right OEM-grade or genuine mount matters more than the brand label on the box — a soft mount that flexes too much amplifies vibration; a hard mount transmits shock directly to the chassis.

Kingmay Auto Parts supplies engine and transmission mounts from our Guangzhou warehouse for the four platform families that dominate African, Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian taxi and ride-share fleets: Toyota Corolla (E210/170), Camry (XV70), RAV4 (XA50), Hyundai Elantra (AD/CN7), and Kia Sportage (QL/NQ5). All mounts carry IATF 16949 factory certification, ship boxed with grade markings, and carry a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects.

Mount Types: Solid Rubber, Hydraulic & Electronic Variable

Three mount constructions cover nearly every modern Toyota, Hyundai and Kia application. Choosing the right type is the difference between a smooth idle and a repair that comes back within 30 days.

Type Construction Damping Behavior Typical Application FOB Guangzhou (USD)
Solid Rubber Bonded natural rubber, no fluid High stiffness, abrupt response, transmits vibration Older engines, rear mounts on most platforms $15 – $38
Hydraulic (Filled) Rubber outer with silicone or glycol fluid cavity Tuned damping, low-frequency isolation, fluid absorption Front engine mount on 90% of modern 4-cylinder $28 – $72
Electronic Variable Hydraulic mount with solenoid valve, ECU-controlled Soft at idle, stiff under load via vacuum or electric signal Premium sedans (Camry XV70), some Sportage / Tucson $58 – $135

Hydraulic mounts are the default in modern front-wheel-drive cars because they isolate the engine's idle vibration (typically 700-900 rpm) from the firewall and steering column. The fluid cavity acts as a tuned mass damper: vibration energy is absorbed and dissipated as heat rather than transmitted. Solid rubber mounts are still used at the rear of the engine and on the transmission side because the load direction there is different and hydraulic mounts would allow too much engine movement under torque.

Electronic variable mounts add a solenoid that opens a fluid bypass when the ECU detects hard acceleration, briefly stiffening the mount to control engine lift. The Camry XV70 2.5L and Sportage NQ5 2.5L use this technology. Replacement requires a scan-tool relearn procedure — the ECU must be commanded to cycle the new mount solenoid several times to bleed air from the fluid cavity and confirm the position sensor reads correctly.

NVH Failure Diagnosis: Vibration, Clunk & Engine Lift

The five most common mount-related complaints and how a workshop confirms the diagnosis before ordering parts:

1. Idle vibration through the steering wheel and seat. Press the clutch pedal (manual) or shift to neutral (automatic) and compare the vibration level. If the vibration drops by 50% or more, the front engine mount is the suspect. On Toyota Corolla E210, the front right mount (12305-0T200) carries most of the engine weight and is the first to fail.

2. Clunk on hard acceleration or gear selection. Have an assistant watch the engine from above while the driver accelerates briskly in first gear. If the engine visibly rocks more than 10 mm, the rear transmission mount (12371-0T100 on Corolla, 21850-2B100 on Elantra) has lost its rubber-to-metal bond. The clunk is the engine shifting against a loose mount and hitting the rubber stop.

3. Engine lift on acceleration. Open the hood and observe the engine at idle vs under load. If the engine tilts back under acceleration, the front hydraulic mount has lost fluid pressure. On electronic-variable mounts, a stored DTC (P1450 in Toyota, P0420/P0606 series in Hyundai-Kia) usually accompanies this. The fix is the mount plus a scan-tool relearn.

4. Vibration that worsens with the AC compressor cycling. Turn the AC on and watch the engine mount area. If vibration spikes when the AC clutch engages, the mount is partially failed but the symptom only appears under the additional torque load. Replace the front mount.

5. Vibration that changes with engine temperature. Hydraulic mounts work best when warm. If vibration is worse cold than hot, the mount has lost fluid and is no longer damping — replace. This is the most common cold-start complaint in markets where ambient temperature is high enough that mounts never fully warm up.

Pro Tip: Always replace mounts in pairs on the same axle. A new front mount fitted alongside a worn rear mount shifts the vibration node backward and creates new NVH paths. Workshop labor is roughly the same whether one or two mounts are replaced, so distributors should recommend the pair by default.

Quality Grades: G enuine vs OEM-Grade vs Aftermarket

Engine mounts are available in three quality grades. The differences matter for warranty exposure, NVH performance and customer satisfaction.

Genuine (Toyota Genuine / Hyundai-Kia Mobis) — Produced by the OEM or licensed supplier, sold in OEM packaging with the maker's logo and 12-month factory warranty. Prices run 2-3x the OEM-grade equivalent. Required for vehicles still under factory powertrain warranty, and preferred by dealer networks. For most independent workshops, genuine mounts price the repair out of the market.

OEM-Grade — Produced in IATF 16949-certified Chinese factories on OEM tooling, using OEM-grade natural rubber (60-70 Shore A hardness for solid mounts) and OEM-matched silicone fluid for hydraulic mounts. Hydraulic damping frequency response is within 5% of genuine. This is our recommended grade for distributors serving independent workshops: NVH performance matches genuine, the price is 50-60% below genuine, and the 12-month warranty covers rubber cracking, fluid loss and metal-to-rubber bond failure.

Aftermarket Economy — Produced to fit dimensions only, using lower-durometer rubber and unspecified fluid. NVH performance is typically 15-25% worse than genuine, and the mount may crack within 12 months in hot climates. Prices run 60-70% below genuine. Suitable only for markets where the buyer's customer explicitly chooses the cheapest repair. We recommend a test-fit and idle vibration comparison before committing.

To verify grade, request the factory's IATF 16949 certificate, the rubber compound data sheet (Shore A hardness, tensile strength), and a sample for fit-check and idle-vibration comparison. A reliable supplier will offer a sample order at the sample-tier price before any container commitment — treat any supplier that refuses samples or demands full payment before shipment as a red flag.

Container Loading & Shipping Strategy

Engine and transmission mounts are compact and dense, so they pack efficiently into mixed containers alongside brake pads, filters and other maintenance parts. Each mount ships in an individual carton with foam protection; hydraulic and electronic mounts ship sealed in moisture-barrier film and should be stored in a dry warehouse below 80% humidity.

Our standard packing specification:

FAQ: Engine Mount & Transmission Mount Wholesale from China

How do I know whether to replace the engine mount or transmission mount first?

Replace the engine mount first if the symptom is idle vibration or engine lift; replace the transmission mount first if the symptom is a clunk during gear selection, hard acceleration, or rocking when reversing. Most modern cars need both within the same 12-18 month window because the loads balance across the engine and transmission. We recommend replacing both engine and transmission mounts on the same axle at the same time to balance labor cost and avoid creating new NVH paths.

What is the difference between a hydraulic and an electronic variable engine mount?

A hydraulic mount uses a sealed fluid cavity to absorb vibration energy — the fluid moves and dissipates energy as heat. An electronic variable mount adds a solenoid valve that opens or closes a fluid bypass based on engine load, controlled by the ECU. At idle the valve is open and the mount is soft; under hard acceleration the valve closes and the mount stiffens to control engine lift. Electronic variable mounts require a scan-tool relearn procedure after installation. Replacement of a hydraulic or electronic variable mount must be done with the vehicle on a level surface and the engine cool to allow accurate positioning.

What is the minimum order quantity for engine mounts from China?

MOQ is 10 pieces per part number at the wholesale tier for solid mounts and 5 pieces at the wholesale tier for hydraulic and electronic mounts (because of the higher unit cost). Sample orders of 1-4 pieces are accepted at the sample tier price. For a mixed container, we recommend a first order of 250-300 pieces across the seven platform families we stock — 100 solid rubber rear mounts, 120 hydraulic front mounts, 30 electronic variable mounts, and 30 sub-frame bushing pairs — covering the most common NVH repair scenarios across Toyota and Hyundai-Kia fleets in African, Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian markets while keeping initial working capital around $8,000-$11,000 FOB Guangzhou.

How long do OEM-grade engine mounts last?

OEM-grade engine mounts typically last 80,000-120,000 km under normal driving conditions. In taxi and ride-share fleets where the engine idles 50-60% of operational time and the vehicle runs 60,000-80,000 km annually, mount life drops to 50,000-80,000 km. Hydraulic mounts suffer additionally from fluid loss in hot climates where cabin and engine-bay temperatures exceed 60°C; OEM-grade hydraulic mounts in Saudi Arabia and the UAE typically last 60,000-90,000 km versus 100,000-140,000 km in temperate climates. Solid rubber mounts tolerate heat better and last 80,000-130,000 km across all markets.

Do you offer a warranty on engine and transmission mounts?

Yes. All mounts carry a 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects — rubber cracking, fluid loss in hydraulic mounts, solenoid failure in electronic mounts, and metal-to-rubber bond failure. The warranty excludes damage from incorrect installation, over-torqued bolts, or vehicles involved in a collision. Claims require photos of the defective mount, the OE reference stamped on the rubber or metal body, and the original commercial invoice. For container orders of 50+ pieces per part number, we offer a pre-shipment batch test report covering Shore A hardness, tensile strength and static load-deflection.

Can I mix engine mounts, transmission mounts and sub-frame bushings from different platforms in one container?

Yes — this is the recommended strategy. A single 20ft container can carry Toyota, Hyundai and Kia mounts together, which lets you serve the full local fleet with one shipment and spreads freight cost. The example mix of 100 solid rubber rear mounts, 120 hydraulic front mounts, 30 electronic variable mounts, and 30 sub-frame bushing pairs across seven platforms invoices around $9,500-$12,500 FOB Guangzhou. We produce a packing list and loading plan per SKU so your customs broker and warehouse can verify the shipment on arrival.

Why the RAV4 Is the World’s Most Exported Hybrid SUV

The Toyota RAV4 has been the best-selling SUV on the planet for most of the past decade, and in 2026 it is also the most requested Toyota model in our Guangzhou export pipeline after the Land Cruiser Prado. The reason is simple arithmetic for importers: a compact SUV with Toyota's fifth-generation hybrid system, a 514-liter boot, 8 airbags and the TSS 3.0 safety suite carries a resale premium in every market from Dubai to Nairobi to Almaty that no Chinese-brand crossover at the same FOB price can match yet.

Three things changed in 2026 that make the RAV4 more interesting for exporters than it has been in years. First, FAW Toyota launched the sixth-generation Rongfang (the Chinese-market RAV4) in August 2026 with an all-hybrid lineup — there is no longer a petrol-only version to confuse buyers with. Second, the entry 2.0L Dual Engine Elite opened at a promotional RMB 136,200 (about $19,100), the first time a hybrid RAV4 has been priced below the equivalent petrol model in China. Third, a wave of 2024-2026 certified-used and near-new units is now flowing into the export channel at $23,000-$31,000 FOB — the sweet spot for African and Central Asian importers who want Toyota reliability without new-car capital outlay.

Globalucar currently holds two RAV4 units in Nansha-ready condition — a 2024 2.0L CVT 2WD Fashion Plus at $23,250 FOB and a 2026 2.0L AWD Luxury with 100 km on the clock at $31,449 FOB — and sources new sixth-generation hybrid units directly from FAW Toyota dealer stock for volume orders. This guide covers the sixth-generation specs, in-stock pricing, five-market landed cost math, and the compliance details that decide whether an RAV4 export clears customs without surprises.

Sixth-Generation RAV4: What Changed in August 2026

The sixth-generation RAV4 keeps the TNGA-K platform and the squared-off silhouette of its predecessor, but nearly everything under the skin moved forward. The headline changes for export buyers:

  • All-hybrid lineup. Every 2026 Rongfang trim carries the Dual Engine (THS) hybrid system. The 2.0L petrol and 2.5L petrol engines of the fifth generation are gone from the Chinese lineup, which simplifies both buyer education and parts stocking.
  • New lithium battery. The hybrid battery switched from nickel-metal hydride to a ternary lithium pack that is roughly half the size, mounted under the rear seat. Boot capacity holds at 514 liters, expanding to about 1,700 liters with the rear seats folded, and the rear floor stays flat.
  • More electric power. Motor output increased 32% and power-electronics losses dropped 19%, helped by silicon-carbide switches in the inverter. Combined system output for the 2.5L version reaches 163 kW in E-Four form.
  • TSS 3.0 on every trim — full-speed adaptive cruise, lane centering, pre-collision braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection — plus 8 airbags including a front-center airbag, and A/B pillars in 1,470 MPa high-strength steel.
  • Smarter cabin. A Qualcomm-chip infotainment head unit with multi-dialect voice control, phone mirroring and remote vehicle status replaces the criticized fifth-gen system.

The wheelbase and footprint are unchanged from the fifth generation (4,620 × 1,855 × 1,680 mm, 2,690 mm wheelbase), which means shipping costs, container plans and lift-gate dimensions that exporters calculated for fifth-gen units carry over unchanged.

Full Specifications: 2.0L & 2.5L Dual Engine Lineup

The Chinese-market sixth-generation RAV4 offers two hybrid outputs. Both use an Atkinson-cycle Dynamic Force four-cylinder, an e-CVT planetary transmission, and a lithium-ion pack under the rear seat.

For fleet buyers the 2.0L Elite is the volume play: it undercuts the 2.5L on price by roughly $8,000 at FOB and its measured consumption — 3.14 L/100 km in the China Automotive Center full-course test — is the lowest of any RAV4 ever built. The 2.5L AWD is the premium play for markets with gravel roads, mountain terrain or dust-season visibility demands, and its ~8-second 0-100 km/h time puts it ahead of most 2.0T competitors in the class.

Powertrain Deep Dive: Fifth-Gen THS, E-Four & Real-World Fuel Economy

The fifth-generation Toyota Hybrid System in the sixth-gen RAV4 is the same architecture that has earned Toyota more than 34 million hybrid owners worldwide, with three engineering upgrades that matter for hot-climate markets.

First, the switch to a ternary lithium battery halves pack volume and improves charge acceptance, which matters in stop-start traffic in Lagos or Jeddah where the system cycles constantly. Second, silicon-carbide switching devices in the power control unit cut inverter losses 19%, reducing heat load in engine bays that already face 50°C+ ambient temperatures. Third, the E-Four system drives the rear wheels with an independent motor instead of a driveshaft — no transfer case to service, no rear driveshaft to fail on rough roads, and a flat rear floor because nothing runs under it.

A Nairobi fleet running 30,000 km per year saves roughly $830-960 per vehicle per year versus the petrol fifth-gen — enough to recover the hybrid price gap within two to three years while holding stronger resale value.

Kenya is the priciest landing — the 25% duty, IDF, RDL and 16% VAT stack to nearly $18,000 on a $30,500 CIF value — but Kenyan buyers offset it with the strongest hybrid resale premium in East Africa, and the 2.0L HEV Elite at $19,500 FOB lands closer to $32,000, within reach of the CR-V petrol buyer it converts from.

The Tucson wins on outright FOB price and is the right answer for pure budget buyers — see our Tucson vs Tiggo 8 comparison for that case. The CR-V matches the RAV4 on space and badge strength but burns 45% more fuel and carries a mechanical AWD system with more service points. The RAV4 Hybrid's advantage is total cost of ownership over a 3-4 year hold: the fuel saving alone is $700-1,000 per year at 30,000 km, and hybrid RAV4s consistently top independent resale tables in the Gulf and East Africa, which is what fleet buyers actually monetize.

Target Markets, Compliance & the 180-Day Rule

UAE and Saudi Arabia. Both register the China-built RAV4 without restriction — the model is type-approved regionally and the FAW Toyota build carries the same 2.5L hybrid system as the Japan-built version. GCC-spec items to confirm at order: Arabic-language infotainment where required, and Gulf-region warranty registration through the destination distributor if the buyer wants local service coverage. Import duty is 5% in both markets; Saudi adds 15% VAT.

Nigeria and Kenya. Kenya requires imported used vehicles to be under 8 years old from first registration — both our 2024 and 2026 stock units qualify with room to spare — and right-hand drive. Nigeria accepts left-hand drive; the 2024 2.0L 2WD unit at $23,250 is our most-ordered RAV4 for Lagos because its landed cost near $36,000 fits the popular mid-SUV retail band.

Central Asia. Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan import China-built Toyotas at scale through Khorgos and Alashankou. The China-assembled RAV4 enjoys strong acceptance because the region's existing Corolla and Camry fleets already run Chinese-built Toyota parts. Confirm current EAC duty (15% for new vehicles) and the recycling-fee bracket with your broker; rail freight from Guangzhou to Almaty runs 12-18 days.

The 180-day rule. China's 2026 tightening of the zero-kilometer export policy requires a vehicle to be registered for at least 180 days before it can be exported as a used car, or it must move through the licensed new-car export channel. All Globalucar used and certified-used RAV4 units already satisfy the registration requirement — the 2026 AWD Luxury unit, registered February 2026, cleared the window in August. New sixth-generation units ship under our new-car export license with full CCC and customs documentation. Buyers sourcing from other channels should verify the registration date on the de-registration certificate before paying, because a violation strands the vehicle at Chinese customs.

FAQ: Toyota RAV4 Export from China

Can I export a brand-new RAV4 from China, or only used units?

Both channels are open. New sixth-generation units ship under Globalucar's licensed new-car export channel with 3-5 week allocation from FAW Toyota dealer stock — the 2.0L HEV Elite from $19,500 FOB at volume and the 2.5L HEV AWD Luxury from $27,200 at 20+ units. Used and certified-used units (currently $23,250 and $31,449) ship within 7-10 days because they are already de-registered and export-ready. The practical difference is capital and time, not legality — but the 180-day rule applies to the used-car channel, so every unit's registration date is verified before contracting.

How does the China-built RAV4 differ from the Japan-built version?

The powertrain is the same fifth-generation THS hybrid system with the same 2.5L Dynamic Force engine and e-CVT. Differences are in trim naming, infotainment localization (the Chinese head unit runs a Qualcomm chip with Mandarin-first voice control, which most export buyers have reflashed or replaced with CarPlay/Android Auto mirroring), and some market-specific equipment such as the panoramic monitor on top trims. Structurally and mechanically, parts catalogs are shared, so destination-market Toyota dealers service them with standard RAV4 parts.

What is the 180-day rule and does it affect RAV4 exports?

Yes — it is the single most important compliance point for used-vehicle exports from China in 2026. A vehicle must hold a Chinese registration for at least 180 days before it can be exported under the used-car channel; zero-kilometer "used" cars that never registered can no longer slip through. Both RAV4 units in our stock meet the requirement, and we provide the de-registration certificate showing the first registration date with every file. New-car exports bypass the rule entirely but require the licensed new-car export channel and full documentation.

Which markets accept China-built Toyota hybrids?

The GCC (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar), Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and East Africa, Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan), Russia and the Caucasus, and Southeast Asia all register China-built Toyotas routinely — the region already runs millions of Chinese-assembled Corollas, Camrys and RAV4s. Markets with local Toyota assembly plants (some ASEAN states, South Africa) protect domestic production with higher duties, so landed-cost math decides those cases individually.

How much does shipping cost and how long does it take?

RORO from Nansha to Jebel Ali or Dammam runs $1,400-1,600 and 18-24 days; to Lagos $1,600-1,800 and 28-35 days; to Mombasa $1,500-1,700 and 24-30 days. Container shipping adds $300-500 per unit but protects the vehicle and allows mixed loads — a 40ft high-cube container carries three RAV4s with wheels chocked and battery isolated. Rail to Khorgos/Almaty runs $1,800-2,000 per unit and 12-18 days door-to-port. All figures include marine insurance at 0.3% of value.

What warranty applies to exported RAV4 units?

New units carry Toyota China's 3-year / 100,000 km vehicle warranty and the hybrid battery's 8-year coverage; transferability to the destination market depends on whether a local distributor accepts China-market vehicles, which most GCC and Central Asian distributors do. For used and certified-used units, Globalucar provides a 12-month exporter warranty covering the hybrid system, transmission and major driveline components, with claims handled through our Guangzhou service desk and parts shipped from our Toyota parts inventory — the same catalog that stocks engine and transmission mounts for the Corolla, Camry and RAV4 platform family.

Why Shock Absorbers & Strut Mounts Are High-Margin Repeat Stock

Every vehicle with independent front suspension needs two things after the 60,000 km mark: shock absorbers to dampen wheel movement and strut mounts to keep the coil-over assembly attached to the body. Together they form the most predictable repeat-revenue category in a wholesale auto-parts catalog because wear is invisible until it is dangerous, and because a single front-strut job on a common sedan sells shock + mount + bearing + boot + spring-seat kit as a bundle.

For distributors in Africa, the Middle East, Latin America and Southeast Asia, the economics are attractive. A front shock absorber for a Toyota Corolla or Hyundai Elantra lands in-country at $18-35 retail after a $8.50-20.00 FOB purchase, and a complete strut-mount-and-bearing kit bought at $10-22 FOB retails at $35-70. Because demand is tied to vehicle age rather than economic cycles, a well-stocked shock-and-suspension line smooths cash flow when new-car accessory sales dip.

Kingmay's Guangzhou inventory covers the three volume segments importers ask for most: Toyota Corolla / Camry / RAV4, Nissan Sentra / Sylphy / X-Trail, and Hyundai Elantra / Tucson / Sonata / Kia Sportage / Cerato / K5. All units are packaged for sea containers, labeled with OE-grade references, and available in MOQs from 50 pieces up to full mixed-container loads.

Twin-Tube vs Mono-Tube Shock Absorbers: Which Suits Your Market?

Not every replacement shock is the same. Twin-tube remains the dominant design for mass-market passenger cars because it is cost-effective, durable on broken asphalt and forgiving of minor oil contamination. Mono-tube shocks are the choice for SUVs, performance trims and markets with a high share of gravel or desert driving because they resist fade better and react faster to high-frequency inputs.

Most Kingmay volume is twin-tube gas-charged for the Toyota, Nissan and Hyundai Kia passenger-car programs. Mono-tube units are available for Tucson, Sportage, RAV4 and X-Trail rear applications where longer travel and fade resistance matter. If you are buying for a fleet that covers mixed city and gravel routes, a 70/30 twin-tube/mono-tube split is usually the right container plan.

Failure Diagnosis: When to Replace Shocks & Strut Mounts

The most common mistake in suspension wholesale is selling only the shock absorber when the mount is also worn. A clunk over speed bumps usually means the strut mount bearing has lost its preload, not that the shock is dead. The table below links symptoms to the part that actually fixes them.

Training repair-shop customers to sell mounts with shocks increases average order value by 30-50% and reduces comebacks. A strut mount that fails six months after a shock replacement turns a happy customer into a warranty claim; replacing both at the same service is standard practice in mature markets and should be promoted the same way in emerging ones.

Quality Grades: OEM, OES, Aftermarket & Reman

Kingmay supplies three quality grades for suspension parts. The right grade depends on who your customer sells to.

  • OEM-grade / OES (Original Equipment Supplier): Made by the same tier of factories that supply global brand dealerships. Matching surface finish, valving curves and bushing compounds.   • Aftermarket performance: New units built to ISO/TS 16949 processes with gas-charged twin-tube or mono-tube construction. Slight cosmetic tolerance differences from OE but full functional spec. This is the volume grade for independent repair shops and parts retailers.

FAQ: Shock Absorber & Strut Mount Sourcing from China

How do I know if a shock absorber is twin-tube or mono-tube?

Twin-tube shocks have a wider body relative to the rod and the oil/gas is separated by a floating piston inside a single tube. Physically, most twin-tube units have a visible dust shield and the body diameter is similar from top to bottom. Mono-tube units usually have a slimmer body, a larger piston rod and often an external gas reservoir or remote canister on performance models. If in doubt, request the cross-section drawing or the manufacturer's specification sheet before ordering.

Should I replace strut mounts when replacing shocks?

Yes, if the vehicle has more than 80,000 km or the mounts are more than five years old. Strut mounts carry the full weight of the front corner through a rubber insulator and a thrust bearing. A worn mount causes a clunk over bumps, steering shimmy and premature shock failure because the shock is no longer aligned with the body. Replacing mounts with shocks is standard good practice and the bundle is easier to sell to repair shops.

What is the difference between a shock absorber and a strut?

A shock absorber is a standalone damping unit that bolts to the suspension and body. A strut is a structural part of the suspension: it combines the shock absorber, coil spring and upper mount into one assembly and replaces the upper control arm on many front-wheel-drive cars. When someone asks for a "strut," they usually mean the complete coil-over assembly or at least the strut mount and bearing that sit at the top of it.

Are Chinese aftermarket shocks reliable for hot climates?

Reliable if sourced from a factory with proper oil and seal specifications. The key failure points in hot climates are oil foaming at high temperatures and seal hardening from ozone and UV exposure. Kingmate specifies gas-charged twin-tube units with oil rated to -40°C / +150°C and EPDM or Viton-class seals for markets above 40°C ambient. Ask for the temperature certificate if your destination is the Gulf, North Africa or inland West Africa.

Can I mix Toyota, Nissan and Hyundai Kia parts in one container?

Yes. Mixed-container loading is normal for distributors. We recommend grouping by carton size to maximize cube utilization: shocks and strut mounts in one block, control arms and tie rods in another, and small hardware in side-fill cartons. A typical 40ft HC load for a multi-brand suspension distributor is 40% shocks, 25% mounts/bearings, 20% control arms/ball joints/tie rods and 15% sway-bar links and bushings.

What documents come with a wholesale order?

Each shipment includes a commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and a pre-shipment inspection report with photos of packed cartons. For container orders we also provide the container loading plan and gross/net weight summary. If your customs broker needs a specific declaration (HS 8708.80 for suspension parts, for example), tell us before loading and we will label the cartons and invoice lines accordingly.

Why Russian and Central Asian Importers Buy the Tiggo 8 Series

The Chery Tiggo 8 has become the most requested Chinese SUV in the Russia-bound export trade, and the numbers behind that position are easy to check. Chery has held the top spot among Chinese brands in the Russian market since 2023, with the Tiggo 7 Pro and Tiggo 8 Pro Max regulars in the country's ten best-selling SUV charts (AEB registration data, 2026). For a wholesaler in Moscow, Yekaterinburg or Almaty, the Tiggo 8 Pro packages a 7-seat family SUV with a 1.6T turbo engine, a 2,710 mm wheelbase and a parts network Chery has spent five years building across the Eurasian Economic Union.

The arbitrage that drives the Chery Tiggo 8 export business is the retail-to-cost spread. Russian dealers list the Tiggo 8 Pro and Pro Max at roughly 2.3 to 2.8 million rubles — about $31,500 to $38,400 at the 2026 exchange rate near 73 RUB/USD. The same vehicle leaves Nansha Port at less than half of that figure, which is why licensed exporters, parallel-import dealers and fleet buyers all compete for allocation of this one model line.

In Central Asia the story is the same with a different calendar. Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan share Russia's EAC certification framework as EAEU members, Uzbekistan has been cutting import duties on passenger vehicles since 2023, and Chery's contract assembly in Karaganda plus dealer networks in Almaty, Astana and Tashkent have normalized parts supply. A Tiggo 9 bought at FOB Nansha and cleared in Almaty or Tashkent competes directly with Russian-market retail — at a shorter shipping leg.

Tiggo 8 Pro vs Tiggo 9: Full Specification Comparison

The two vehicles serve two different missions. The Tiggo 8 Pro is the volume product: a mid-size 7-seat SUV with the 1.6T SQRF4J16 engine, built for families and ride-hailing fleets, tuned to run on 92 RON fuel and priced for markets where $15,000-class FOB still buys real equipment. The Tiggo 9 is the flagship: Chery's 2.0T Kunpeng engine with 254 hp, an 8-speed automatic on export trims, and the chassis dimensions that let it sell against the Haval H9 and Hyundai Santa Fe at retail. The table below sets out the numbers buyers actually ask about before they ask about price.

Two specification details matter more for this trade lane than the headline power figures. First, both engines are calibrated for 92 RON fuel, which matches what is actually sold across Siberia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan — a real cost-of-ownership argument your retail customers will understand. Second, the 1.6T's 7.1 L/100 km WLTC figure holds up in city use at -25°C with block heaters fitted, a data point Moscow and Novosibirsk dealers now ask for on every Chinese SUV quotation.

Three notes on how these Tiggo 8 Pro FOB price points behave in practice. Dealer-stock allocation runs two to four weeks from deposit, because Chery prioritizes domestic retail and Russian official-channel shipments before independent export orders. Container economics matter at this price class: a 40-foot high-cube takes three Tiggo 8 Pro units on their wheels, or four with a steel loading rack, so freight per vehicle drops roughly $500 when you fill the box. And under China's tightened 180-day rule for near-new vehicles, new units ship only through the licensed new-car export channel — Globalucar holds that license, so the units we quote carry proper new-car documentation from day one.

Russia Import Cost: Duty, VAT and the Utilization Fee

This is the section where budgets slip, because the tax stack on a vehicle entering Russia in 2026 involves four separate charges plus service fees. The worked example below follows a Tiggo 8 Pro 1.6T Luxury arriving at Vladivostok with a CIF value of $15,600 (FOB $13,700 plus roughly $1,900 RoRo freight). The figures come from a broker-cleared 2026 Vladivostok clearing schedule, and they match what independent importing guides are publishing for this engine class this year.

Read against the FOB table above, that stack puts the cleared cost of this Tiggo 8 Pro at roughly $31,800 to $35,200 on the ground in Vladivostok — squarely inside the Russian retail band of $31,500 to $38,400. The margin on the 1.6T FWD car is therefore thin and lives or dies on the utilization-fee coefficient, which changes by federal decree. Professional importers concentrate their volume on the Tiggo 8 Pro Max 2.0T and Tiggo 9 trims instead, where the retail-to-cost gap widens enough to pay for freight, clearance and a dealer margin. Confirm the current coefficients with your Moscow or Vladivostok broker before contracting — we provide the invoice-side numbers, your broker provides the local-side numbers, and the two must be checked together.

On the compliance side, a type-approved model like the Tiggo 8 Pro clears through a documentary EAC declaration rather than full physical testing. Your clearing broker prepares the SBKTS (certificate of vehicle safety construction) and the EPTS (electronic passport) from the export documents we issue. Two localization items surface after clearance: the Chinese-spec infotainment unit needs a region flash for full Russian language at $280–420 in Moscow, and a unit landing on worn 235/55R19 tires adds $95–140 per tire to make it showroom-ready. Both are line items worth booking before the deposit, not after.

Port Choice: Vladivostok, Novorossiysk and the Rail Alternative

Vladivostok handles about three quarters of all China-built SUV imports, and for good reason: RoRo freight from Shanghai or Ningbo runs $1,800–2,400 per vehicle with a 5–8 day transit and three to four sailings per week through 2026. Customs release for a documented Tiggo 8 Pro takes four to eight working days. From there, TransSib rail to Moscow covers the remaining 9,000-plus kilometers in 8–14 days, or trucking does it in 14–21. For Far East, Siberian and Ural buyers, the port is effectively local.

Novorossiysk serves European Russia, Krasnodar, Rostov and the Caucasus with a shorter final leg. The ocean route via the Suez Canal costs $3,800–5,200 per vehicle and takes 28–35 days at one to two sailings per week, with customs release in five to ten days. Choose it when your buyer sits west of the Volga and can wait a month; otherwise the Vladivostok-plus-rail combination usually beats it on total landed time.

Quick answer on routing: Far East, Siberia, Urals → Vladivostok RoRo (5–8 days at sea + rail/truck onward). European Russia → Novorossiysk via Suez (28–35 days) only if your buyer can wait; otherwise Vladivostok + TransSib rail lands a Tiggo 8 in Moscow in under three weeks door to door.

Central Asia: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan

Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, as EAEU members, apply the same EAC framework and the union's common customs tariff — the duty and utilization-fee logic from the Russia section carries over, administered by local brokers in Almaty, Astana and Bishkek. What changes is the routing: instead of an ocean leg, units move by rail from Guangzhou through the Khorgos/Alashankou land border, roughly 6,000 kilometers in 18–25 days, then clear for the Kazakh market. We covered this corridor in detail in our Toyota Corolla Cross FOB Khorgos guide, and the same math applies to a Tiggo 8 Pro at its lower FOB price.

Uzbekistan sits outside the EAEU but has cut passenger-vehicle import duties in stages since 2023, and Tashkent dealers actively source Chinese SUVs through both direct clearance and Kazakh transit. Kyrgyzstan's historical role as a low-duty re-export hub has narrowed as EAEU enforcement tightened after 2023 — plan to clear in the country of final sale with a local broker rather than routing through Bishkek for paperwork reasons. On warranty: Chery's official Russian network markets a 7-year/200,000 km new-car warranty, but that coverage attaches to officially imported units; export-channel vehicles are supported by Chery's growing parts distribution instead, which is why we include the parts-supplier introduction with every fleet order.

Pre-Shipment Checks That Protect Your Margin

Every one of the post-clearance costs listed earlier can be predicted before the vessel sails. These are the six checks we run on every Tiggo 8 order:

  1. VIN and export chassis verification — the plate, MIIT type approval and invoice must match the licensed export channel exactly.
  2. Service book and stamps — a complete Chery service book protects $1,200–1,800 of resale value in Russia; gaps get documented before shipping.
  3. Tire condition — tread photos on all four 235/55R19 (or 235/45R20) positions plus the spare, so the buyer budgets $0 or $600, never a surprise.
  4. A/C full-load test — 15 minutes at maximum, verifying 5–8°C outlet temperature and no compressor cycling shudder, since an overhaul runs $380–620 in Moscow.
  5. Multimedia region-flash decision — confirmed with the buyer pre-deposit so the $280–420 Moscow flash is either booked or skipped knowingly.
  6. Inspection report with photos — 40+ images covering interior, chassis numbers and any transport marks, issued before the balance payment.

How to Order a Tiggo 8 from Globalucar

Single-unit trial orders are accepted — many Tiggo 8 relationships start with one 40-foot container — and we support mixed loading with other models when you are filling a box. Every quote comes with the FOB price, freight options for Vladivostok, Novorossiysk or Khorgos, and the document set your broker needs for SBKTS and EPTS preparation.
