content:
Quick Answer: The 140th Canton Fair runs October 15 – November 4, 2026 at the Pazhou complex in Guangzhou, and auto parts sit in Phase 1 (October 15–19), alongside vehicles, new-energy vehicles, motorcycles and bicycles. Doors open 9:30–18:00 daily; the last session drew roughly 314,000 overseas buyers from 220 countries and regions. This guide covers the phase schedule, buyer registration, a day-by-day sourcing plan for auto parts, hall logistics at Pazhou, and how to combine the fair with year-round sourcing from Guangzhou.

Every October, the centre of gravity of the world's physical goods trade moves to a bend in the Pearl River. The Canton Fair — the China Import and Export Fair, running since 1957 — is still the largest procurement event on earth by floor area, and for auto parts buyers it is the one week of the year when thousands of Chinese parts manufacturers, export desks and trading houses are standing in the same halls, with samples on the table and decision-makers on the booths.

This guide is written for parts distributors, workshop-chain buyers and fleet procurement teams planning to source auto parts at the autumn 2026 session. It covers the facts that determine your travel dates, the registration process, how the vehicle-and-parts halls are organised, a realistic five-day sourcing plan, the questions that separate real suppliers from booth decorators, and how a Guangzhou-based sourcing partner fits into the picture. We publish application-specific sourcing guides alongside this one — for example, our Toyota brake pads and rotors wholesale guide — so you arrive with an application list rather than a blank notebook.

Why Phase 1 Matters for Auto Parts Buyers

The Canton Fair splits its roughly 1.55 million square metres into three five-day phases, and product categories do not repeat between them. Auto parts, vehicles, new-energy vehicles and smart mobility, motorcycles and bicycles all sit in Phase 1 — which makes the third week of October the highest-density five days of the year for vehicle-sector sourcing in China. Electronics, machinery, hardware and tools share the same phase, which matters if your program extends to workshop equipment, diagnostics tools or hardware alongside the parts themselves.

The draw is not just exhibitor count. It is comparison density: for a fast-moving category like brake components, filters or suspension parts, you can walk a dozen candidate factories in a single morning, collect samples in the afternoon, and have price and capability spreadsheets that would take three separate sourcing trips to build any other week. Buyers who arrive with a structured plan routinely compress a quarter of supplier-development work into five days.

The scale numbers explain the effort. The most recent spring session drew roughly 314,000 overseas buyers from 220 countries and regions, and the vehicle-and-parts category consistently ranks among the most internationally attended sections of Phase 1. Hotels near the Pazhou complex sell out for these dates months ahead — which is the first practical reason to start planning early.

Canton Fair 2026 Dates: The Full Phase Schedule

The autumn 2026 session of the fair (the 140th) runs from October 15 to November 4 across three phases, with three-day changeover breaks between them. For auto parts buyers, the entire trip revolves around Phase 1; the table below shows how the phases map to product categories and what each means for a vehicle-sector visitor.

PhaseDates (2026)Product CategoriesRelevance for Auto Parts Buyers
Phase 1Oct 15–19Auto parts, vehicles, NEV & smart mobility, motorcycles, bicycles, electronics, machinery, hardware, tools, lighting, new energyCore phase — plan your trip around these five days
ChangeoverOct 20–22Halls closed for booth changeoverWindow for factory visits in the Pearl River Delta and Guangzhou supplier meetings
Phase 2Oct 23–27Home goods, gifts, decorations, furniture, building materialsNot relevant for parts; some buyers use it for packaging suppliers
ChangeoverOct 28–30Halls closedSecond window for factory visits and follow-up meetings
Phase 3Oct 31 – Nov 4Textiles, shoes, toys, office supplies, health, foodNot relevant for auto parts

Daily opening hours are 9:30 to 18:00. A practical rhythm for Phase 1: halls are fullest and energy highest on days one and two; by day four, booth staff have time for longer technical conversations, which is when the serious negotiation happens. Plan your must-meet list for days one to three and keep days four and five for second visits and deeper discussions with shortlisted suppliers.

Where Auto Parts Sit Inside the Pazhou Complex

The fair occupies the China Import and Export Fair Complex at 382 Yuejiang Middle Road, Haizhu District — the Pazhou complex, four linked exhibition districts (A, B, C and D) stretched along the riverfront. Vehicle and parts exhibits concentrate in specific halls within these districts, with the exact hall allocation published in the official floor plan in the weeks before opening; the official Canton Fair website and app carry the hall map, exhibitor search and booth-level navigation. Two consequences follow from the physical layout.

First, the complex is genuinely vast — the walking distance between opposite ends is measured in kilometres, not metres. Buyers who try to "browse everything" exhaust themselves by midday of day one. The winning approach is to shortlist exhibitors through the official exhibitor search before arrival, mark booths on the app's floor plan, and route each day around one or two hall clusters.

Second, because vehicles, parts, new-energy mobility and motorcycles are co-located in the same phase, adjacent halls frequently hold the complete supply chain for one product family — for example, brake component factories, friction-material specialists and testing-equipment suppliers within walking distance of each other. Ask each good booth one extra question: "who else in this hall should I meet for this product family?" — the answer is often the most valuable intelligence of the day.

Buyer Registration: Badge, Invitation Letter and Visa

Overseas buyers enter the fair with a buyer badge (a QR-code card issued after registration). The process is fully online through the official Buyer Service System, and pre-registering is strongly recommended — it speeds up badge collection and keeps you out of the on-site queue on opening morning. The practical steps:

  • Create a buyer account on the official Canton Fair Buyer E-service Tool with your company details and business credentials.
  • Apply for the buyer badge and wait for verification; returning buyers can often reuse their existing badge or re-register in minutes.
  • Arrange your China entry documents: check visa requirements for your nationality, or use an invitation letter from a Chinese supplier or trade partner where that simplifies the application. China's visa-free transit and entry policies have expanded considerably — verify the current policy for your passport before booking, as rules continue to evolve.
  • Collect the badge at a designated collection point in Guangzhou (including at the complex), carrying the original identity document you registered with.

Buyer registration itself is handled through the official system at no charge for verified overseas buyers; be wary of any third-party site charging for "Canton Fair registration" — the official channel is the only one that matters. Once registered, the same account gives you access to the year-round online Canton Fair platform, which mirrors the offline exhibitor catalogue — useful both before the fair (shortlisting) and after it (follow-up).

A Five-Day Sourcing Plan for Auto Parts Buyers

Five days is enough to build a serious supplier shortlist — if each day has a job. The plan below reflects how experienced parts buyers structure Phase 1; adjust the weighting to your category mix.

DayFocusWhat You Should Walk Out With
Day 1 (Oct 15)Orientation + top-priority boothsPre-shortlisted 8–12 booths visited; samples requested; first price indications
Day 2 (Oct 16)Systematic category sweepCoverage of your core categories (brakes, filters, suspension, electrical); comparison sheet started
Day 3 (Oct 17)Second visits + technical deep divesCertification documents (IATF 16949, ECE R90 where applicable); MOQ and pricing tiers discussed
Day 4 (Oct 18)Negotiation dayShortlist of 5–8 real candidates; sample orders agreed; payment and QC terms outlined
Day 5 (Oct 19)Closing + Guangzhou meetingsConfirmed follow-up actions; meetings booked with Guangzhou-based export partners for the changeover days

One discipline separates professional buyers from tourists: record every conversation the same day. Photograph business cards against booth numbers, note prices and claims in one spreadsheet each evening, and mark each contact A/B/C by priority. By day four you will have spoken to more suppliers than memory can hold — the spreadsheet is the asset you fly home with.

The Ten Questions to Ask at Every Booth

Booth displays are marketing; your questions are due diligence. Ten questions that consistently surface the truth about a parts supplier:

  • Are you the manufacturer or a trading company — and can I visit the factory this week or next?
  • Which certifications do you hold, and can you show the certificate numbers (IATF 16949, ECE R90 for brake parts, EMARK for lighting)?
  • What is your main export market, and what share is aftermarket versus OE channel?
  • Which OE references does this product cover, and do you supply the cross-reference list?
  • What are your MOQ per reference and your price tiers by volume?
  • What is the production lead time for a first order, and for a repeat order?
  • How is the product packed for ocean freight, and can I see the export carton?
  • Do you accept third-party pre-shipment inspection, and which agencies have visited you?
  • What are your payment terms for a first order?
  • Who in your team handles English communication after the fair — can I meet them now?

The answers you want to avoid are as informative as the ones you want to hear: vague certification answers, "our factory is far away, no visits", or no named post-fair contact person are each reliable disqualifiers. Suppliers who pass these ten questions on the booth can usually survive a real audit; suppliers who flinch on two or more rarely improve after you wire a deposit.

Getting to Pazhou: Flights, Metro and Hotels

Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport connects to the fair complex by metro (roughly 60–75 minutes with one transfer) or by taxi (45–90 minutes depending on traffic). Guangzhou South railway station — the high-speed rail hub for the Pearl River Delta, including the 30-minute connection from Shenzhen and Hong Kong links — is on Metro Line 2 with a direct connection toward the complex.

For the complex itself, the practical access points are Metro Line 8 (Xingangdong and Pazhou stations) and Line 11 (Pazhou). During the fair, trains and stations are busy from 8:30; arriving at the halls by 9:15 makes the difference between a calm first hour and a queue. Hotels in the Pazhou and Haizhu district command premium prices during Phase 1 and sell out early; many experienced buyers stay along Line 8 or Line 11 one or two stops out, or in the Zhujiang New Town business district, trading a 20-minute commute for materially better rates and dining.

Payment and connectivity are easier than they used to be: international cards work in an increasing number of venues, mobile payment apps accept overseas card binding, and eSIM or airport SIM options cover data. Still, carry some cash-equivalent backup and your bank's cards — a fair week is a bad week to debug payment problems.

Canton Fair vs Year-Round Sourcing: How They Fit Together

A fair is a compression event, not a complete sourcing system. The Canton Fair's organisers run the official online platform and app year-round, with the exhibitor catalogue, product search and messaging available 365 days a year — so the contacts you make in October remain reachable through official channels in February. Professional buyers therefore treat the fair as one leg of an annual rhythm: discover and compare at the fair, verify and sample in the weeks after, order at volume once inspection results land, and use year-round communication for replenishment.

For repeat orders and program management, a fair-only relationship has a structural weakness: the booth staff you negotiated with are salespeople, not order managers. This is where a Guangzhou-based export partner earns its fee — consolidating SKUs from multiple factories into single containers, running pre-shipment inspections with your checklist, handling export documentation, and being reachable in your working hours. Before ordering through any partner, the same due diligence applies: certifications, references, and third-party verification. Our own OE-parts library and OE number lookup tool exist precisely to make program buying verifiable — every application you source should be pinned to a checkable part number, not to a photo on a booth wall.

Sourcing from Guangzhou During Fair Season: The Local Advantage

Guangzhou is not only the fair's host city — it is one of the largest auto parts trading hubs in southern China, with wholesale markets, export warehouses and a dense cluster of parts factories across the wider Pearl River Delta. The changeover days between phases (October 20–22 and 28–30) are the natural window to use that geography: factory visits in the Delta parts belt, sample collection from suppliers met on the booths, and consolidation planning for the orders you intend to place.

Globalucar operates its vehicle and parts export program from Guangzhou's Baiyun district through fair season and all year. For buyers attending the 140th session, we offer the local counterpart role: meet in Guangzhou during or after Phase 1 to review application lists and OE references face to face, visit our export warehouse, and coordinate factory visits and quality inspection for the parts program you assemble at the fair. Bring your shortlist; we will tell you what we can supply directly from our catalog, what we can source faster, and where our cross-referenced OE number library already covers your applications.

What to Pack and What to Budget

The packing list for a parts buyer is short but specific, and the budget lines are dominated by the fair-week hotel premium. The table below is the checklist we send to first-time buyers joining our program.

ItemWhy It MattersNotes / Budget Guide
Comfortable shoesYou will walk 15–20 km a day on concrete hallsBroken-in, not new — blisters end sourcing days early
Business cards (200+)Still outperform app exchanges at boothsPrint name, WhatsApp, company and market focus

FlightsPrices climb as October 15 approachesBook as soon as your dates are fixed

Factory-visit window (optional)Changeover days Oct 20–22 are the natural windowBuyers combining fair + factories typically spend 9–12 days in China

One final packing decision worth making deliberately: travel light on the way in. The buyers who struggle at security on the way home are the ones who left with a full suitcase and then collected a booth's worth of catalogs and samples anyway.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Canton Fair 2026?

The 140th Canton Fair (autumn 2026) runs October 15 to November 4, 2026, in three phases: October 15–19, October 23–27, and October 31 – November 4, with changeover breaks on October 20–22 and October 28–30. Auto parts are in Phase 1, October 15–19.

Which phase of the Canton Fair has auto parts?

Auto parts, vehicles, new-energy vehicles and smart mobility, motorcycles and bicycles are all in Phase 1 (October 15–19, 2026). Electronics, machinery, hardware and tools share the same phase, which is convenient for buyers sourcing workshop equipment alongside parts.

How do overseas buyers register for the Canton Fair?

Register through the official Canton Fair Buyer E-service Tool online: create a buyer account, apply for the buyer badge, and collect the QR-code badge at a designated collection point in Guangzhou with your original identity document. Pre-registration avoids the on-site queue on opening day.

Is buyer registration for the Canton Fair free?

Buyer badge registration for verified overseas buyers is handled through the official system at no charge. Be wary of third-party websites charging fees for "Canton Fair registration" — use the official channel only.

How many days should an auto parts buyer spend at the fair?

Plan on at least four of the five Phase 1 days: two for coverage of your core categories, one for technical deep dives and second visits, and one for negotiation and closing. Buyers adding factory visits in the Pearl River Delta typically stay 9–12 days in total, using the October 20–22 changeover window.

Can I visit the Canton Fair as an individual buyer?

The fair is a trade event open to business visitors with a registered buyer badge — company details and business credentials are part of the registration. It is not a consumer exhibition, but individual purchasing agents, traders and consultants with a business affiliation register and attend routinely.

title: Canton Fair 2026 Closes: What the 140th Session Delivered for Auto Parts Buyers
description: The 140th Canton Fair closed on 4 November 2026 with about 340,000 buyers. What the numbers mean, and the six-week plan that turns contacts into orders.
keywords: auto parts follow up after canton fair
toc: Canton Fair 2026 Closed on 4 November: What That Actually Ends
The 140th Canton Fair in Numbers
What Canton Fair 2026 Phase 1 Told Us About the Auto Parts Trade
The 72-Hour Window Before the Trail Goes Cold
Sort Every Contact into Four Buckets
A Six-Week Canton Fair Follow-Up Cadence

From 340,000 Buyers to One Auto Parts Supplier List

Frequently Asked Questions
content:
The 140th Canton Fair closed at 18:00 on Wednesday 4 November 2026, ending a 21-day calendar that ran three phases with two changeover breaks and marked the fair's 70th year. For auto parts buyers the closing bell is not the end of the buying cycle. It is the start of the 30 days that decide whether the contacts collected at Pazhou turn into purchase orders, and most of the failure happens in week one, quietly, while everyone is still answering emails on the flight home.

What follows is a recap of what the session actually delivered, and the follow-up sequence we run with buyers who leave Guangzhou holding sixty business cards and no plan for them.

Canton Fair 2026 Closed on 4 November: What That Actually Ends

Only the exhibition closed. The online platform that runs alongside the physical fair stays open through the year, and the suppliers you met are still producing and still answering WeChat at 23:00 Guangzhou time. Phase three ran 31 October to 4 November under the "Better Life" theme, with 25,000 booths and more than 12,000 exhibitors across 21 sections, roughly 190 new-product launches and a reported 15% rise in new products on show. None of it is automotive. It matters to a parts buyer for one reason: during phase three the city's freight capacity, hotel stock and translator supply return to normal, which is the window in which factory visits and loading inspections stop being a scheduling problem.

The automotive window was phase one, 15 to 19 October, where vehicles, new energy vehicles and smart mobility, parts, machinery, hardware and tools sit. If you were not in Guangzhou for those five days, Canton Fair 2026 is over for you in the physical sense. The sourcing work is not.

The 140th Canton Fair in Numbers

Headline figures from a fair this size are usually quoted without context. Here is the version we use internally, with the parts-buyer implication attached to each line.

MetricFigureWhat it changes for a parts buyer
Session dates15 October – 4 November 2026, three phasesA 21-day calendar; your buying window inside it was five days
Phase 1 (vehicles and parts)15–19 OctoberThe only stretch where brake, cooling, suspension, engine and electrical suppliers exhibit
Phase 223–27 OctoberConsumer goods, not parts; the changeover week is when factory appointments get easy
Phase 331 October – 4 November, 21 sections, 25,000 boothsNot parts; marks the point where freight and inspection schedules normalise
Overseas buyers by 19 October189,000 from 214 countries and regions, up 13.3% year on yearMore competition for the same supplier hours, not less
Overseas buyers, whole sessionAbout 340,000The pool your future email list is drawn from
Venue area1.55 million m² across four zonesWalking speed is a sourcing constraint, not a detail
Phase-1 intended turnoverUSD 1.37 billion, reported as a record at the phase closeIntent, not contracted value — treat it as sentiment

Two warnings on those numbers. Phase-level turnover carries a definition — intended, agreed or contracted — and the definitions differ between briefings, so compare direction rather than decimals. And a 13.3% rise in arrivals did not mean 13.3% more booth time: the supplier who answered your OE question properly was probably the one with fewer visitors, not more.

What Canton Fair 2026 Phase 1 Told Us About the Auto Parts Trade

The buyer mix moved toward Asia-Pacific. Buyers entering through Guangzhou ports during the session came 60.54% from APEC economies. That is a detail about order size and payment behaviour, not about travel. Those markets tend to place smaller, more frequent orders with tighter specification control, and they expect WhatsApp-level speed. If your follow-up is a formal PDF sent once a week, you are behind the supplier who replied on the walk back to the metro.

Suppliers are selling capacity, not just cartons. Several exhibitors put "Malaysia plant" or "Thailand production" on the booth wall, and the conversation moved from finished-goods price to supply-chain backup. For an auto parts buyer that becomes a question on the follow-up call: which line items are made where, and does the second site cover the same OE references or only the fast movers.

The product mix shifted, the failure modes did not. New energy content was everywhere, with a reported 15% rise in new products launched. The parts that generate warranty claims in your market are still brake friction, cooling, suspension joints and electrical sensors — categories where the difference between a good and a bad supplier is a material certificate and a batch number, not a booth video.

The 72-Hour Window Before the Trail Goes Cold

Memory decays faster than most buyers expect. Sixty conversations in five days blur into a general impression within a week, and by Monday you remember the booth colour but not which supplier quoted USD 4.20 and which quoted 4.85 on the same ceramic pad. Everything below is best done inside 72 hours of leaving the hall, ideally in the hotel the same evening.

  1. Photograph every business card next to the sample you took. Not the card alone. The pairing is the record; a folder of 60 card photos is useless by Thursday.
  2. Write one sentence per supplier, in your own words. Not "good supplier" but "quoted 4.20 at 500 sets, hesitated on the OE cross-reference for the Tucson front pad, said batch numbers are printed on the box". The hesitation is the finding.
  3. Record a 40-second voice note in the corridor if you cannot write. Transcription is cheap; a lost detail is not.
  4. Log the validity date from the quotation itself. If the sheet has no validity date, that becomes question one in your first email.
  5. Label the sample before it goes into the suitcase with supplier name, date and reference, because customs and your own warehouse will separate them for you.

Unglamorous work, and almost nobody does it. It is also why two buyers who visited the same 30 booths end up with different supplier lists six months later.

Sort Every Contact into Four Buckets

You do not have 60 leads. You have four groups, and only one of them deserves your first week. Sorting takes about 40 minutes with the notes in front of you, and it prevents the most common post-fair mistake: treating the most talkative supplier as the most qualified one.

BucketWhat you saw at the boothAction inside 72 hoursDeadline
A — quoted and sampledPrice sheet with a validity date, sample taken, OE references confirmed against your listSend a written spec sheet with photos, confirm the reference numbers, ask the three questions the booth could not answerDay 2
B — quoted, no samplePrice given verbally or on a one-page sheet, sample promised but not packedRequest the sample against your own reference number and pay the courier cost yourselfDay 3
C — catalogue and a colleagueBooth staff handed you to "our export manager" and took your cardOne email, one specific question, no attachmentsDay 5
D — could not answer OE or certification questionsVague answers on material grade, batch traceability or test reportsPark it. Re-test at the next cycle with a written technical questionDay 7

The buckets are not a permanent ranking. They stop bucket D from consuming the hours bucket A needs. A supplier who cannot describe its friction material face to face will not do it better over email, and learning that later costs a container of pads that fail in the first 8,000 km.

A Six-Week Canton Fair Follow-Up Cadence

Most follow-up plans die in week two, when your own customers start asking about delivery. The cadence below is deliberately slow: one reason to write each week, one thing asked for, nothing else.

WeekWhat you sendWhat you ask forReply rate we see
1Spec sheet with photos, target quantity, destination portA corrected quotation against your specification6–7 in 10
2Sample order or sample-fee payment confirmationProduction date and courier tracking5 in 10
3Packaging, marking and label requirementsCarton dimensions, gross weight, label proof4 in 10
4Inspection plan and third-party quoteA confirmed inspection date and factory address3 in 10
5Trial order draft with payment termsProforma invoice and bank details on company letterhead2–3 in 10
6Booking intention and target sailingVessel schedule and cut-off dates2 in 10

Those reply rates come from our own inbox across recent cycles, not from an industry benchmark, and they are why we start with 12 to 15 suppliers rather than three. Six weeks produces two or three who are genuinely ready to ship. That is a normal outcome, not a disappointing one.

Why the October Canton Fair Price No Longer Applies

A quotation collected at the fair is a snapshot of a cost structure on one day in October. Between that day and a December order, four lines move: steel and pig iron, rubber and friction compound, ocean freight, and the exchange rate the supplier used. None of them move dramatically on its own. Together they routinely turn a 4.20 pad into a 4.45 pad, and buyers who treat the Canton Fair price as a fixed reference spend the next two months arguing about a number nobody can hold.

The professional move is to ask for the quotation's cost basis rather than to defend the number. Two questions do most of the work: which input is most volatile in this product, and how much movement triggers a re-quote? A supplier who can answer both has a costing system. A supplier who says "price is fixed, don't worry" either has not thought about it or intends to absorb the change at your expense later, usually through a substitution you did not approve.

Ask for 15 to 30 days of validity on the written quotation and agree in advance what happens after that window. It is a two-line email that prevents a five-week negotiation.

From 340,000 Buyers to One Auto Parts Supplier List

The session drew about 340,000 overseas buyers and more than 30,000 exhibitors. Your job between now and the spring session is to convert that noise into a list short enough to manage: two or three suppliers per part family, each with a sample record, a written quotation, an inspection result and a shipment behind it.

Score the survivors on four things, and resist adding a fifth. Material certification and batch traceability, because friction and load-bearing parts fail on material, not on price. OE cross-reference accuracy, because a pad that fits a 2016 Tucson and not a 2018 one generates returns that cost more than the margin. Packaging discipline, because cartons sized for domestic trucks waste 8–15% of your container. And responsiveness measured in hours during a real problem.

Then place a trial order small enough to survive a mistake. A first order of 200 sets across four references tells you more about a supplier than a container of one fast-moving part, and it costs less when the answer is wrong.

Building the 2027 Auto Parts Sourcing Calendar Before Momentum Dies

Write down when you will next be in Guangzhou, then work backwards from that date. Buyers who do this stop treating the fair as an annual event and start treating it as one checkpoint in a cycle.

WindowWhat to completeOutput you should hold
November – December 2026Bucket A follow-up, samples in hand, trial orders placedTwo or three signed proforma invoices
January 2027Ship before the Chinese New Year production stop; confirm each factory's shutdown and restart datesCargo on the water, or a written sailing date
February – March 2027Review claims, returns and fitment complaints from the trial ordersA revised specification per part family
April 2027141st session (spring); organisers publish exact dates — book accommodation early, Pazhou hotels fill months aheadA pre-booked appointment list, not a cold walk-in
May – August 2027Deepen the two suppliers who shipped well; add one alternative per critical referenceA dual-source plan for your top ten SKUs

Regional shows fill the gaps if you need a second data point on a supplier — the Automechanika editions and CAPAS in Chengdu run on their own calendars, and each has a different buyer mix. Check the dates with the organiser rather than from memory; they shift more often than most buyers assume.

What We Do After the Halls Close

Globalucar is a Guangzhou-based exporter and a sourcing partner during fair season, not an exhibitor at Pazhou, so we do not publish a booth number. What we can do in the weeks after the fair is more useful than a badge scan: hold samples in our Baiyun office for comparison, consolidate parts from three or four factories into one shipment, run a pre-shipment inspection, and quote FOB Guangzhou or FOB Nansha against your own specification rather than a catalogue page.

If you left Guangzhou with a shortlist and want a second opinion, send the OE numbers and the quotation sheets. We will say which references we can cross-check against our own database and which we cannot, which is the fastest way to learn whether the price you were quoted matches the part you were shown.

Frequently Asked Questions

When exactly did the 140th Canton Fair end?

The physical exhibition closed on 4 November 2026, the last day of phase three, which ran from 31 October. Phase one, the automotive window, ran 15 to 19 October. The online platform continues outside those dates.

I missed phase one. Can I still buy auto parts from those suppliers?

Yes, and the process is the same except for the sample. Ask for one against your own OE reference, pay the courier, and treat the sample as the specification. You lose the ability to compare ten suppliers in one afternoon; you recover it by narrowing faster and inspecting earlier.

How long should I wait before following up after the fair?

Two working days for bucket A suppliers, not two weeks. Booth teams clear their card stacks in the first week, after which your email competes with the domestic order book. A short message with the specification attached beats a long one asking how business is.

Is the price quoted at the fair still valid in December?

Usually not, unless the sheet states a validity period. Steel, rubber, freight and exchange rates move between October and December. Ask for the cost basis and the trigger for a re-quote rather than arguing over the original number.

How many suppliers should I shortlist from a session this size?

Twelve to fifteen for follow-up, three to five for sampling, two or three for a trial order. Anything above that is a list you will not maintain. The bottleneck is the inspection and documentation work each one requires.

Do I need to attend both the autumn and spring sessions?

Not every year, but alternating has a cost: suppliers rotate new references into the spring session and price levels reset. If you are developing new part families, the spring session is where sampling costs least.

The fair is a compressed version of a market: 340,000 buyers, 30,000 exhibitors, five days of automotive content and a great deal of noise. The buyers who get value from Canton Fair 2026 are rarely the ones who collected the most cards. They are the ones who sorted the cards within three days, wrote to fifteen suppliers with a specification instead of a greeting, and placed a trial order small enough that being wrong was affordable. That work starts now, not at the next opening ceremony. For a second pair of eyes on the shortlist you brought home, our Guangzhou team is on WhatsApp at +86 133 0240 8528 or at ucars@global-ucars.com, and the auto parts finder covers the thirteen brands we stock most deeply.

title: Canton Fair Auto Parts Halls: Where to Find Brakes, Filters, Suspension & Electrical at Pazhou
description: A hall-by-hall map of the Canton Fair auto parts halls at Pazhou: where vehicles and spare parts sit in Phase 1, how to find brake, filter, suspension and electrical suppliers, hall numbering rules, metro exits and a day-one walking plan.
keywords: Canton Fair Phase 1 auto parts section
where are auto parts at Canton Fair
toc: 1. Why the Hall Layout Matters More Than the Fair Dates
2. Pazhou Complex at a Glance: Four Areas, One Plan
3. Where Vehicles and Auto Parts Sit in Phase 1
4. Finding Brakes, Suspension and Steering Suppliers
5. Finding Filters, Engine Parts and Cooling Suppliers
6. Finding Electrical, Lighting and EV Component Suppliers
7. How the Hall Numbering Works — and a Sample Walking Day
8. Navigation Tools That Save Hours
9. Layout Mistakes First-Time Buyers Make
10. How Globalucar Complements Your Hall Walk
Frequently Asked Questions
content:
Short answer: At the 140th Canton Fair (autumn 2026), the vehicles and auto parts sections sit inside Phase 1 (October 15–19) at the Pazhou Complex in Guangzhou's Haizhu District. The complex is divided into four areas — A, B, C and D — and in recent sessions the vehicle and spare parts exhibits have been concentrated in the newer halls on the west side, with electronics, machinery, hardware and lighting filling the rest of Phase 1. Because hall assignments shift between sessions, always confirm your target aisles in the official buyer app map on arrival, and build your day around one area at a time.

The most expensive mistake an auto parts buyer can make at the Canton Fair is not missing a supplier — it is losing a full day to walking. The Pazhou exhibition halls cover roughly 1.55 million square meters, and a buyer who arrives without a hall plan can easily log 12 kilometers indoors and still leave without a single useful contact. This guide maps out where the Canton Fair auto parts halls sit inside the complex, how to find brakes, filters, suspension and electrical suppliers efficiently, and how to turn a layout plan into a daily walking schedule that ends with real quotations in your inbox.

1. Why the Hall Layout Matters More Than the Fair Dates

Most first-time buyers fixate on dates. Dates matter, but the Canton Fair auto parts halls question decides how much you actually achieve during the five days of Phase 1 (October 15–19, 2026). The 139th session welcomed about 314,000 overseas buyers from 220 countries and regions, and most of them spent their first morning figuring out where to go. A buyer who studies the layout before flying in starts meetings at 9:30 sharp while others are still reading directory boards.

There is a second reason: the fair is organized by product section, not by supplier quality. Two brake pad manufacturers can sit in different areas because one registered under friction materials and the other under motorcycle parts. If you only walk the obvious vehicle section, you will miss exhibitors whose products fit your catalog. And the layout also determines logistics — which metro exit you use and where you can sit down with a supplier all depend on which area hosts your priority sections.

2. Pazhou Complex at a Glance: Four Areas, One Plan

The China Import and Export Fair Complex — almost everyone calls it the Pazhou Complex — sits at 382 Yuejiang Middle Road, Haizhu District, on the south bank of the Pearl River. It is organized into four exhibition areas, each with two floors of halls. The official opening hours are 9:30 to 18:00 daily, with buyer registration desks typically running from about 8:30.

The four areas of the Pazhou Complex and their Phase 1 (Oct 15–19) product focus
AreaPosition in complexNearest metro (Line 8)Phase 1 product focus
Area ANorth-west corner, near Yuejiang Middle RoadXingangdong, Exit AElectronics, appliances, machinery, tools
Area BEast of Area A, next to the Pazhou hotel clusterPazhou, Exit A/BHardware, building equipment, lighting, machinery
Area CSouth side, across Xingang East Road, linked by covered bridgePazhou, Exit C (about 300 m walk)Phase 1 sections vary by session; check the app map
Area DNewer halls on the west/south-west sideXingangdong Exit A, walk west and south (or Pazhou Exit D)Vehicles, spare parts, new energy in recent sessions

Treat the table as a planning aid, not a guarantee. The fair re-assigns sections between sessions as the exhibitor mix changes, and third-party guides often disagree on exact hall numbers for the same session. The official Canton Fair app and website publish the authoritative hall map for each phase, and the floor plan inside the halls matches it.

3. Where Vehicles and Auto Parts Sit in Phase 1

Phase 1 is the only phase that matters for automotive sourcing. The vehicles section — sedans, SUVs, commercial vehicles, new energy vehicles — and the vehicles spare parts section both run October 15–19, 2026. In recent editions the vehicle displays have occupied the newer, larger halls on the west side of the complex, where high ceilings and ground-floor loading suit full vehicle exhibits, while spare parts, motorcycle and related sections have been placed in adjacent halls.

What does this mean in practice? Build your shortlist around three concentric rings:

  1. Ring 1 — the vehicle and spare parts section itself. These halls hold the larger parts groups, new energy vehicle brands and OEM-adjacent exhibitors. Walk this ring on your first day.
  2. Ring 2 — adjacent Phase 1 sections. Machinery, hardware, tools and electronics halls sit in Areas A and B. Many auto parts factories register there because their business scope covers multiple categories.
  3. Ring 3 — the online platform. The fair's online platform runs all year and mirrors the offline exhibitor list. Search it before you fly and you will know which halls deserve a slow walk and which can be skipped.

Once the official hall map for the 140th session is live in your buyer account, convert each ring into a list of hall numbers and bookmark them in the app. Ten minutes of preparation saves roughly two hours per day on the floor.

4. Finding Brakes, Suspension and Steering Suppliers

Chassis and braking components are among the strongest categories for overseas buyers at the fair, because the factories behind them usually run their own casting or friction-material lines and can quote genuine factory-direct terms. Expect to find brake pads, brake discs, calipers, wheel cylinders, shock absorbers, control arms, ball joints and steering linkages spread across the vehicle spare parts section and, in some sessions, the motorcycle parts halls.

When you approach a chassis exhibitor, keep the conversation specific. Booth staff are often sales assistants on their first fair, so the questions that matter are:

  • Which vehicle platforms does the part number cover — Toyota, Hyundai, Kia, VW, or Chinese brands?
  • Is the product supplied to OEM assembly lines, the aftermarket, or both?
  • What certification documents can be shown today — ISO, E-mark, or third-party test reports?
  • What is the minimum order quantity per item, and how are mixed models consolidated into one container?

A useful trick: ask to see the friction material or rubber compound samples, not just the boxed product. A supplier who brings raw material samples to the fair is usually a manufacturer; a supplier who only shows retail boxes is usually a trading company. Neither is wrong — traders can be excellent consolidators — but knowing which one you are talking to protects your price expectations.

5. Finding Filters, Engine Parts and Cooling Suppliers

Engine-related components — oil filters, air filters, fuel filters, spark plugs, pistons, gaskets, water pumps, radiators and condensers — are scattered more widely than chassis parts because they straddle several official sections. Filter manufacturers frequently register under hardware or machinery accessories; radiator and condenser factories often appear next to general machinery suppliers. Two field tactics work well. First, use the exhibitor search in the buyer app with product keywords rather than section names — searching "oil filter" returns every exhibitor handling that product regardless of their registered section. Second, walk one full aisle of a machinery hall on your first afternoon even if it is not on your plan. Filters, hoses, bearings and small engine components surface there constantly, and some of the best quotations experienced buyers collect come from booths they never planned to visit.

Part categories, where to hunt, and the questions that qualify a supplier
CategoryWhere to focusQualifying questions
Brake pads, discs, drumsSpare parts halls; friction material exhibitorsWhich OE numbers? E-mark certification? Friction material source?
Suspension & steeringSpare parts halls; chassis exhibitorsOwn casting line? Warranty terms? Rubber part supplier?
Filters (oil/air/fuel)Spare parts and machinery accessory hallsFilter media brand? MOQ per model? Private label options?
Cooling (radiator, condenser)Machinery halls; cooling system exhibitorsAluminum or copper-brass? Leak test standard? Sample lead time?
Electrical & sensorsElectronics halls, Area A/BWhich vehicle platforms? Batch test reports? Chip origin?

6. Finding Electrical, Lighting and EV Component Suppliers

Electrical parts have the widest footprint of any category. Starters, alternators, ignition coils, sensors, switches and wiring harnesses sit in the electronics halls alongside consumer electronics exhibitors, and lighting sections — including vehicle lamp and LED factories — have historically filled several halls in Area B during Phase 1.

The new energy vehicle wave has widened this further. Battery packs, drive motors, controllers, on-board chargers and charging station components now occupy a visible share of Phase 1, typically near the vehicle exhibits in the newer halls. For buyers serving markets where EV adoption is accelerating — the Gulf, Southeast Asia, Latin America — these aisles are worth a dedicated half day, because many exhibitors there are newer factories with more flexible minimum order quantities.

One caution: electrical components are where quality risk is highest and hardest to judge at a booth. Ask for batch-level test reports rather than datasheets, and note the exact factory name on the report — not the trading company name on the booth — so your pre-shipment inspection later checks the right entity.

7. How the Hall Numbering Works — and a Sample Walking Day

Hall numbers look confusing until you learn one rule: each area numbers its halls in a simple sequence, and the suffix tells you the floor — halls ending in .0 are on the ground floor, halls ending in .1 are on the second floor. Walking the full length of the complex from hall 1 to the last hall in Area C takes 35 to 45 minutes at fair pace; reaching Area D from Area A adds roughly another 30 minutes.

Those distances are why experienced buyers structure each day around a single area instead of chasing suppliers across the complex. A realistic first-day plan looks like this:

Sample day-one walking plan for an auto parts buyer (Phase 1, 9:30–18:00)
TimeZoneFocus
08:30–09:30Badge + entranceCollect badge, confirm hall map in app, coffee, booth list review
09:30–12:00Vehicle & spare parts hallsRing 1: chassis, brake and filter shortlist; collect business cards, scan QR codes
12:00–13:00Rest areaLunch, sort cards, WhatsApp notes while memory is fresh
13:00–15:30Adjacent machinery hallsRing 2: filters, cooling, engine components hiding in machinery sections
15:30–17:00Electronics hallsElectrical parts, sensors, lighting; EV component aisles
17:00–18:00Follow-up desk or hotelSend same-day follow-up messages while booths are still open

On days two and three, mirror the structure for the halls you could not finish. Resist the urge to "just quickly cross" to another area mid-morning — the crossing always costs more than an hour once you include crowds and security checks at the hall entrances.

8. Navigation Tools That Save Hours

The fair has invested heavily in wayfinding, and using these tools properly is the difference between a planned day and a lost one:

  • Official buyer app. Includes the interactive hall map, exhibitor search and booth favoriting. Pre-mark your booths before arrival and the app plots them on the map for you.
  • Metro Line 8. Xingangdong station (Exit A) puts you at the Area A entrance; Pazhou station (Exits A/B) serves Area B, and Exit C walks you to Area C in about 300 meters. The line runs at enhanced frequency on fair days.
  • Electric shuttle carts. Small electric carts run between areas for roughly 10–20 RMB per ride — worth knowing on day three.
  • Pearl River promenade. The outdoor walkway along the river between Areas A and B is usually less crowded than the indoor corridors.
  • Hotel shuttles. Dozens of designated hotels run shuttle buses during the fair. Check your hotel's schedule the night before — the last departures fill up fast after 18:00.

Avoid the taxi queue at closing time. When thousands of buyers leave at 18:00, the ride-hailing lines at Pazhou can take well over an hour. Either stay in the halls until the rush fades — good booths still welcome visitors until closing — or use the metro.

9. Layout Mistakes First-Time Buyers Make

Every fair, the same five mistakes cost first-time buyers real money:

  1. Assuming the "vehicles" sign covers everything automotive. Filters, cooling and electrical suppliers register under other sections. Without a keyword search you will never find them.
  2. No pre-marked booth list. Buyers who navigate "by eye" lose 90 minutes or more daily. The app's favoriting function exists precisely to prevent this.
  3. Area-hopping during peak hours. Crossing from A to D at 11:00 or 15:00 means shoulder-to-shoulder corridors and security queues. Cross at lunch or plan one area per day.
  4. Ignoring the second floor. Halls ending in .1 hold real exhibitors, and they are quieter — some of the best conversations happen upstairs.
  5. No recording system. By day two, business cards blur together. Write one line on each card — price level, MOQ, impression, next step — before you leave the booth.

10. How Globalucar Complements Your Hall Walk

The Canton Fair auto parts halls are excellent for discovering new suppliers, but five days is a short window for qualifying factories, comparing real prices and arranging samples. That is where a local partner earns its keep. Globalucar is a Guangzhou-based vehicle and auto parts exporter — our office in Baiyun District is a short drive from the Pazhou Complex, and during fair week we meet buyers face to face, arrange factory visits across Guangdong's parts manufacturing belt, and quote from an established supplier network that keeps operating long after the halls close on October 19.

A practical pattern many buyers use: walk the fair to see what exists and benchmark prices, then spend the inter-phase break days (October 20–22) visiting factories and consolidators outside the fairground. If you plan to be in Guangzhou during Phase 1, contact Mr Didi at ucars@global-ucars.com or WhatsApp +86 133 0240 8528, or leave a message through our contact page to arrange a meeting or a parts sourcing session. Bring your target OE numbers or a photo of the parts you need — we can check availability against our Kingmay Auto Parts line, which covers engine, fuel, cooling, suspension and electrical systems for Toyota, Hyundai, Kia, VW and 100 other models.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which area of the Canton Fair has auto parts in 2026? The vehicles and vehicles spare parts sections run in Phase 1 (October 15–19, 2026). In recent sessions they have been placed in the newer halls on the west side of the Pazhou Complex, with related categories spread across Areas A and B. Confirm the exact halls in the official app map for the 140th session, because assignments change between editions.

How big is the Pazhou Complex and how long does it take to walk? The complex covers roughly 1.55 million square meters across four areas. Walking from the first hall in Area A to the last hall in Area C takes about 35–45 minutes at fair pace, and reaching the Area D halls adds roughly another 30 minutes. Plan one area per day instead of crossing the complex repeatedly.

What is the fastest way to find a specific part, like a brake pad for a Toyota Corolla? Use the exhibitor search in the official buyer app with product keywords such as "brake pad" or the part category, not section names. The search returns every exhibitor handling the product regardless of their registered section. Bookmark the booths in advance and the app will plot them on the hall map for you.

Which metro station should I use for the Canton Fair auto parts halls? Metro Line 8 serves the complex directly. Xingangdong station (Exit A) is closest to Area A, Pazhou station (Exits A/B) serves Area B, and Pazhou Exit C connects to Area C with a walk of about 300 meters. For the newer western halls, Xingangdong Exit A followed by a walk west and south works well.

Can I see electric vehicle components at the fair too? Yes. Phase 1 includes new energy vehicle sections — battery, motor, controller and charging component exhibitors are usually concentrated near the vehicle displays in the newer halls. If your market is adopting EVs quickly, reserve a dedicated half day for these aisles; many exhibitors there are newer factories with flexible minimum order quantities.

Is it worth visiting if I only have two days? Yes, if you pre-mark your booths and stick to one area per day. Two focused days covering the spare parts halls and one adjacent section produce better results than four scattered days. Many buyers pair the fair with one or two factory visit days in the October 20–22 break, which is when deeper supplier qualification actually happens.

1. The 60-Second Pre-Departure Canton Fair Buyer Checklist: Documents, Devices & Tools

First-time Canton Fair buyers tend to over-pack clothes and under-pack the few documents that actually matter at the gate. The fair's online buyer registration system takes roughly five minutes to fill in from a laptop and saves 30 to 45 minutes of queue time at the on-site badge counter on Day 1. Beyond the badge, this Canton Fair buyer checklist splits into five carry-on groups: documents, devices, measurement tools, sample references, and the social layer. Documents include the buyer badge, the printed invitation letter, business cards in English and Chinese, a tax registration document if you intend to issue a formal purchase order, and a packing list template from your home freight forwarder. Pack these in a single clear plastic folder that sits on top of your bag. Buyers who skip any of these items at the gate lose the next 90 minutes to logistics that should have been a 30-second exchange.

2. Documents and Devices: What Senior Buyers Carry That Newcomers Forget

Senior Canton Fair auto parts buyers run a tighter kit than tourists because the conversation inside a booth is short, technical and reversible only on the spot. The kit splits into five small groups. First, documents: buyer badge, invitation letter, two passport photos (for last-minute Chinese visa renewals if your trip extends), tax ID, business cards, and your home country's import license number if your jurisdiction requires one for HS-coded goods. Second, devices: a phone with Chinese data roaming activated before departure (5 to 8 USD per day for most plans, well below local SIM cost and zero registration friction), a small power bank, and an HDMI-capable tablet if you expect suppliers to show CAD drawings of moulded parts. Third, measurement tools: a digital calliper accurate to 0.01 mm (most Chinese mould-makers carry one, but if you want to spot-check the unit a buyer brought, you save 20 minutes per booth), a small torch for inspecting interior surfaces of castings, and a 1-metre rigid ruler for cartons. Fourth, sample reference: if you are sourcing to fit a specific OE reference, print the OE number on a single A4 sheet along with the vehicle's year, engine code and market (GCC, EU, LATAM). Suppliers cross-reference much faster with this than with a verbal description. Fifth, the social layer: a Chinese payment app installed on your phone if you intend to settle small sample fees by Alipay or WeChat Pay; most major booths accept it but the formal contract still runs on a bank wire.

3. Pre-Fair Online Work: Filter Exhibitors by OE Number, Category & Country

Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair (Oct 15-19, 2026) hosts roughly 20,000 booths across the Pazhou complex. Walking all of them in five days is impossible, which is why the week before departure is the most productive hour of the entire trip. Two free tools cut that workload by 80 percent. First, the official cantonfair.org.cn exhibitor search lets you filter by product category (Vehicle and Auto Parts is category 4 under Mechanical & Hardware), by country of origin (China), and by hall number once you know the hall layout. Save the resulting CSV and sort it by booth number to plan a walking route that does not backtrack. Second, your own OEM parts database: pre-load the OE numbers you intend to source (typically 5 to 15 references from a real procurement list) and email them to five shortlisted suppliers a week before the fair. Their replies by Day 1 will tell you which suppliers actually hold stock for your reference versus which ones will quote on the spot. The third free tool, often overlooked, is the Globalucar OE Lookup on global-ucars.com: it returns cross-references across 12,000+ OE numbers with FOB Guangzhou indicative price ranges. Use it to set a walk-away price before you enter the booth, not after.

4. Day-1 In-Booth Negotiation: Six Questions to Ask Brake Pad Suppliers

Brake pads and rotors are the highest-traffic category at Phase 1. The walk-in question every booth hears is "what's your best price on a Toyota Camry 2018 front pad set". The question that separates serious buyers from walk-ins is what comes next. The six-question test for any brake pad supplier, in the order they should be asked: 1) What is the friction material grade — semi-metallic, low-metallic, ceramic, or NAO? Most will answer low-metallic because it is the default Chinese aftermarket grade. The serious ones will name the brand of formula (Bosch-equivalent, ATE-equivalent, Ferodo-equivalent) and quote an ECE R90 code. 2) What is the minimum order quantity for a custom-formula run versus the catalogue item? Custom MOQ is typically 1,000 to 3,000 sets; catalogue item MOQ is typically 200 to 500 sets. 3) What is the lead time from PO to EXW — 15, 25, or 35 days? Anything above 35 days means the supplier is relaying your order to a sister factory. 4) What testing reports can you show me on the booth? ECE R90 is the European legal minimum; for GCC markets, SASO 1173 is required; for North America, the FMSI code and a copy of the friction material data sheet. 5) Do you have a copy of the IATF 16949 certificate valid through 2027? If yes, ask which certification body issued it (BSI, TUV, SGS are credible; small Chinese-issued bodies are not). 6) Can you take a counter-sample today and ship it by DHL to my office for fitment verification before I sign the PO? A serious supplier will say yes within 30 seconds. The ones who hedge on the counter-sample are the ones you cross off the list.

5. The Filter and Lubricant Stall Playbook: MOQ, Lead Time and Compliance Docs

Oil filters, air filters and fuel filters are easier to source at Canton Fair than brake pads because the SKUs are more standardised, but they have a hidden compliance dimension that catches first-time buyers. The visible stall signage at Phase 1 concentrates on price per unit, but the questions you must ask sit one level below. For oil filters, the four binding specs are: thread size (M20x1.5, M22x1.5, 3/4-16 UNF are the three dominant Asian sizes), gasket diameter, bypass valve setting (typically 0.8 to 1.0 bar), and anti-drainback valve presence. A Chinese aftermarket filter without an anti-drainback valve is cheaper and will leak on cold start, which is why serious fleet buyers will not touch it. For air filters, the binding spec is the media: cellulose (12-month replacement cycle), synthetic (24-month), and HEPA-grade (36-month). Most Canton Fair stalls will quote cellulose media unless you ask. For fuel filters, diesel vs gasoline matters — diesel filters carry a water separation stage at 50 to 100 micron that gasoline filters do not. The MOQ for filters is consistently lower than for brake pads: 500 pieces for catalogue SKUs, dropping to 100 pieces for end-of-line OEM replacements. Lead time is 7 to 15 days for catalogue, 25 to 30 days for custom-branded.

6. Suspension and Steering: What Is Sampleable, What Is Not

Suspension and steering parts — control arms, ball joints, tie rod ends, shock absorbers, struts, stabiliser links — sit in a different negotiation mode than filters and pads because the unit cost is higher and the safety margin is thinner. Two facts that change the conversation. First, almost no Chinese aftermarket suspension supplier will ship a counter-sample of a strut assembly, because the unit cost is 35 to 80 USD and the dimensional verification requires a vehicle on a lift. Instead, they will quote from a CAD drawing and a factory-side dimensional report. The CAD report must show the OE reference, the OE-equivalent part number on their side, and the dimensional tolerance band; if the tolerance band is wider than +/- 0.5 mm on a load-bearing surface, walk away. Second, ECE R90 does not cover suspension parts; the binding compliance document is ECE R13 or ECE R13-H for brake-related suspension, and ISO/TS 16949 / IATF 16949 for the production process. For GCC markets, SASO 1177 is the equivalent; for the Russian and CIS markets, GOST R certification is non-negotiable. Suppliers who claim "we can do all certs" are usually not the ones with the strongest certs. Ask for the certificate number and verify it on the issuing body's website before paying the deposit.

7. Electrical and Sensors: ECE R10, EMC, and VIN-Decoded Cross-Reference

Electrical and sensor parts at Canton Fair Phase 1 are a different category of negotiation again because certification is the gating factor, not unit price. Three compliance documents are non-negotiable depending on the destination market. ECE R10 covers electromagnetic compatibility for any electronic part plugged into a vehicle CAN bus; ECE R7 covers lighting (headlamps, tail lamps, signal lamps); ECE R118 covers fire behaviour for interior wiring. For sensors specifically — lambda, MAF, MAP, ABS wheel speed, knock — the binding spec is the cross-reference table from the OE part to the supplier part, decoded by VIN. A Chinese aftermarket sensor with "fits Toyota Camry 2018-2024" on the box is almost certainly a 1 to 3 percent dimensional compromise; the only safe suppliers are the ones that publish a per-VIN cross-reference table on their website or in their catalogue PDF. The negotiation tempo on Day 1 is also different: electrical buyers tend to spend longer per booth (20 to 30 minutes) because they need to inspect the connector, the wiring harness entry, the potting compound, and the labelling. Plan accordingly: an electrical-only Day 1 is realistic for a buyer who wants to cover 8 to 12 suppliers; a mixed-category Day 1 caps at 15 to 20 suppliers across all six categories.

8. Recording What You Saw: Three Methods Senior Buyers Actually Use

The most common buyer mistake at Canton Fair is treating the fair as a one-shot deal and leaving with photos they cannot decode a week later. Three recording methods that work. Method 1: voice memo with a fixed script. At every booth, after the conversation, record a 30-second memo with the booth number, supplier name, part discussed, unit price, MOQ, lead time, and one differentiating fact ("they showed ECE R90 cert #E4*1179*2018*0045" or "they could not produce a friction material data sheet"). Most buyers who use this method reduce their post-fair shortlist time from three weeks to one. Method 2: standardised paper card per supplier. Print 50 small cards before departure (one per supplier), each with fields for booth number, supplier name, contact, key part, price, MOQ, sample fee, and a 0-5 score for credibility. A photo of the card at the end of Day 5 is your entire shortlist in one image. Method 3: photo log with EXIF date. Most modern phones already tag photo metadata with date and time. Snap the booth number sign, then a photo of the product, then a photo of the supplier's business card, in that order. Sort by timestamp later and you have a chronological trip log without any extra effort.

9. Day-5 Follow-Up: The 48-Hour Window That Determines Your Margin

Phase 1 closes at 18:00 on Day 5 (Oct 19, 2026). The 48 hours between the close and the next morning is the single most under-used window in the Canton Fair cycle. Two things happen in that window: the best suppliers send their revised pricing because they now know they have lost buyers to competitors, and the worst suppliers go silent because they have filled their order book. The professional buyer uses the window by sending a single, structured email to the shortlist within 24 hours of Phase close. The email has five fields: thank-you note (one sentence), recap of the part discussed at the booth, the price they quoted on the spot, the buyer's target price (typically 8 to 15 percent below the quoted price for catalogue parts, 5 to 10 percent for custom), and a request for a counter-sample shipment within 7 days. By Day 10 after the fair, half of the suppliers will have replied with a revised price; by Day 14, the buyer's shortlist has consolidated to 3 to 5 candidates; by Day 21, the first PO can be issued. Buyers who wait until Day 14 to send the email get quoted 5 to 10 percent higher prices because the suppliers have moved on.

10. Frequently Asked Questions: Canton Fair Buyer Checklist for Auto Parts Buyers

What is the best time to arrive at Canton Fair Phase 1 for auto parts buyers?

Day 1 morning (09:30 to 11:00) is the worst window for serious sourcing because every booth is crowded with walk-ins and the senior sales staff is tied up greeting buyers. Day 1 afternoon (14:00 to 17:30) or Day 2 morning are the two best windows: booths are quieter, senior staff is free, and the supplier has had 24 hours to recover from the morning rush. Most top auto parts suppliers at Canton Fair are also at the autumn edition (Phase 1, Oct 15-19), so the timing holds for repeat buyers.

Do I need a visa invitation letter for Canton Fair 2026?

Yes, for most non-visa-free nationalities. The invitation letter is issued free of charge by the Canton Fair once you complete online buyer registration and upload your passport scan. The processing time is 5 to 10 working days, so apply at least three weeks before departure. The letter is a Chinese government-issued document that smooths the M-visa application at your local Chinese consulate; it is not the visa itself.

How much cash should I bring to Canton Fair for sample fees?

For a five-day sourcing trip covering 30 to 50 suppliers across six auto parts categories, plan on 800 to 1,500 USD in cash or instant-payment app balance for sample fees. Most sample fees for brake pads, filters, and small electrical parts run 5 to 50 USD per sample. Larger items such as strut assemblies or ECU modules can run 100 to 300 USD per sample. Ask the supplier to deduct the sample fee from your first PO before paying it in cash.

Is Chinese the working language at Canton Fair auto parts booths?

Mandarin is the working language at most Chinese exhibitor booths. English is widely understood at the larger, export-focused booths in categories 4 (Vehicle and Auto Parts). Arabic, Russian and Spanish speakers are increasingly common at booths targeting Middle East, CIS and LATAM buyers respectively. If your Chinese is zero, bring a translator for the first half-day; by Day 2, the technical vocabulary converges on English terms (MOQ, lead time, OE reference, FOB, ECE R90).

Can I take product samples home in my luggage from Canton Fair?

Yes for small, low-value items (brake pads, filters, sensors, ignition coils). Declare them at customs on exit if they have commercial value above 50 USD. For larger or heavier items (strut assemblies, exhaust components, radiators), the supplier will arrange courier shipment through DHL, FedEx or a nominated freight forwarder. Plan on 7 to 15 days door-to-door for DHL/FedEx, 25 to 35 days for sea freight.

What is the difference between FOB Guangzhou, FOB Shenzhen and EXW Nansha for Canton Fair orders?

FOB Guangzhou or FOB Shenzhen means the supplier delivers the goods to the named Chinese port and loads them onto the buyer's nominated vessel; the buyer pays ocean freight and insurance from that point. EXW Nansha (or EXW any inland city) means the buyer takes responsibility at the supplier's factory gate and arranges all inland transport to the port plus ocean freight. FOB is the Canton Fair default and is recommended for first-time buyers because the supplier's nominated freight forwarder handles the export customs clearance. EXW is cheaper in unit cost (typically 1 to 3 percent lower) but requires the buyer to engage a Chinese freight forwarder, which is more setup cost than it is worth for first-time buyers below 5 containers per year.
