content:
Every buyer arrives at Pazhou with the same twenty or thirty questions, and most of them get answered badly at a hotel lobby or a WeChat group. This page collects the thirty that come up most often from auto parts importers, answered with the operational detail that actually changes a decision: which phase has your category, what the badge costs, how long a quotation stays valid, when to pay, and what happens to a shipment after the halls close. Dates and rules are for the 140th session, 15 October to 4 November 2026.

The 2026 Calendar, in One Table

The fair runs in three phases with two switch-over gaps. Auto parts sit in Phase 1 only, which is the single most expensive misunderstanding in this category: a buyer who books flights for late October will walk into furniture and then clothing.

PeriodDates (2026)What is exhibitedRelevance to an auto parts buyer
Phase 115–19 OctoberVehicles and two wheels, auto parts, hardware and tools, machinery, electronics, new energyThe only phase with parts, tools and workshop equipment
Switch-over20–22 OctoberHalls closed and rebuiltFactory visits, sample review, supplier meetings outside the venue
Phase 223–27 OctoberHouseware, gifts and decorations, building and furnitureUseful only for packaging, display and shop-fitting suppliers
Switch-over28–30 OctoberHalls closedSecond window for plant audits in Guangdong
Phase 331 October – 4 NovemberTextiles, garments, shoes, bags, food, medical, stationery, toysNo auto parts; sourcing continues in the city, not on the show floor

Opening hours are 9:30 to 18:00 daily. The venue is the Canton Fair Complex in Pazhou, Haizhu District, across roughly 1.55 million square metres with about 75,000 booths and more than 32,000 exhibitors. The 139th session drew around 314,000 overseas buyers from 220 countries, which is the number to keep in mind when you plan walking routes: this is a city, not a hall.

Before You Book the Flight

1. Is the buyer badge free?

Pre-registration online is free and the badge is issued against your passport at the registration counters and appointed hotels. On-site registration without pre-registration is commonly reported to carry a service fee in the region of RMB 100–150, plus a queue. Pre-register at least two weeks before you travel.

2. Do I need a visa, and how do I get the invitation letter?

Most nationalities need a business (M) visa. The buyer registration system issues an invitation letter once your registration is approved, and that letter supports the visa application. Several countries currently hold visa-free or trial visa-free entry, but the lists change; confirm with the Chinese embassy in your country before paying for flights.

3. How many days do I need for auto parts?

Three full days in Phase 1 is the practical minimum for a first visit, four if you are covering both parts and workshop equipment. The complex is measured in kilometres, and a bad route can cost half a day. Shortlist exhibitors in the official app before you land and walk with a plan by hall number.

4. Where should I stay?

Walking distance to Pazhou is convenient and expensive; fair-week hotel rates commonly run two to three times the normal level, and walkable rooms sell out weeks ahead. Metro Line 8 serves the complex directly, so a hotel two or three stops away often beats paying for proximity. Our Guangzhou travel guide covers the trade-offs zone by zone.

5. Will my phone and my money work?

Google services and WhatsApp are not reachable on local networks, so install a working VPN before departure. Alipay and WeChat Pay linked to an international card cover almost every payment, including metro and convenience stores. Carry a few hundred yuan in cash for the exceptions.

At the Venue

6. Which hall has auto parts?

Parts are grouped in the vehicles and two wheels section of Phase 1, alongside motorcycles, bicycles and vehicle accessories. Hall numbering changes between sessions, so use the official floor plan for the 140th session rather than a map from last year, and confirm the hall with the exhibitor before you walk.

7. Can I attend more than one phase on the same badge?

Yes. One badge covers the whole session, so a buyer sourcing parts in Phase 1 and packaging in Phase 2 does not pay twice. The badge is personal and checked at every entrance.

8. Can I buy samples or small quantities at the booth?

This is a wholesale fair and MOQs commonly start in the hundreds per reference. Samples are usually available, sometimes free and sometimes at a stated charge, and exhibitors are most willing to sell display stock on the final afternoon of their phase. Agree the sample price and the courier cost in writing before the item leaves the booth.

9. Is there an official interpreter service?

The fair runs an official interpretation service, and most booths have English-speaking sales staff. For technical negotiation on materials, tolerances or tooling, a bilingual colleague or a local sourcing partner is worth more than booth-level translation, because the vocabulary that matters is engineering vocabulary.

10. How do I find a specific exhibitor inside the complex?

The 140th session extends the ASK ME assistant introduced in April, with booth-level indoor navigation across the venue and photo-to-product matching. Treat it as a routing tool, not a verification tool: it tells you where a booth is, not whether the company behind it is a factory.

11. What should I bring on the day?

Passport, badge, business cards in English and Chinese, a power bank, a notebook, and a phone with the exhibitor list already shortlisted. Comfortable shoes matter more than a suit. Bring your own measuring tools if you are qualifying parts on the floor; a caliper settles arguments that a brochure cannot.

Talking to Suppliers

12. Factory or trading company — how do I tell at the booth?

Ask which plant makes the part, in which city, and how many production lines it runs. A trader will answer with a product range; a factory will answer with a location and a capacity. Then check the business licence, whose registered scope and address either match the story or do not.

13. Is the quoted price final?

No. Booth prices are opening positions and a negotiation round after the fair is normal. What you should not do is negotiate a discount without changing anything else: volume, packaging, payment terms and delivery window are the four levers that move a price honestly.

14. What does a proper quotation contain?

Reference, description, material or grade, quantity, unit price, currency, Incoterm with a named port, lead time, MOQ, packaging, validity date and payment terms. If any of those is missing, the quote cannot be compared with another one, and the lowest-looking number usually turns out to be EXW with no export clearance included.

15. What MOQ should I expect on parts?

Stocked catalogue references can start in the tens of pieces. Made-to-order references run into the hundreds, and private-label packaging commonly starts around 500 pieces per reference. Because minimums apply per reference, a mixed container is negotiated line by line rather than as one number.

16. Should I pay a deposit at the booth?

No. A deposit belongs after a written contract, a verified bank account and, for anything beyond a trial order, a factory audit or at least a documented plant visit. Paying at the booth removes every lever you have.

17. How do I keep track of forty conversations?

Photograph the booth number and the business card together, and write three lines on the spot: what they make, what they quoted, and what you still need. Suppliers receive hundreds of cards; the buyers who win are the ones whose notes are still readable in week three.

Verification, Before Money Moves

18. What does the business licence prove?

That the company exists, its registered capital, its scope and its address. It does not prove that it manufactures, and it does not prove that it can export. Cross-check the registered address against the plant address on the quotation.

19. Does IATF 16949 certification mean the parts are good?

It means the plant runs a documented automotive quality system within a stated scope. Check the certificate number in the public database, read the scope, and check the expiry date. It says nothing about the specific lot you are buying; that is what material certificates and inspection are for.

20. How do I check an OE number?

Take the number off the part being replaced, confirm it against the VIN and production date, then compare the supplier's cross-reference. Treat every cross-reference as a claim to be verified, not as an equivalence. Our OE parts lookup and the OE reference library are starting points, not final authority.

21. When is a factory audit worth the money?

Before any order that would hurt to lose. A third-party audit of a parts plant typically costs a few hundred US dollars and takes a few days to schedule, which is small against a container. For trial orders, a documented visit and a production-line sample are a reasonable substitute.

Orders, Payment and Paperwork

Term you will hearWhat it means in practiceWhen it is reasonable
30 / 70Deposit with the order, balance against the B/L copyRepeat supplier with a delivery record
30 / 70 after inspectionBalance released once the pre-shipment report passesFirst order from a new supplier
100% before productionYou carry all the risk from day oneSample orders under a few thousand dollars
L/C at sightBank pays against compliant documentsLarger orders, unfamiliar counterparty

22. What payment terms are normal?

Thirty per cent deposit with the order, seventy per cent against the bill of lading copy or after pre-shipment inspection, is the common structure. Anything demanding full payment upfront from a new supplier is a reason to slow down, not to negotiate harder.

23. T/T or L/C?

T/T is normal below roughly USD 50,000 and cheaper for both sides. Above that, or with a new supplier in a new market, an L/C shifts risk but adds bank charges and document strictness: one mismatched description can hold payment for weeks.

24. Who arranges shipping under FOB?

You do. Under FOB the supplier delivers to the named port and clears export; you nominate the forwarder, pay ocean freight and insurance, and handle import. Name the port precisely — "FOB Nansha" or "FOB Shenzhen (Yantian)", never "FOB China" — because inland trucking differs by port.

25. Which documents should arrive with the container?

Commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin where a preferential rate applies, and the export declaration on request. Check the HS code on the invoice before the vessel sails; correcting a classification after arrival is far more expensive than correcting it in Guangzhou.

After the Halls Close

26. How fast should I follow up?

Within 72 hours, while the booth conversation is still identifiable. Reference the booth number, the part discussed and the price quoted, attach your specification, and ask two or three specific questions. A generic "please send your best price" gets a generic reply, if any.

27. How long does a quotation stay valid?

Ask for a stated validity, commonly 15 to 30 days. Steel, rubber and freight move, and a quote without a validity date is an invitation to renegotiate at the worst moment — after you have promised your own customer a price.

28. When should I order samples?

Immediately after shortlisting, and from the production line rather than from display stock. Test the sample against the old part: dimensions, material, finish, markings. Approve it in writing with photographs, because the approved sample becomes the reference for the pre-shipment inspection.

29. Can I still source after 4 November?

Yes, and most of the year happens outside the fair. Guangzhou suppliers quote year-round, and a buyer with a shortlist can run sampling, inspection and shipping on a normal schedule. The fair compresses discovery; it does not replace follow-up.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can anyone attend the Canton Fair?

It is a trade fair for buyers, not a public exhibition. Register as an overseas buyer with your passport and business details, and you will be issued a badge. Consumers looking for single items are usually turned away at registration rather than at the door.

Is the Canton Fair cheaper than Alibaba?

Not automatically. Many exhibitors sell on both channels. The advantage of the fair is physical verification: real samples, real staff, and a face to hold to a delivery date. The disadvantage is that booth rent is priced into the quotation.

Can I bring a colleague or my family?

Additional staff can be registered as buyer representatives, usually against a fee and a company letter. Children are admitted under the fair's visitor rules but the halls are not a family venue: distances are long, aisles are crowded and there is nothing to do for a child in a parts hall.

What if I lose my badge?

Report it at a registration counter and apply for a replacement; a fee in the region of RMB 200 is commonly reported. Keep a photograph of the badge number on your phone so the replacement is quick.

Do I need to speak Chinese?

No for the booth, yes for the factory. Sales staff speak working English, but once you move to a plant, the people who know why a batch failed often do not. Budget for interpretation on factory days, not on show days.

What is the one thing buyers regret most?

Arriving in the wrong phase, or arriving in the right phase without a shortlist. Both are avoidable with a calendar check and two hours of preparation, and both cost a week of travel that cannot be recovered.

A One-Page Checklist

If you keep nothing else from this page, keep the sequence. The order matters more than the detail.

WhenDo thisOutput you should hold
8 weeks outRegister, apply for the invitation letter, book a refundable hotel near Line 8Badge approval, visa application lodged
4 weeks outBuild the shortlist from the exhibitor list; write your specification and target price15–25 exhibitors with hall numbers
Phase 1Walk the shortlist, collect quotations on a single template, photograph booths10 comparable quotes, 10 named plants
Switch-overVisit two or three plants; order production samplesAudit notes, sample tracking numbers
72 hours afterSend structured follow-ups with specifications attachedWritten replies with validity dates
Week 3–6Approve samples, place a trial order, agree inspection protocolSigned PO, approved sample record

The fair is a discovery mechanism with a very short memory. Everything that determines whether the trip pays for itself happens in the five weeks after the badge is clipped back onto your bag.

title: Canton Fair Phase 1 Opening Day: Game Plan for Auto Parts Buyers
description: Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair runs 15-19 October 2026. A day-one game plan for auto parts buyers: where the parts halls sit, remote badge pick-up, how to sequence the floor, the five questions to ask every booth, what to record, and the mistakes that cost the rest of the week.

content:
Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair opened on 15 October 2026 and runs to 19 October. The buyers who get value out of it are rarely the ones who walk the most halls — they arrive with a sequence. Day one at Pazhou is where a five-day sourcing trip is either set up or quietly wasted: the complex covers roughly 1.55 million square metres, some 32,000 exhibitors are on the floor, and the auto parts, vehicle and new energy categories you came for sit alongside machinery, hardware and lighting across the same five days. This guide is the day-one plan: what is open, where the parts halls fit, how to sort your badge before you queue, how to sequence the floor without burning your energy by noon, what to ask and record at each booth, and the mistakes that cost buyers the rest of the week.

What Is Open: Phase 1 at a Glance

Before you plan the day, confirm the frame you are working inside. The 140th session runs in three phases, and for auto parts only the first one matters — Phase 2 moves to housewares, gifts and building materials, and Phase 3 to textiles, toys and food. The China Import and Export Fair Complex in Pazhou hosts all three, but the exhibitor list changes completely between phases, so a buyer who arrives in the wrong window finds nothing relevant.

Two numbers frame the week: about 1.55 million square metres with around 32,000 exhibitors, and roughly 314,000 overseas buyers from 220 countries and regions at the previous session. Scale like that rewards filtering far more than walking.

ItemPhase 1 detailWhy it matters on day one
Session140th Canton Fair (autumn 2026)Confirms which official schedule and app data applies
Phase 1 dates15–19 October 2026Five trading days; day one is for scanning, not closing
Trading hours09:30–18:00 dailyEight and a half hours minus lunch and transit
VenueChina Import and Export Fair Complex, Pazhou, Haizhu District, GuangzhouAreas A–D are internally connected but walking costs time
Exhibition areaAbout 1.55 million m²Plan by area, not by “the whole fair”
ExhibitorsAround 32,000Pre-filtering on the official platform is mandatory
Changeover breaks20–22 October and 28–30 OctoberNatural windows for factory visits outside the halls

Treat the 09:30–18:00 window as roughly six usable hours after security, transit and a meal. That is the real budget for day one, and why the sequence below matters more than stamina.

Where Auto Parts Sit Inside Phase 1

Auto parts does not occupy a single labelled building — it sits inside a cluster of vehicle-related categories that run together through Phase 1. Alongside vehicle and auto parts, the phase covers new energy vehicles and smart mobility, motorcycles, bicycles, new energy products, lighting, electronic and electrical products, hardware and tools, plus a long tail of machinery and industrial categories.

The practical consequence is that your target suppliers are scattered across several areas rather than gathered in one. A brake parts buyer may find friction material suppliers in one area and machining-capable factories in another, while the moulding and packaging capability that decides landed cost sits elsewhere again. Buyers who assume there is a single “auto parts hall” spend their first morning discovering that there is not.

Our walk-through of the auto parts halls at Pazhou maps how brakes, filters, suspension and electrical suppliers distribute across the complex. Read it the night before and mark your top fifteen exhibitors on the venue plan — that list is your day-one route.

Badge First: Registration and the Remote Pick-Up Option

Nothing else works until the badge is sorted, and this is the step most first-time buyers lose an hour to. Overseas buyer pre-registration runs year-round through the official buyer service system, and the buyer badge itself is free for qualified overseas buyers. The detail that saves the most time: first-time overseas buyers can complete pre-registration online and then collect the badge at remote registration centres rather than queueing at the complex.

Those remote points include Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport, Guangzhou South Railway Station, the Pazhou Hong Kong–Macao passenger port, designated badge hotels, and the Canton Fair office in Hong Kong. If you are flying in on the morning of day one, collecting at the airport or your hotel the evening before is the difference between starting at 09:30 and starting at 11:00.

If you have not registered at all, do it on the official platform before you leave the hotel — our step-by-step guide to registering as an overseas buyer, including the invitation letter and visa questions, covers the sequence. Keep your passport, a photo of it, and your confirmation accessible; you will show them repeatedly.

Your First 90 Minutes Inside the Complex

The first ninety minutes are for setup, not selling. Enter through the gate for your target area, clear security, and get oriented before you speak to anyone. The complex is large enough that a wrong entrance costs twenty minutes of walking before you have met a single supplier.

Once inside, do four things in order. Collect or confirm your badge and keep it visible. Download or open the official app and sign in, since exhibitor search, booth navigation and messaging all run through it. Pull up your pre-filtered exhibitor list and sort it by area so that your route does not cross the complex twice. Then set a meeting rhythm: two or three substantive conversations per hour is a realistic ceiling once you include walking time, and trying to beat it produces a stack of business cards you cannot act on later.

The fair continues to extend real-time indoor navigation and positioning across the complex. Use it, but keep a screenshot of your route as backup — connectivity inside a crowded hall is not guaranteed.

How to Sequence the Halls on Day One

The most common structural mistake on day one is front-loading conversations. Buyers meet their most promising supplier first, spend ninety minutes in a deep discussion, and reach their second target at 13:00 with no baseline for comparison. Day one is a scanning day: gather enough quotes and samples to compare, and save the negotiation for days three and four when you have five competing offers in hand.

TimeActivityTarget output
09:00–09:30Arrive, clear security, enter your first areaInside the hall before trading gets busy
09:30–11:00Fast pass over your pre-filtered listShortlist of 8–12 booths worth a second visit
11:00–13:00Deep conversations at the top 4–6 shortlisted boothsQuotation sheets with MOQ, lead time and packaging
13:00–14:00Lunch and same-day notes while memory is freshWritten notes on every booth visited
14:00–16:30Second area or the remaining shortlistComparison set across at least 3 suppliers per part
16:30–18:00Book follow-ups, confirm factory visit slotsCalendar holds for days 2–5 and the changeover break

Two scheduling notes. The 20–22 October changeover break has no exhibition running, making it the window for factory visits outside Pazhou — confirm those slots on day one while suppliers are still on site. And because Phases 2 and 3 bring different exhibitor lists, any supplier you want to see again must be re-booked inside 15–19 October.

Five Questions to Ask at Every Auto Parts Booth

Booth conversations drift toward price far too early. Price is the last variable worth pinning, because it means nothing until you know what is being quoted. These five questions take under ten minutes together and separate a real manufacturer from a catalogue reseller.

QuestionWhat a strong answer sounds likeWhat should slow you down
Are you the manufacturer or a trading company?Names the factory, the production site and the processes done in-houseVague answers about “our partner factory” with no location
Can you quote against this OE number?Confirms the number, states fitment and any supersessionQuotes only a generic part category with no number check
Which certifications cover this part?Names IATF 16949 or ECE R90 where relevant, with certificate scope and validityA certificate photo with no number, scope or expiry readable
What is the MOQ and the lead time?Specific MOQ per reference, realistic lead time, states whether mixed orders countA single MOQ quoted for every part regardless of type
How is it packed and how many fit a container?Gives carton quantity, packing method and a 20ft or 40ft loading figure“We will check later” on packing, which hides freight cost

The fifth question is the one buyers skip, and it is where landed cost is actually decided. A part quoted two percent lower but packed twenty percent less efficiently loses the difference in freight. Our guide on verifying auto parts suppliers at the fair covers certificates, OE cross-references and factory audits in more depth — bring it with you.

What to Record Before You Walk Away

By the end of day one, booths blur. Two suppliers with similar catalogues become indistinguishable within forty-eight hours unless you captured something specific at the time. The fix is a fixed record you fill in standing at the booth, before the next conversation overwrites the last one.

FieldWhy it matters later
Area, aisle and booth numberLets you return on day three without searching
Company name and business card photoCards get separated from notes; a photo does not
OE numbers quoted, with your own fitment listThe only reliable basis for comparing two quotations
Quoted price, MOQ, lead time, incotermWithout the incoterm, two prices are not comparable
Packing data and container loading figureDetermines landed cost more than unit price does
Sample photo with label and booth sign in framePrevents the classic “which supplier sent this” problem
Your verdict: shortlist, maybe, or dropA one-word judgement made on the spot beats a vague memory

Our buyer checklist for Phase 1 covers what to bring — cards with a WeChat QR code, a caliper, a portable charger and a printed OE list. Seven fields per booth feels heavy until day four, when only one of three suppliers has complete numbers.

Day-One Mistakes That Cost Buyers the Week

Six errors account for most wasted Canton Fair trips, and every one of them is a day-one error. Negotiating seriously on day one before you have competing quotes. Committing to a factory visit without checking how far it is from Pazhou. Accepting a quotation without an incoterm. Photographing products without capturing the booth number. Spending the morning in the wrong area because you entered at the nearest gate rather than the right one. And skipping the changeover-break planning until the last day, by which point the good factory visit slots are gone.

There is also a quieter one: treating the five days as the whole opportunity. The official online platform and app run year-round and mirror the on-site categories, so a supplier you miss this week is still reachable in November. Buyers who combine both — this is covered in our comparison of Canton Fair sourcing versus year-round online sourcing — recover most of what a tight schedule costs them.

Using the Online Platform While You Walk the Halls

The official website and app operate continuously through the year with the same categories as the physical fair, which makes them useful inside the halls rather than only after them. Exhibitor and product search filters by industry, product type, parameters and company type, so you can resolve a question on the floor instead of noting it for later. Buyers can publish purchasing intentions, exchange e-cards, and book appointments; suppliers can also initiate contact once you are connected.

The app adds the pieces that matter on day one: booth navigation, digital catalogues, an AI assistant for answering fair questions, AI note-taking, itinerary planning and badge application. Set it up the evening before, not at the gate. Combined with real-time navigation deployment across the venue, it turns the app into your floor plan rather than a brochure.

One caution: the platform is a discovery and communication tool, not a verification tool. Everything it tells you about a supplier still needs the on-booth checks — licence, certificates, samples, OE numbers — before it becomes a purchase decision.

Where a Guangzhou-Based Export Partner Fits

Not every buyer arrives with a team. If you are sourcing alone, or covering several part categories in five days, a local partner changes what day one can achieve: someone to pre-screen the exhibitor list, join supplier meetings as a second pair of ears, and translate not just language but the difference between a factory quoting its own line and a trader quoting someone else’s.

At Phase 1 this week, 15–19 October 2026? Send your OE number list and target categories — we are based in Guangzhou, a short drive from Pazhou, and can prepare a walking route, sit in on supplier meetings, or meet you between halls for sample review. Contact Mr Didi: ucars@global-ucars.com  |  WhatsApp +86 133 0240 8528  |  or reach us through our contact page. Checking a part number before you quote it? Look it up in our OE parts library, or read our full Canton Fair 2026 auto parts buyer’s guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

What time does Canton Fair Phase 1 open?

Trading runs 09:30–18:00 daily across 15–19 October 2026. Arriving before 09:30 lets you clear security and enter your first area before the halls fill. After security, transit between areas and a meal, budget roughly six usable hours rather than the full eight and a half.

Do I need a badge, and can I get one at the venue?

Yes, overseas buyers need a buyer badge, and pre-registration through the official buyer service system is open year-round and free for qualified overseas buyers. First-time overseas buyers can pre-register online and collect the badge at remote centres including Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport, Guangzhou South Railway Station, the Pazhou Hong Kong–Macao passenger port, designated badge hotels and the Canton Fair office in Hong Kong — which avoids queueing at the complex on day one.

Which phase should auto parts buyers attend?

Phase 1 only, 15–19 October 2026. Auto parts, vehicles, new energy vehicles and smart mobility, motorcycles and bicycles all sit in Phase 1, alongside hardware, tools, lighting and machinery. Phase 2 moves to housewares, gifts and building materials, and Phase 3 to textiles, toys and food, with exhibitor lists changing completely between phases.

How many suppliers should I visit on the first day?

Plan a fast pass over your pre-filtered list in the morning to shortlist eight to twelve booths, then hold substantive conversations at four to six of them. Two or three real conversations per hour is a realistic ceiling once walking time is included. Day one is for building a comparison set, not for closing — negotiate on days three and four with several quotes in hand.

What should I record at each booth?

Capture area, aisle and booth number; company name with a photo of the business card; the OE numbers quoted against your own fitment list; price with MOQ, lead time and incoterm; packing data and container loading figures; a sample photo with the label and booth sign in the same frame; and a one-word verdict. Without the incoterm, two prices are not comparable, and without the booth number you cannot return.

Can I still source from Canton Fair exhibitors after 19 October?

Yes. The official website and app run year-round with the same categories as the physical fair, supporting exhibitor search, purchasing intentions, e-card exchange and appointment booking. The 20–22 October and 28–30 October changeover breaks have no exhibition running, which makes them the practical windows for factory visits and sample reviews outside the halls.

title: Canton Fair Phase 1 Wrap: How to Shortlist Suppliers in 48 Hours
description: Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair closed on 19 October. A 48-hour routine for turning booth notes into a supplier shortlist: one row per supplier, a weighted scorecard, three buckets, the follow-up that gets answered, and what to demand before the 20-22 October changeover.
toc: What You Are Holding — and Why It Expires in 48 Hours
Step One: One Supplier, One Row
Step Two: Score Everyone on the Same Sheet
Step Three: Sort Into Three Buckets
Step Four: Send the Follow-Up That Gets an Answer
What to Demand Before 22 October
Five Ways Buyers Damage Their Own Shortlist
What the 20–22 October Break Is Actually For
When Price Is the Only Thing Left

Frequently Asked Questions

content:
Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair closes at 18:00 on 19 October, and by tonight the aisles at Pazhou will be empty again. What you do in the next 48 hours decides whether five days on the floor turn into a supplier list you can actually buy from, or into a stack of business cards you will never read twice. This is the shortlisting routine that works when you are holding dozens of booth notes, a handful of quotations, and a flight home.

What You Are Holding — and Why It Expires in 48 Hours

By the afternoon of day five, most buyers are carrying the same mess: a phone gallery full of booth photos with no captions, business cards with handwritten numbers on the back, three quotations received over WeChat, one over email, and a memory that already cannot tell the coated rotor supplier from the plain one. That is normal. The problem is not the volume of notes — it is that none of it is comparable yet.

Raw booth notes are impressions. A shortlist needs rows. Until every supplier occupies one row with the same fields filled in, you are ranking on enthusiasm, and enthusiasm at a trade show correlates poorly with delivery performance. The four steps below convert impressions into a ranking you can defend to your own purchasing team three weeks from now.

If you recorded booths using the field list in our Canton Fair buyer checklist, this stage is mostly transcription. If you did not, you will be reconstructing from photographs — which is exactly why the 48-hour window matters.

Three things expire at once when the halls close. First, the exhibitors leave: the changeover break runs 20–22 October with no exhibition in session, and most booth staff travel back to their factories the same evening. A salesperson answering from a production office is not the same person who pulled a sample off the shelf for you on Tuesday.

Second, the quotation you were given was priced against a fair-week context — floor-space urgency, competitor booths within earshot, a sales manager authorised to discount. That context disappears with the booth. Buyers who wait until November frequently discover the price moved, or that the "we will confirm" item was never actually quoted.

Third, and most expensive, is your own recall. Five days of booths blur fast. The supplier who mentioned they hold stock for your specific OE numbers is indistinguishable from the one who said they could develop them — unless you wrote it down. Two weeks later you cannot tell, and you will send the same generic follow-up to both.

Working inside 48 hours does not mean deciding in 48 hours. It means getting every supplier into a comparable state while the people who met you are still reachable and still remember you.

Step One: One Supplier, One Row

Build a single sheet — a spreadsheet, not a document — with one row per supplier and the same nine fields on every row. Resist the urge to write paragraphs. If a field cannot be filled from your notes and photographs, leave it blank rather than guessing; a blank is honest and a guess is expensive.

FieldWhy it earns a column
Company name + booth areaTwo suppliers may share a trading name; the hall and aisle locate them later
Contact person + WeChat/WhatsAppThe person who met you, not the general inbox — this is who answers
Categories they actually makeSeparates factories from trading companies reselling the same catalogues
OE numbers confirmed vs "can develop"The single strongest predictor of whether a first order runs smoothly
Quoted price, currency and IncotermQuotes are only comparable when the term matches; note FOB port too
MOQ per part numberA low unit price with a 2,000-piece MOQ is a different product
Lead time for a first orderIncludes tooling where new development is required
Sample statusSeen / requested / paid for / shipped — and the date you asked
Certificates shownName them specifically, do not write "has certificates"

Once the sheet exists, count the blank cells. A supplier with four blanks out of nine is not a shortlist candidate — it is a conversation you never finished. That is useful information, and it is far cheaper to learn on day five than after a deposit.

Step Two: Score Everyone on the Same Sheet

Now weight the columns. A simple 100-point scorecard beats a gut ranking, because it forces you to decide in advance what matters for your business rather than for the supplier's pitch. The weights below suit auto parts importers buying service-line parts for existing vehicle parc; adjust them if you are building a new catalogue from scratch.

CriterionWeightWhat a high score looks like
OE coverage on your actual list25Confirms your part numbers from stock, not "we can develop"
Sample quality seen by hand20Machining, coating, packaging and markings inspected, not photographed
Commercial terms15FOB price, MOQ and payment terms stated in writing
Documentation15Named certificates, test reports, traceable batch records
Responsiveness during the fair15Answered within a day, brought the right person to the booth
Logistics fit10Consolidates with your existing Guangzhou shipments or a known forwarder

Score each supplier 0–5 on every criterion and multiply by the weight. The output is rarely a surprise — you usually know who your top three are — but the exercise exposes the uncomfortable cases: the supplier with the lowest price and the weakest documentation, or the one who was charming and gave you no numbers at all. Those are the two profiles that generate most post-fair disputes.

Step Three: Sort Into Three Buckets

Drop the scored list into three buckets and stop treating them the same way.

Bucket A — pursue now. Score above roughly 75, with confirmed OE numbers and a written quotation. These get a specific follow-up within 24 hours and a sample order request. Two or three suppliers per category is the right size; more than that and you are spreading your own attention too thin to negotiate well.

Bucket B — keep warm. Scored 55–75, usually because documentation or samples are incomplete rather than because the price is wrong. These get one clear request for the missing item and a deadline. Many Bucket B suppliers become A within a fortnight simply because nobody else asked them for the certificate.

Bucket C — archive. Below 55, or with blank fields you cannot close. Archive them with a note explaining why. A note written today costs thirty seconds; the same reasoning reconstructed in March is impossible, and the supplier's card will resurface in your next sourcing round.

Step Four: Send the Follow-Up That Gets an Answer

Generic messages lose. "Thank you for your time, please send your catalogue" arrives in an inbox alongside two hundred identical notes and reads as nothing. What gets a reply is specificity: the exact part numbers, the quantity band, the port, and a question that requires a real answer rather than a brochure.

Part of the messageWhat to write
Subject lineYour company + the part category + the fair — no "greetings"
Opening lineWhere you met them and one concrete detail from the conversation
The askA quotation against named part numbers, in a named quantity, FOB a named port
The extra questionOne thing only a real factory can answer: tooling, coating spec, batch traceability
The deadlineA date, and what happens on that date — "so we can confirm before the 22nd"
ChannelEmail for the record, WhatsApp or WeChat for the nudge 24 hours later

Send it to the person who met you, and copy the company address. If you met three people at one booth, message the one who answered your technical questions — that is usually the person with access to production, not the one with the business cards.

What to Demand Before 22 October

The changeover break is the natural cut-off. Ask for these items now so that the answers land while you are still in China and can act on them, rather than after you have flown home and lost the room to negotiate.

Ask forWhat it tells you
Written quotation with part numbers, price, MOQ, Incoterm and portWhether the verbal number survives contact with their sales office
Certificate copies with number and scopeWhether the certificate covers your part family, not just the factory
Sample plan: cost, courier, dispatch dateWhether they treat samples as a step or as an obstacle
Tooling cost and ownership, if new developmentWho owns the tooling and whether a second source is possible later
Production lead time for a repeat orderWhether the first container is repeatable or a one-off effort
Reference customers in your regionWhether they already ship to your market and know its paperwork

Our guide to verifying auto parts suppliers on certificates, OE numbers and factory audits goes through how to read what comes back. Two documents arrive in the first reply more often than buyers expect — and both are easy to check.

Five Ways Buyers Damage Their Own Shortlist

Ranking on price alone. A price without an Incoterm, an MOQ and a lead time is not a quotation. It is an opening remark. Comparing opening remarks across five suppliers produces a winner who cannot deliver.

Keeping everyone. A shortlist of eleven is not a shortlist. Every supplier you keep costs you an email, a sample negotiation and a mental slot; three per category is workable and nine is not.

Waiting for the perfect quotation. Suppliers do not send a complete quote for free to an unknown buyer. Ask for the two fields you actually need — usually price at a stated quantity and lead time — and build from there.

Following up only by email. In China the reply almost always arrives on WeChat or WhatsApp first. Send both, and keep the email thread as the record you will quote from later.

Skipping the note on rejected suppliers. Without a reason recorded, the same card comes back in six months and you will re-run the whole evaluation from zero.

What the 20–22 October Break Is Actually For

The changeover is not dead time. With no exhibition running, it is the only clear window for factory visits outside Pazhou — Foshan, Dongguan, Zhongshan and the Pearl River Delta parts belt are all within reach, and the suppliers you met are back at their plants. This is where a Bucket A supplier either holds up or does not: the booth was a presentation, the factory is the evidence.

Use the break for three things: see one factory per shortlisted supplier if geography allows, review physical samples with a caliper rather than a photograph, and settle the commercial terms that were too awkward to finish on a crowded aisle. Our Guangzhou travel guide for Canton Fair week covers transport and payment practicalities if you are extending the stay.

When Price Is the Only Thing Left

Eventually two suppliers sit within a few percent of each other and the scorecard cannot separate them. Break the tie on things that cost you money later rather than now: who holds stock against your OE numbers, who has shipped to your market before and understands its paperwork, who answers in hours rather than days, and whose packaging survives a long-haul container. A two-percent price difference disappears the first time a shipment is held at customs for missing markings.

It is also worth keeping a second source in Bucket B for the same part family. Single-source dependence on a supplier you met five days ago is a risk you are taking on your own balance sheet, and the cost of maintaining one alternative quotation is close to zero.

Where a Guangzhou-Based Export Partner Fits

Everything above assumes you are still in Guangzhou and still reachable. Many buyers are not — the fair ends, the flight leaves, and the follow-up has to run from another time zone against suppliers who are now back at full production workload.

That is the gap a local partner closes. We are based in Guangzhou, a short drive from the Pazhou complex, and during fair season we can visit the suppliers on your list on your behalf, collect and inspect samples, and put the quotations side by side in one comparison sheet with the Incoterms and MOQs normalised. If you recorded OE numbers rather than part descriptions, send that list — it is the fastest route to a quotation that means something. Our comparison of Canton Fair sourcing against year-round online sourcing explains how we keep the conversation going after the halls close.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does Canton Fair 2026 Phase 1 close?

Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair runs 15–19 October 2026 at the Pazhou complex in Guangzhou, with negotiation hours from 09:30 to 18:00 daily. The changeover break follows on 20–22 October with no exhibition in session.

Do auto parts return in Phase 2 or Phase 3?

No. Phase 2 (23–27 October) covers consumer goods, gifts, home decor, building materials and furniture, and Phase 3 (31 October–4 November) covers toys, textiles, garments, shoes, stationery, medical and food. Auto parts appear only in Phase 1, so any supplier you missed cannot be revisited at this session.

How soon should I follow up after the fair ends?

Within 48 hours of the halls closing. Booth staff travel back to their factories during the 20–22 October changeover, response times lengthen, and quotations given in the fair-week context are easiest to confirm while the people who met you are still at their desks.

How many suppliers should stay on a shortlist?

Two or three per part category. That is enough to negotiate and to hold a second source, and few enough that you can actually manage the sample requests and quotation comparisons without losing track of the details.

What if a supplier never answers the follow-up?

Send one nudge on WeChat or WhatsApp after 24 hours and one more after three days, then move them to the archive with a note. Silence during the shortlisting stage is itself an answer about how the relationship will run once there is a deposit at stake.

Can I still source after the fair closes?

Yes. The official Canton Fair online platform and app run year-round with the same product categories, so exhibitors remain contactable after the halls empty. Many buyers use the fair to build the shortlist and the online platform to continue the conversation through the year.

title: Canton Fair Price Negotiation: Realistic Auto Parts Discounts
description: How much discount is realistic on auto parts at Canton Fair: 3-8% bands by category, MOQ price steps, payment-term costs and the spec cuts to refuse.
keywords: how much discount at canton fair
toc: Why the Real Discount Window Opens After Phase 1 Closes
What “Discount” Means in an Auto Parts Quotation
The Realistic Discount Ladder
Where the Margin Actually Lives
MOQ Is the Price Lever That Actually Moves
Payment Terms Carry a Price
Concessions That Cost the Supplier Nothing
Three Discounts That Cost You Money
The Counter-Offer Script: Six Questions
Timing Your Close: Phases, Validity and Production Slots
Frequently Asked Questions
content:
Phase 1 of the 140th Canton Fair closed on 19 October with 189,000 overseas buyers from 214 countries and regions, up 13.3 percent on the last session. Most left Pazhou with a folder of quotations and one unresolved question: how much of that number is negotiable? For auto parts the answer is a band rather than a figure — on commodity friction and chassis parts a 3 to 8 percent cut from the first quote is normal, 12 percent or more warns that the specification is about to change, and when you ask matters as much as how.

Why the Real Discount Window Opens After Phase 1 Closes

The price quoted at a booth is a show price. Everyone on that floor knows the buyer is comparing twenty suppliers in three days, so the salesperson quotes the top of the range and holds two or three concessions back. That is not dishonesty; it is how a five-day exhibition works.

The conversation changes once the halls go dark. Phase 1 ran 15–19 October, the changeover covers 20–22 October, and Phase 2 (23–27 October) is home goods and building materials — no auto parts until the 141st session in April 2027. Phase 3 (31 October–4 November) is textiles and toys. So a Canton Fair price negotiation on parts almost always happens by email, in the week after your flight home, with a sales team that has time to check stock and ask the plant manager for a real number.

Two forces pull in opposite directions in that window. Factories are hunting orders to fill Q4 capacity, which softens unit prices; they are also booking slots against a February production stop and a pre-holiday freight peak, which hardens lead times. Ask for the discount in the first week after the fair, ask for the schedule in November, and put both into one proforma invoice. Our 48-hour shortlist routine covers the filtering step; this is the pricing conversation itself.

What “Discount” Means in an Auto Parts Quotation

Before comparing percentages, fix the baseline. Three numbers get called a discount here, and confusing them is how buyers end up paying more than last year. The catalogue price is a list for distributors, routinely 20 to 30 percent above real FOB. The first quote at the fair is a trimmed version of it, still carrying a negotiation reserve. The number you name is only useful if it is anchored to a cost you understand.

So the useful question in any auto parts price negotiation is not “how low can you go” but “what is this price built on”. A brake pad quotation rests on a friction mix code, a pad thickness, a backing plate gauge, a shim type, a box configuration and an Incoterm. Change one and the price moves without anyone calling it a discount. A supplier who drops 12 percent without touching one of those has either been overquoting you all along, or intends to change them later.

The Realistic Discount Ladder

The bands below come from our own 2026 quotation files for Guangzhou and Pearl River Delta suppliers — the spread between the first written quote and the price an average-volume buyer settles at. Treat them as order of magnitude, not as a tariff.

Part categoryFirst quote to settled priceWhat has to be true to reach the top of the band
Brake pads (high-volume Toyota, Hyundai, Kia applications)3–8%Single mix code, 500+ sets per part number, neutral packing, 50% deposit
Rotors and drums (castings)2–6%Buyer absorbs freight weight, accepts one coating spec, orders a full pallet
Filters, bearings, hardware, seals4–10%Consolidated order across many SKUs from one supplier, annual frame
Suspension and steering (control arms, ball joints, tie rod ends)3–7%Mixed container across platforms, longer lead time, no custom marking
Sensors and electronics (ABS, TPMS, ignition)1–4%Little room: component cost dominates, volumes thin per SKU
Private label or tooled parts0–3% on price, more on termsTooling amortization, print quantities, payment terms, sample waivers

Read the last column rather than the percentages. The band is not an entitlement — it is what a factory can fund. Friction and hardware are elastic because the bill of materials is flexible; sensors are not, because nobody negotiates with a chip. Push a sensor quote to the bottom of the pad band and the reply is a polite email, not an order confirmation.

Where the Margin Actually Lives

To argue price credibly you need to know which line of the quote has room. Below is the cost stack we see repeatedly for a front pad set at 500 sets, as a share of FOB value.

Cost lineShare of FOBCan a factory move it without you noticing?
Friction compound28–34%Yes — mix grade and pad thickness are the classic levers
Backing plate, shim, hardware12–16%Yes — plate gauge and shim presence are easy to trim
Pressing, curing, grinding labour and energy10–14%Barely — cycle time is fixed by the press
Inner box, carton, pallet, marking6–9%Yes, and often a fair trade to make explicitly
Factory overhead, scrap, rework8–11%Only through order stability
Factory profit6–10%Yes, down to 3–4% for a repeat buyer with clean payments
Export docs, inland haul to Nansha, forwarder fees3–5%Yes, by changing the Incoterm rather than the price

Two conclusions follow. Profit is the smallest single line, so a factory giving away 10 percent has handed over its entire margin plus a slice of overhead — which is why deep discounts rarely survive to the second order. And the two biggest lines are the easiest to alter, so any discount above roughly 6 percent needs a written specification in the proforma invoice.

MOQ Is the Price Lever That Actually Moves

Volume is the concession every factory understands. These five references, priced at three levels under identical specification and packaging.

OE referenceApplicationProduct200 sets/pcs5001,000
04466-12130Toyota Corolla / Auris (E18)Front brake pad setUSD 4.8USD 4.2USD 3.9
04465-06090Toyota Camry (V50 and later)Front brake pad setUSD 5.1USD 4.5USD 4.1
04465-26300Toyota Hiace (H200)Front brake pad setUSD 5.4USD 4.8USD 4.4
51712-02100Hyundai / Kia front axleBrake discUSD 11.5USD 10.4USD 9.6
28101-02A10Hyundai / Kia applicationsBrake pad setUSD 4.6USD 4.0USD 3.7

The step from 200 to 500 units is worth roughly 10 to 13 percent per unit — more than any argument about margin will win. The step from 500 to 1,000 adds another 7 to 8 percent, because the set-up cost has already been absorbed. That is the shape to exploit: reach the first volume step on your two or three fastest movers, buy slow movers at 200, and stop pushing. Demanding 1,000-unit pricing on 200 units across forty SKUs asks a factory to fund inventory nobody will sell.

Reference numbers matter here. Suppliers quote from an OE index, and our OE parts library covers brake, chassis and engine references across Toyota, Hyundai and Kia so you can build the volume list before writing to anyone. For the friction and coating decisions underneath the price, see the brake sourcing guide from this session.

Payment Terms Carry a Price

Every payment term has a financing cost inside it, and at factory level that cost lands in the quotation as a percentage. Asking for a lower unit price while holding 60-day credit asks the supplier to lend to you and discount the loan; the two cancel out.

Payment structureEffect on unit priceWhy the factory prices it that way
100% deposit before production2–4% below baselineNo working capital tied up; offered on small or repeat orders
50% deposit / 50% before shipment0.5–1.5% below baselineStandard for a first order; covers raw material purchase
30% deposit / 70% before shipmentBaselineThe default T/T structure in most quotes you collected at the fair
L/C at sight1–2.5% above baselineBank charges, document handling, slower cash release
60-day credit after bill of lading2–3.5% above baselineFactory borrows working capital at its own cost for two months

Two details sit outside the table and are worth as much as the percentages. Who pays the wire fee: at USD 30–50 per transfer, four part-payments on a USD 12,000 order is real money. And validity: a USD quote held for 30 days is a different offer from one held for 90, and a supplier asked for 90 will build an exchange-rate cushion into it.

Concessions That Cost the Supplier Nothing

Not every concession is a price cut, and factories grant these more readily because they cost little.

Carton configuration and slot. Moving from a printed colour box to a plain carton with a branded label saves 2 to 4 percent of packaging cost, which a supplier can pass through. If your customers buy off a shelf, keep the box; selling to workshops, take the saving. And a factory at 70 percent utilisation prices an order it can schedule in its quiet week better than one squeezed in before a peak — ask which week is light.

Mixed applications in one shipment. Freight per set falls when a container carries six applications from one supplier instead of one application from six. Unit prices barely move; landed cost drops.

Incoterm and banking. FOB Nansha, EXW factory and CIF destination are three prices for the same goods; with a forwarder you trust, EXW plus your own booking usually beats a CIF quote with an inland margin inside it. Sample costs refunded against the first order, and tooling amortised across three shipments instead of paid upfront, improve cash flow without touching the unit price.

Three Discounts That Cost You Money

The discount that hurts is paid for out of the product. Three versions recur in friction and chassis parts, each with a written defence.

Thinner friction, cheaper mix. A pad ground to 7.5 mm instead of 9 mm saves compound and looks identical in a photograph. Service life falls by roughly the same proportion, and your customer finds out in eight months rather than eight days. Defence: state pad thickness and mix grade in the proforma invoice, then check the first shipment with a caliper.

Thinner plate, missing shim. Backing plate gauge dropping from 1.5 mm to 1.2 mm, or a shim quietly dropped from the assembly, saves visible steel and less visible noise control. Defence: name the plate gauge, the shim type and whether anti-squeal coating is applied, then sign off a first-article sample against those values.

Certificates that do not cover the SKU. A friction approval is issued for a product family and a formulation, not for a factory in general, so forty applications are not covered by one test report. Defence: ask for the approval number and its application list, then match your OE list against it. Our guide to verifying suppliers by certificate and audit turns that into a checklist.

The Counter-Offer Script: Six Questions

Most buyers lose the negotiation in the first email by naming a number without a reason. A number with a reason is a proposal; a number alone invites silence or a quiet downgrade.

Before naming anything, get six answers in writing. Which friction mix code and pad thickness is this price built on? What is the backing plate gauge and shim specification? What happens to price and lead time at 600 sets instead of 200? What is the price on a 50 percent deposit? Which references ship from your Guangzhou warehouse and which need a production run? How long does the quotation hold?

Those answers give you a baseline comparable across suppliers, plus a cost model that shows which concession to spend. A supplier who answers all six has stock visibility and its own tooling; one who answers two is a trader, and the price should reflect it. Then name your target: 5 to 7 percent under the settled Canton Fair band, attached to something you are giving — a doubled first order, a 50 percent deposit, a two-month delivery window, plain packing. Ask for 15 percent with nothing attached and the reply is a discount on paper plus a thinner pad in the carton.

Timing Your Close: Phases, Validity and Production Slots

The calendar does more work than most buyers realise. Phase 1 ended on 19 October, the second changeover runs 28–30 October around Phase 2, and the fair closes on 4 November after Phase 3. Those dates do not touch auto parts supply directly, but they shape attention: until 4 November every supplier you met is handling two other categories and a stream of new enquiries, and the buyer who writes within five working days keeps the top of the file.

Quotation validity is the practical clock. Most sheets in your folder carry 15 or 30 days, which puts the decision in mid-November. Confirm by then and you get a production slot that ships before the February holiday; confirm in December and the price holds while the ship date slips — a difference in landed cost that usually exceeds the discount you were arguing over.

Two habits make the timing work. Follow up every three working days with one new piece of information — a revised quantity, an added application, a packaging decision — because a message that adds something gets answered. And once the price is agreed, ask for the loading plan: carton counts, pallet heights and container fill decide freight per unit.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much discount is realistic on auto parts at Canton Fair?

For commodity categories — brake pads, filters, hardware, common chassis parts — 3 to 8 percent off the first written quote is normal once volume, packing and payment terms are settled. Precision and electronic parts move 1 to 4 percent. Above 12 percent usually signals a specification change.

Should I negotiate at the booth or after the fair?

After. The booth quote is a show price held back for comparison shopping, and the salesperson cannot check stock or call the plant. Write within five working days of leaving Pazhou with your volume and payment structure.

What MOQ should I expect for brake and suspension parts from China?

Brake pads usually quote 100–500 sets per part number, discs 100–300 pieces, calipers 50–200 units, and suspension items 100–300 pieces.

Which payment term gets the lowest price?

50/50 T/T, at 0.5 to 1.5 percent below the standard 30/70 without the working-capital penalty of credit. L/C at sight adds 1 to 2.5 percent; 60-day credit adds 2 to 3.5 percent.

Can I get a lower price by accepting a longer lead time?

Yes, usually 1 to 3 percent, because the factory can slot your run into a quieter week instead of interrupting a peak line. Spend that concession before touching the friction specification.

Are auto parts cheaper at Canton Fair than on sourcing platforms?

Not automatically. The fair gives face-to-face verification and a faster read on who owns tooling; platforms give price transparency with less certainty about the factory behind them. The pattern we recommend is in our comparison of fair and online sourcing.

If you want a second price on a specific application list before replying to a supplier, send the OE references. We quote brake, chassis and engine parts for Toyota, Hyundai and Kia platforms from verified Guangzhou suppliers and will tell you which line of your quotation has room. Write to Mr Didi at ucars@global-ucars.com, message WhatsApp +86 133 0240 8528, or use the contact form; our Baiyun office is a short drive from Pazhou. Price bands are listed in the auto parts catalogue, and the parts finder works by brand, model and system.

title: From Canton Fair to Container: Turning Quotations into FOB Shipments
description: The operational gap between a signed quotation and a loaded container: what a shippable FOB quote contains, who books what, the cut-offs that sink shipments, LCL versus FCL arithmetic and consolidation.
toc: Why a Good Quotation Produces a Bad Shipment

From Approved Sample to Purchase Order
Who Does What Under FOB
The Three Dates That Sink Shipments
LCL or FCL: The Arithmetic Buyers Skip
Consolidating Three Suppliers Into One Container
Payment Against Documents
The Five Mistakes That Kill a Good Quotation
A Workable Timeline for a First Container
Frequently Asked Questions
content:
A quotation is a promise about a price. A container is a promise about a date, a weight, a document set and a bank transfer, and the distance between the two is where most first orders die. This is the operational sequence between a signed quotation at Pazhou and a loaded container at Nansha: what the quotation must contain, who books what under FOB, which cut-off dates actually sink shipments, and how to consolidate three suppliers into one bill of lading without losing traceability.

Why a Good Quotation Produces a Bad Shipment

Most quotations collected at the fair are built to win a comparison, not to survive a booking. They quote a unit price, a MOQ and a lead time, and stop there. Then the order moves into a different world: carton dimensions, pallet counts, gross weight, HS classification, export clearance, booking cut-offs and a payment schedule tied to a document that does not exist yet.

Each of those is a place where the price quietly changes. A supplier quoting USD 4.20 per filter can deliver a container at USD 5.10 landed at the port because the cartons were sized for a domestic truck, the pallets were not fumigated, and the goods were declared under a code that triggered an inspection. None of that is dishonesty. It is the ordinary result of a quotation that was never designed to be shipped.

What a Shippable FOB Quotation Contains

Ask every shortlisted supplier to complete the same template before you compare anything. The template is the comparison; a price list is not.

FieldWhy it decides the shipmentWhat "good" looks like
Incoterm and named portFixes who pays inland trucking, export clearance and origin charges"FOB Nansha, Incoterms 2020" — a port, not a country
Unit price at stated quantityReveals the volume break before you commitPrice at MOQ, at 1× container and at 2× container
Carton dimensions and gross weightDrives CBM, container fit and freight per pieceLength × width × height in cm, kg per carton, pieces per carton
PalletisationChanges usable CBM by 8–15% and may require ISPM 15 treatmentStated pallet footprint, stackability, fumigation status
HS code (6-digit minimum)Sets duty, inspection risk and whether a preference certificate appliesSupplier's proposed code, to be confirmed by your broker
Lead time and production startDistinguishes stock from made-to-orderDays from deposit, plus the deposit's clearing date
ValidityProtects you when steel, rubber or freight moves15–30 days, in writing
Payment scheduleDetermines your cash exposure before the B/L exists30% deposit, 70% against B/L copy or after inspection

Two of these fields do the most work and are the most often skipped: carton dimensions and the HS code. The first decides whether your cargo fits the container you booked. The second decides whether it clears at the duty rate you modelled.

From Approved Sample to Purchase Order

The purchase order is not a formality; it is the document that converts a conversation into a specification. Write it after the sample is approved, not before.

  1. Approve the sample in writing. Photograph it, label it with the reference and the date, and state in the PO that this sample is the inspection reference.
  2. Freeze the specification. Material grade, surface finish, marking, packaging and label artwork all belong in an annex. "As discussed" is not a specification.
  3. Fix the quantity per reference. A container is built from line items; the total is a result, not an instruction.
  4. Name the inspection point. Pre-production, during production and pre-shipment are different checkpoints with different costs. Our inspection guide sets out what each one can catch.
  5. State the documents you expect. Invoice, packing list, B/L, certificate of origin, and material certificates for friction, suspension and load-bearing parts.
  6. Agree the delay clause before the deposit. A realistic remedy for late delivery is easier to agree at order stage than after the vessel has sailed without your cargo.

Who Does What Under FOB

Under FOB the supplier's job ends when the cargo is on board at the named port. Yours starts there, and the handover is where responsibility quietly gets lost.

TaskSupplierBuyerCommon failure
Production and packingYesSpecifiesCartons built for domestic pallets, wasting CBM
Inland trucking to portYes—Booked too late for the gate-in window
Export customs declarationYesProvides classification inputHS code invented at the last minute
Ocean booking and freight—YesBuyer books after production, misses the sailing
Marine insurance—YesAssumed the forwarder's liability covers cargo
Origin charges and THCUsually included in FOB priceConfirms what is includedDuplicate origin charges billed at destination
Import clearance and duty—YesDocuments arrive after the vessel

Book the forwarder before you sign, not after production finishes. A booking made in week one gives you a sailing date to write into the contract; a booking made in week six gives you whatever space is left, at whatever rate is left.

The Three Dates That Sink Shipments

Every booking carries several cut-offs and they are not interchangeable. Missing the wrong one costs a week; missing the right one costs the container.

Cut-offTypical timingWhat happens if you miss it
Booking / space confirmation2–4 weeks before ETD in peak seasonNo space; cargo rolls to the next vessel
SI (shipping instruction) cut-off3–7 days before ETDB/L details wrong or late; amendment fees and customs mismatch
VGM (verified gross mass)Typically 24 hours before loadingContainer not loaded, regardless of paperwork
Gate-in / port cut-off2–4 days before ETDTruck turned away, storage and rebooking costs
Document cut-off for the B/L1–3 days after sailingOriginal B/L delayed, buyer cannot clear on arrival

Timings vary by carrier, port and season, and peak-season congestion in the Pearl River Delta can compress all of them. Treat the table as a planning frame and the carrier's booking confirmation as the authority. The practical rule: work backwards from the sailing date, and put every cut-off into the same calendar as the production schedule.

LCL or FCL: The Arithmetic Buyers Skip

Auto parts are dense, which changes the usual advice. A pallet of brake rotors is heavy and small; a pallet of plastic trim is light and bulky. The decision is not "small goes LCL" — it is which constraint binds first, weight or volume.

Shipment shapePractical optionWhat drives the costWatch out for
Under ~2 CBM, urgentAir or expressChargeable weightDense metal parts price badly by air
2–12 CBMLCLPer CBM, with a minimumDestination charges often exceed freight
12–24 CBMLCL or a 20ftBreak-even depends on destination feesCo-loading damage on heavy cartons
24–28 CBM20ft FCLFlat container rateWeight limit before volume limit
55–68 CBM40ft HQFlat rate, best cost per CBMPayload limit on dense parts

Rough usable capacity is about 28 CBM for a 20ft and 65–68 CBM for a 40ft high cube, but a container of brake discs will hit the road-weight limit long before it is full. Ask the forwarder for the payload limit on your lane, then calculate the load by weight as well as by volume. LCL freight is commonly quoted per CBM with a minimum charge, and the destination side — documentation, terminal handling, delivery order — frequently costs more than the ocean leg on small shipments.

Consolidating Three Suppliers Into One Container

The most common shape of a first auto parts order is three or four suppliers, none of whom can fill a container alone. Consolidation solves that, but only if traceability survives it.

  • Use one forwarder for the whole shipment. Two forwarders means two sets of origin charges and an argument about who booked what.
  • Keep separate packing lists per supplier. One master B/L can carry several house bills, but each supplier's cartons must be identifiable on arrival.
  • Mark cartons by supplier code and reference. A colour-coded label per supplier is the simplest system that survives a warehouse transfer.
  • Inspect at the consolidation warehouse, not only at each factory. Damage happens in transit between plants; a second count at the warehouse catches it while the supplier is still responsible.
  • Check the export declaration split. Multiple suppliers means multiple exporters of record; confirm who declares what, and that the totals match the commercial invoice.

Consolidation also changes the inspection plan. If three factories finish in three different weeks, the pre-shipment inspection has to happen at the warehouse against the combined packing list, otherwise the last supplier's cartons never get looked at.

Payment Against Documents

The payment schedule and the document set have to be designed together. A 70% balance "against the B/L" is only meaningful if the B/L actually proves what you paid for.

  • 30% deposit / 70% against B/L copy. Fits a repeat supplier with a delivery record. The weakness: you pay before you have seen the loaded cargo.
  • 30% deposit / 70% after pre-shipment inspection. Fits a first container from a new supplier. The supplier holds the cargo until the balance clears, so build a few days into the schedule.
  • L/C at sight. Fits orders above roughly USD 50,000 or an unfamiliar counterparty. Strict document compliance is the price: one mismatched description can delay payment for weeks.
  • Balance against telex release. Only works when you control the forwarder, which under FOB you do — provided the B/L is issued to your account.

Under FOB you nominate the forwarder, which gives you one useful lever: the B/L is issued to your account, so the supplier cannot release cargo to a third party. Use it. Confirm in writing that the B/L will be issued as "freight collect", that the shipper is the supplier, and that the consignee is your company exactly as it appears on your import licence.

The Five Mistakes That Kill a Good Quotation

  1. Booking after production. The order is ready and the next sailing is in three weeks. Book in week one.
  2. One HS code for a mixed container. Brake pads, filters and bearings do not share a classification. A blanket code invites inspection and duty reassessment.
  3. Cartons measured in the supplier's units. Centimetres versus inches, pieces per carton versus per inner box — a single unit error changes the CBM by an order of magnitude.
  4. No approved sample record. Without it, the inspection has no benchmark, and every argument about "within tolerance" becomes an opinion.
  5. Documents that disagree. Invoice, packing list and B/L must match on quantity, description and weight. Customs systems compare them automatically.

Each of these costs less to prevent than to fix. The prevention is a single page: the quotation template, the approved sample record and the cut-off calendar, kept together from the day the order is placed.

A Workable Timeline for a First Container

Auto parts orders from Guangdong to most destinations run six to ten weeks from deposit to arrival, with the ocean leg taking the largest share. The sequence below is the one that leaves room for the failures that always happen.

WeekActionOwner
0Approve sample, sign PO, pay deposit, book forwarderBuyer
1Confirm booking and sailing date; lock cut-offs into the calendarBuyer / forwarder
2–4Production; mid-production check on the first batchSupplier / QC
4–5Pre-shipment inspection; correct and re-check if neededQC
5Submit SI, confirm VGM, truck to port by gate-inSupplier / forwarder
5–6Export clearance, loading, B/L issuedForwarder
6–9Ocean transit; documents couriered or released electronicallyForwarder
9–10Import clearance, duty, deliveryBuyer / broker

The buffer is deliberate. A first container that runs to a perfect schedule is the exception; a first container that recovers from one slipped cut-off is normal. Plan for one slip and the order still arrives when you promised.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is FOB always better than CIF for auto parts?

For regular shipments with your own forwarder, FOB usually gives better cost visibility and control. CIF is simpler for a first trial order, but suppliers commonly add a margin to freight, and you inherit their carrier choice and insurance terms.

Can the supplier book the container and still quote FOB?

That is CIF or CFR in practice, whatever the quotation says. Under true FOB you nominate the carrier. If the supplier insists on booking, ask for the freight cost broken out separately so you can compare it with your own rate.

How much does a 40ft container of auto parts hold?

About 65–68 CBM of usable volume, but dense parts such as rotors, drums and suspension components hit the payload limit first. Calculate by weight as well as by volume before you commit to a container size.

What documents do I need for import clearance?

Commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and a certificate of origin if you are claiming a preferential rate. Some destinations add product certificates for friction or safety parts — check before the vessel sails, not after.

Who pays for damage between factory and port?

Under FOB, risk passes when the cargo is on board. Damage before that point sits with the supplier, which is exactly why the loading inspection and the container seal photograph matter: they establish the condition at handover.

How far in advance should I book during peak season?

Four weeks is a working minimum for space on a specific sailing, and longer before major holidays. Booking late does not usually cost more per container; it costs a missed sailing, which is more expensive than the rate difference.

Three documents, sent together, remove most of the ambiguity: the completed quotation template, the approved sample record with photographs, and the cut-off calendar with the sailing date you are targeting. Ask for written confirmation of each in the order acknowledgement.

If a supplier cannot complete the template, that is information. It usually means the shipment has never been planned from the port backwards, and the price you were quoted at the fair was built for a conversation rather than a container. Better to learn that in week one than in week six, when the space is gone and the customer is waiting.

title: Canton Fair vs Year-Round Online Sourcing: How Real Buyers Combine Both
description: Is the Canton Fair worth it, or is online sourcing of auto parts from China enough? Compare supplier verification, cost and risk — then combine both with a 12-month hybrid buying calendar for Phase 1 (Oct 15-19, 2026) and the 360 days between fairs.
