content:
Every October, buyers ask the same question: is a trip to the Canton Fair worth it, or can you handle sourcing auto parts from China entirely online? The honest answer is that neither channel wins on its own. The 140th Canton Fair runs its auto-parts-relevant Phase 1 from 15–19 October 2026 at the Pazhou complex in Guangzhou, while the fair’s official website and app operate 365 days a year, 24 hours a day — a pairing that mirrors how the most successful buyers already work. They use the fair to compress supplier evaluation into five intense days, then use online channels for the other 360 days of ordering, reordering and price checking. This guide breaks down what each channel does better, what a trip actually costs versus the risks of buying blind, and how real buyers combine both into one calendar — the working answer for anyone sourcing auto parts from China in 2026.

Is the Canton Fair Worth It for Auto Parts Buyers? The Short Answer

The Canton Fair is worth it for buyers who need to evaluate suppliers face to face, compare physical samples side by side, or negotiate MOQ and pricing terms that decide whether a container order is profitable. It is not worth it for buyers who only need to reorder an SKU they already validated, or who buy a handful of low-value items where shipping a sample costs more than the sample itself. In other words, the question “is the Canton Fair worth it” depends on which half of your auto parts sourcing from China you are asking about — discovery or execution.

For auto parts specifically, Phase 1 is where the value sits. The 15–19 October window covers vehicles, auto parts, new energy vehicles and smart mobility, motorcycles, machinery and hardware — meaning a garage owner or wholesaler from Lagos, Dubai or Almaty can walk through brake, filter, suspension, electrical and lighting suppliers in a single day. Fair statistics from recent sessions show roughly 30,000+ exhibitors across about 1.55 million square meters, so without a plan the fair is overwhelming; with a plan, it is the fastest supplier-evaluation tool that exists.

Where buyers get burned is treating the fair as the whole sourcing model. A trade show hands you contacts, not containers. The orders, the quality checks, the reorders and the price renegotiations happen the rest of the year — online. That is why the question “Canton Fair vs online sourcing” is a false choice. The buyers who win use both, in sequence.

What a Trade Fair Does Better Than Any Screen

Four things happen at a booth that no listing page can replicate:

  • Side-by-side sample comparison. You can hold two brake pads from two factories, weigh them, check the friction material edge, measure backing plate thickness with a caliper, and see the difference in 30 seconds. Online, the same comparison takes weeks of sample shipping and often still ends in guesswork.
  • Real-time price benchmarking. Walking a hall, you can collect five quotations for the same filter in an hour. On a B2B platform, getting five comparable quotes takes days of messaging, and half the replies come from traders, not factories.
  • Instant trust signals. Who answers your technical question — a salesperson reading a script, or an engineer who talks about friction coefficients and mould tolerances? Twenty minutes at a booth tells you more about a supplier than three months of email.
  • Negotiation momentum. Face-to-face, suppliers are more willing to move on MOQ, mixed-container loading and payment terms. Industry observers commonly cite price gaps of roughly 15–30% between face-to-face deals and online-only orders from the same factories — the exact number varies, but the direction does not.

This is also why the fair matters for newer markets. A buyer sourcing auto parts from China for the first time has no history with any factory. The fair is the fastest way to build that history at low cost: you leave Guangzhou with a shortlist of five to eight verified suppliers instead of 500 unverified ones.

What Online Sourcing Does Better Than a Trade Fair

Online channels dominate on three dimensions the fair cannot touch:

  • Range and searchability. A platform search by OE number, engine code or part name reaches thousands of online auto parts suppliers in seconds. At the fair, you only meet whoever booked a booth. Many strong niche factories — a gasket maker running 40 staff, say — never exhibit.
  • Speed and continuity. Reordering a validated SKU is a five-minute job online. The Canton Fair happens twice a year; your customers’ cars break down every day.
  • Cost of discovery. Browsing is free. A sourcing trip costs flights, hotels and a week of your time. For price discovery and range, online wins before you even book a ticket.

The official Canton Fair website and app now blur this line: they run all year with the same exhibitor and product database as the physical halls, including supplier search by category, specification and trade model, plus messaging. Smart buyers treat it as their research layer between editions — which is exactly the hybrid pattern that makes sourcing auto parts from China workable the other 360 days.

Canton Fair vs Alibaba and B2B Platforms: Head-to-Head

Buyers usually frame the debate as “Canton Fair vs Alibaba” — or Made-in-China, or any other B2B marketplace. The table below compares the channels on the decisions that actually move money when you buy auto parts wholesale from China.

Decision factorCanton Fair (Phase 1)B2B online platforms
Supplier identityVerified in person; factory vs trader visible within minutesProfiles self-declared; requires document checks and video audits
Sample evaluationHandle samples on the spot, compare competitors side by sideCourier rounds, 1–3 weeks per cycle, often only one supplier’s sample
Price benchmarking speed5–8 comparable quotes in one dayDays to weeks; quote quality uneven
MOQ and terms flexibilityStronger; face-to-face trust makes suppliers more open to mixed loading and better termsFixed listing MOQs; negotiation slower and shallower
Range of productsLimited to exhibiting companiesNear-unlimited, searchable by OE number
Cost per supplier evaluatedTrip cost spread over 30–50 shortlisted suppliersNear zero, but higher downstream risk
Best used forShortlisting, first orders, annual termsReordering, niche SKUs, continuous price checks

Read the last two rows together and the hybrid logic falls out: the fair is an evaluation event, the platform is an execution channel. Problems start when buyers ask one channel to do the other’s job — placing a first container order purely off a listing page, or flying 9,000 kilometers to reorder an SKU they already know.

The Real Cost Math: Trip Budget vs Risk of Buying Blind

The fair’s upfront cost is visible and often scares buyers off. The online-only risk cost is invisible and much larger when it hits. A realistic comparison:

Cost item7-day Guangzhou sourcing tripOnline-only order without inspection
Flights (round trip)USD 500–1,200 (Middle East/Africa routes)USD 0
Hotel, 7 nights near PazhouUSD 350–900 (fair week pricing)USD 0
Buyer badgeFree (pre-register online)—
Local transport + mealsUSD 150–300—
Time cost~1 weekWeeks of messaging, sampling, disputes
Downside riskLow — you saw the goods before wiringWrong spec, wrong packaging, non-shipment: one mis-shipped 20ft container of mismatched pads can erase a year of margin

A first trip typically lands between USD 1,200 and 2,500 all-in. Spread across the 30–50 suppliers you can realistically evaluate, that is roughly USD 30–80 per verified supplier — less than the cost of a single wrong sample cycle repeated across three suppliers. The math flips decisively once your auto parts sourcing from China passes a few containers a year.

How Real Buyers Combine Both: The 12-Month Hybrid Calendar

The strongest buyers we work with run a rhythm that looks like this:

PeriodActivityChannel
4–6 weeks before Phase 1Build a 30–50 company target list; send OE lists for quotationsOfficial fair site/app, WhatsApp, email
Fair week (15–19 Oct)Meet shortlist, compare samples, negotiate MOQ and FOB, collect golden samplesPazhou halls, in person
48 hours after each hall daySend recap messages, confirm quotations in writing, rank suppliersWhatsApp + email
Weeks after the fairSample validation, first trial order, factory visit during changeover break (20–22 Oct)Online + factory floor
Rest of the yearReorders, new SKU scouting, quarterly price re-checksOnline channels

Notice how the fair is not a sourcing event squeezed into a calendar — it is the annual anchor point that recalibrates every online decision for the next six months. Prices quoted online in November make sense only if you know what the same part cost at the booth in October.

Before Phase 1: Online Research That Makes the Fair Efficient

The fair rewards preparation with brutal efficiency. Buyers who arrive with a target list see 30–50 relevant suppliers in three days; buyers who arrive cold see 300 booths and remember none of them. Your pre-fair online workflow:

  1. Search the official exhibitor database. Filter by product category and specification, and shortlist companies by export market fit — a factory already shipping to your region knows your compliance paperwork.
  2. Send your OE number list in advance. Serious suppliers reply with quotations and confirm they will bring samples to the booth. Silent suppliers just saved you a stop.
  3. Pre-check certifications. Ask for IATF 16949 certificate numbers and issuing bodies before you fly; verify them during the meeting, not after the order.
  4. Set a daily walking route. Pazhou is divided into lettered areas; map your shortlist against hall numbers so your three most important meetings happen on day one, before fatigue sets in.

Done properly, this online layer converts a five-day fair into a five-day confirmation exercise. Done badly, the fair becomes an expensive directory. Either way, the research is the same work that powers efficient Canton Fair auto parts sourcing for the rest of the year — your OE references, your certified-supplier list and your walking route all live on after the halls close.

During the Fair: What to Lock In Face to Face

Use booth time for the four things that are hard to do remotely:

  • Fitment verification. Bring your caliper and your OE reference sheet. Measure the sample, photograph the packaging, record the part number stamped on the product — not just the one on the catalog page.
  • Certificate review. A trustworthy factory shows the certificate and names the issuing body without hesitation. Hesitation is data.
  • Terms negotiation. MOQ, mixed-container loading, payment structure and sample fees all move more easily across a table than through a chat window.
  • Golden sample handover. Agree that the sample you keep becomes the quality reference for the production order, and photograph both parties holding it.

Record a 30-second voice memo at every booth: company name, booth number, what you discussed, what they promised. By day three the halls blur together, and this memo chain becomes your follow-up database.

After the Fair: Moving Booth Contacts into Year-Round Workflows

The fair ends on 19 October; the sourcing does not. The 48-hour window right after each hall day is where most deals are won or quietly lost, because every serious buyer is sending follow-ups and suppliers triage the buyers who confirm fastest. Your sequence:

  1. Recap in writing within 48 hours. Restate part numbers, quantities, FOB prices and agreed terms. A supplier’s written confirmation is your first quality filter.
  2. Run sample validation. Test against the golden sample, not against memory.
  3. Place a structured trial order — small enough to limit risk, large enough to be taken seriously.
  4. Book a factory visit during the changeover break (20–22 October) if the supplier is in Guangdong. Two hours on their production floor settles questions no certificate can.
  5. Move reorders online. Once an SKU is validated, all repeat purchasing should run through your fastest channel, with quarterly price re-checks benchmarked against the fair quote.

This is also the moment where online auto parts suppliers you never met at the fair earn their place: they fill range gaps, cover niche SKUs and keep pricing pressure on your fair contacts. For a garage owner running Canton Fair auto parts sourcing once a year, this online layer is what keeps the shelves stocked between editions.

Where a Guangzhou-Based Partner Fits into the Hybrid Model

One more channel sits between the fair and your laptop: a local exporter who is in Guangzhou year-round. When you buy auto parts wholesale from China through a partner based here, you get fair-season presence without fair-season logistics — someone who can walk Phase 1 with your list, consolidate samples from ten booths into one shipment, supervise pre-shipment inspection, and keep the year-round online reorders moving while you are 9,000 kilometers away. Hybrid sourcing auto parts from China works best when one local team bridges both halves.

Globalucar (Guangzhou Vehicle External Trade) works exactly this way for buyers across the Middle East, Africa and Central Asia. Our Baiyun office is a short drive from the Pazhou complex, so during the 140th session we can meet you between halls, join supplier meetings with your OE list, or attend on your behalf and send side-by-side sample photos the same day. After the fair, the same team handles consolidation, inspection and FOB Guangzhou loading.

Start with the parts finder or check an OE number in our OE parts library.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Canton Fair worth it for small auto parts buyers?

It depends on annual volume and how many new SKUs you need. If you buy one or two containers a year and mostly reorder known parts, online channels plus a local inspection partner usually cover you. If you are building a supplier base, adding product lines, or your orders have grown past USD 50,000 a year, one trip typically pays for itself through better terms and fewer spec mistakes.

Can I source auto parts from China online without ever attending a trade fair?

Yes, thousands of buyers do. The non-negotiables are: verify the supplier’s business license and IATF 16949 certificate, order pre-shipment inspection on every first order, and start with a trial order before any full container. The fair simply compresses this verification into days instead of months.

Canton Fair vs Alibaba — which is better for auto parts?

They do different jobs. Alibaba and similar platforms win on range, speed and reorder convenience; the fair wins on supplier verification, sample comparison and negotiating power. Use the fair to shortlist and set annual terms, use platforms to execute the rest of the year.

How much does it cost to attend Canton Fair Phase 1?

The buyer badge itself is free when pre-registered through the official system. The main costs are travel: from most Middle East and African markets, a 5–7 day trip runs roughly USD 1,200–2,500 including flights, fair-week hotels near Pazhou, local transport and meals.

How do I verify suppliers I meet at the fair once I get home?

Three checks: confirm the company name on the business card matches the export license, ask for the IATF 16949 or ISO certificate number and verify it with the issuing body, and insist on a written quotation with the exact OE references before any deposit. For larger orders, add a third-party or partner-led factory audit.

When should I start contacting suppliers before the fair?

Four to six weeks out is ideal. That leaves time to send your OE list, collect advance quotations, and book meetings so your first hall day targets confirmed appointments instead of browsing. Messages sent two days before opening usually disappear into the pre-fair rush.

Quick Answer: The 2026 Chery Tiggo 7 is China's best-selling export SUV nameplate: a 4.55 m five-seat crossover with 1.5T (108 kW) and 1.6T TGDI (145 kW / 290 N·m) engines plus a Super Hybrid PHEV, FOB Nansha from $11,900. This guide covers the full specification table, the FOB price ladder with container loading, Russia EAC certification, Brazil tariff routing via Caoa Chery, South Africa's 10-year engine warranty market, and landed-cost snapshots for five markets.

Ask any vehicle export desk in Guangzhou which Chinese model moves the most units per square metre of ship deck, and the answer is rarely a flagship. It is the compact SUV — the segment where Chinese engineering meets the price point that Russia, Latin America, Africa and the Middle East actually buy at volume. Within that segment, the Chery Tiggo 7 is the reference product: Chery's longest-running export nameplate, now in its second-generation facelift, and the default comparison point against the Haval Jolion, Changan CS35 Plus and the used-Japanese competition that dominates every emerging market below $20,000.

This guide sets out the 2026 Tiggo 7 export range as we quote it from Nansha: the two petrol powertrains and the Super Hybrid PHEV, indicative FOB pricing by trim, the certification route for Russia and the EAEU, the tariff arithmetic that decides whether Brazil orders ship from China or from Caoa Chery's local assembly, and the warranty structure that has made South Africa Chery's fastest-growing export market. All prices are FOB Nansha for LHD units; RHD is available on order for select trims.

Why the Tiggo 7 Is Chery's Export Volume Engine

Chery has been China's largest passenger-vehicle exporter for over two decades, and the Tiggo 7 sits at the centre of that trade for three reasons. First, it hits the price-performance intersection: a 2,670 mm wheelbase five-seater with a 1.6T direct-injection turbo engine at a price where rivals offer naturally-aspirated 1.5-litres. Second, it is engineered for bad fuel and bad roads from the start — 92 RON tolerance, 196 mm ground clearance and a suspension tune that survives the broken asphalt of Lagos, Almaty and the Russian regions. Third, it has the parts depth: five years of steady export volume means filters, brake components, suspension bushings and body panels are stocked by independent wholesalers across every market the model has entered.

For a distributor, that third point matters more than any spec-sheet line. A model's retail price is set once at launch; its service network decides whether the dealer can sell it for a decade. The Tiggo 7 crossed that threshold in Russia, Kazakhstan, South Africa, Chile and the Gulf years ago, which is why first-time importers keep landing on it as their opening order: the market already knows the car, and the parts channel already exists. Our earlier guides cover the larger siblings — the Tiggo 8 Pro / Tiggo 9 for Russia and Central Asia — and the equivalent Haval products (H6 and H9 export guide).

Tiggo 7 2026: Engines, Trims and Equipment

The 2026 export range runs three powertrains. The 1.5T is the fleet and price-entry unit — 108 kW and 210 N·m through a 7-speed wet dual-clutch, tuned for 92 RON fuel and cheap servicing. The 1.6T TGDI is the volume retail engine: 145 kW and 290 N·m, 0-100 km/h in 8.3 seconds, with a multi-link rear suspension and 19-inch wheels on upper trims. The Super Hybrid PHEV pairs a 1.5-litre hybrid engine with dual electric motors and an 18.4 kWh CATL lithium-iron-phosphate battery — 150 kW system output, roughly 90 km of electric range and a combined range beyond 1,100 km, which positions it for markets where fuel cost, not infrastructure, is the constraint.

Equipment is where the Tiggo 7 wins its comparison tests: dual 12.3-inch screens, wireless CarPlay and Android Auto, a 540-degree camera, heated and ventilated front seats on upper trims, and a full Level 2 ADAS suite (AEB, adaptive cruise, lane centring, blind-spot monitoring) that arrives as standard on the 1.6T Prestige and above. The model carries a five-star Euro NCAP rating with six to eight airbags depending on trim. Russia-spec units add an engine block heater and cold-climate battery calibration; Gulf-spec units carry upgraded air conditioning for 50°C ambient operation. Read the torque row against the fuel row: the 1.6T's 290 N·m arrives at 2,000 rpm and runs on 92 RON, which is the combination that matters from Yekaterinburg to Ibadan. The PHEV's 90 km electric range covers a typical city delivery cycle on overnight charging from a domestic socket, without demanding public infrastructure that most target markets do not yet have.

FOB Nansha Price List and Order Tiers

The 2026 Tiggo 7 export price ladder is set out below. These are indicative FOB Nansha figures for LHD units at container tier; volume, trim mix and market-spec calibration move the final quotation, and the PHEV carries homologation surcharges in markets that classify it separately for duty purposes.

VariantFOB Nansha (USD)DriveUnits per 40HC

Container loading follows the same wheel-frame rack method as other compact Chinese SUVs: four units per 40-foot high-cube is standard. Above eight units per sailing, RORO beats container economics — Nansha runs direct car-carrier services to Vladivostok (7-12 days), Novorossiysk via transshipment (30-40 days), Santos and Buenos Aires (35-42 days), Durban (25-30 days) and Jebel Ali (18-22 days). Chile and Peru clear Chinese-built vehicles at zero or near-zero duty under the China-Chile and China-Peru FTAs, which is why the Tiggo 7 retails in Santiago at prices that compete with Brazilian-assembly rivals. The 1.5T fleet trim at $11,900 is the number tender buyers compare against used 2018-2020 Japanese crossovers — and where a seven-year-old import cannot match a new-vehicle warranty.

Russia and the EAEU: Certification and the Parallel-Import Reality

Russia remains the Tiggo 7's largest single export market, and the model has been a fixture in the country's top-ten SUV charts since 2023. Imports clear under the EAC framework (TR CU 018/2011) with SBKTS per-unit approval for commercial lots; the practical cost items are the utilization fee — raised again for 2025-2026 — plus recycling-deposit mechanics and the GLONASS-era ERA-GLONASS emergency system requirement, which is now handled at the port-of-entry fitting stage. Our Russia GOST/EAC certification guide walks through the full document chain for first-time importers.

Pre-shipment inspection and export documentation workflow for China-built SUV export orders.

Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia share the same EAC framework, and the Khorgos rail route (18-22 days from Guangzhou) has made Almaty the stocking hub for Central Asian distribution. Uzbekistan's staged import-duty reductions since 2023 have opened a market where the Tiggo 7's 92 RON tolerance and parts availability through Chery's Tashkent dealer network give it a service advantage over less-established Chinese entrants.

Brazil and Latin America: The Tariff Decision

Brazil is the market where sourcing strategy matters most for the Tiggo 7. Fully-built imports from China face a 35% import duty plus IPI and ICMS stacking, which prices direct container shipments out of retail contention. Caoa Chery, Chery's Brazilian partner, assembles the Tiggo 7 family locally at its Jaguarina plant in São Paulo state — so Brazilian orders are quoted through the local-assembly channel, while the China trade serves Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia from port stock. Chile is the opposite case: zero duty under the China-Chile FTA makes it the most price-transparent Tiggo 7 market in Latin America and the reference point for regional price benchmarking. Mexico applies zero duty to Chinese-built vehicles under its own framework but taxes by value; Peruvian and Ecuadorian distributors order steadily at container tier. For a Latin American entrant, the practical question is not whether to stock the Tiggo 7 but which trim — the 1.6T Prestige carries the equipment list that wins comparison shopping in Santiago and Lima, while the 1.5T fleet trim serves ride-hailing and corporate orders.

South Africa and Africa: Warranty Depth as a Sales Weapon

South Africa has become the Tiggo 7's showcase market because Chery South Africa markets a 5-year/150,000 km vehicle warranty backed by a 10-year/1,000,000 km engine warranty for first owners — the longest powertrain cover in the segment, and the single strongest counter to the used-Japanese default. Nigerian, Ghanaian and Kenyan importers order the 1.5T for urban retail where the 92 RON tolerance and simple turbo hardware keep field repairs cheap; the 1.6T serves buyers stepping up from a first car. Two spec decisions matter on African orders: confirm the full-size spare (standard on Prestige trims, optional on fleet) and specify underbody coating for coastal markets. Parts support runs through the same Kingmay-serviced channel as other Chinese brands — a front-end parts set for the Tiggo 7 costs roughly 40% of the equivalent Toyota RAV4 package, which is the number fleet operators in Lagos and Nairobi actually calculate on.

Tiggo 7 vs the Competition

The compact Chinese SUV export trade has three reference products. The comparison below sets the Tiggo 7 against its two most-quoted rivals at FOB tier.

The Jolion wins the wheelbase row and price; the Tiggo 7 wins power, torque and — outside South Africa's GWM dealer footprint — the parts-depth argument. The decision typically resolves by market: where GWM's dealer network is denser, the Jolion retails faster; everywhere else, the Tiggo 7's engine output at the same price bracket carries the comparison-test headlines that drive showroom traffic.

Landed Cost Snapshots for Five Markets

Landed cost decides which trim wins each order. The two most-quoted builds are set out below with indicative duty, freight and tax components — planning estimates, not quotations.

Tiggo 7 1.5T (FOB $11,900) — fleet build:

  • Chile (San Antonio): 0% duty under China-Chile FTA + RORO freight ~$2,300 + 19% VAT on CIF → landed ≈ $16,900
  • Russia (Vladivostok): EAEU duty 15% + VAT 20% + utilization fee + RORO freight ~$1,400 → landed ≈ $19,800
  • South Africa (Durban): 18% duty + ad valorem + 15% VAT + freight ~$1,900 → landed ≈ $19,300

Tiggo 7 1.6T Prestige (FOB $14,300) — retail build:

  • UAE (Jebel Ali): 5% duty $715 + freight ~$1,700 + 5% VAT on CIF → landed ≈ $17,700
  • Kazakhstan (rail via Khorgos): EAEU duty 15% + rail freight ~$2,400 + VAT → landed ≈ $21,200

Two notes. Chile's zero duty is why its retail price is the regional benchmark — the landed figure is almost pure FOB plus logistics, making Santiago the cleanest comparison market for trim pricing. Russia's utilization fee now adds more than the duty itself on sub-2.0-litre petrol units, which has pushed the Russian order book toward higher trims where the fixed fee amortizes better against equipment value.

Ordering Process, Lead Time and Mixed Loading

A first Tiggo 7 order through our desk follows six steps: trim and market-spec confirmation against your country's homologation rules, proforma invoice with FOB or CIF terms, 30% deposit, production slot booking (3-4 weeks if the trim is not in port stock), pre-shipment inspection with photo report, and balance against shipping documents. In-stock units at Nansha ship within 10 days of deposit. Mixed loading keeps first orders low-risk: a typical trial container pairs two or three Tiggo 7 units with a parts package — filters, brake pad sets, suspension bushings, LED lighting — sized to six months of service demand, so the dealer opens with both sales stock and workshop stock in one clearance. The products catalogue lists current fast-moving Chery parts alongside our wider Chinese-brand coverage, and the OE lookup tool cross-references part numbers before you commit the parts line of the order.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the 2026 Chery Tiggo 7 export price from China?

The range runs $11,900 for the 1.5T fleet trim, $12,600 for the 1.5T Prime, $14,300 for the 1.6T Prestige, $15,400 for the 1.6T AWD and $18,900 for the Super Hybrid PHEV — all FOB Nansha at container tier. Volume discounts of 2-4% apply above ten units, and four units fit a single 40-foot high-cube container.

Is the Tiggo 7 available with all-wheel drive?

Yes, on the 1.6T powertrain for select export markets at $15,400 FOB — roughly $1,100 over the equivalent FWD trim. Most volume markets order FWD, since the 196 mm ground clearance and 92 RON tolerance cover the majority of use cases; AWD matters mainly in Central Asia's winter regions and Andean Latin America.

Can the Tiggo 7 be imported into Russia in 2026?

Yes. Clearance runs under the EAC framework (TR CU 018/2011) with SBKTS per-unit approval for commercial lots, plus the utilization fee and ERA-GLONASS fitting. The Tiggo 7 has been among Russia's best-selling Chinese SUVs since 2023, so parts supply and dealer familiarity are established — the practical planning item is the utilization fee, which now exceeds the customs duty on sub-2.0-litre petrol units.

How does the Tiggo 7 compare with the Haval Jolion for import?

The Jolion offers a 30 mm longer wheelbase and a marginally lower FOB at equivalent trim; the Tiggo 7 counters with 35 kW more power and 70 N·m more torque from its 1.6T, standard Level 2 ADAS on the Prestige, and deeper independent parts availability across more export markets. Where GWM's dealer network is denser (Russia, South Africa), the Jolion retails faster; elsewhere the Tiggo 7's power-per-dollar wins the comparison tests.

What is the Super Hybrid PHEV's electric range?

Roughly 90 km of pure-electric range from an 18.4 kWh CATL lithium-iron-phosphate battery, with a combined range beyond 1,100 km once the 1.5-litre hybrid engine engages. It charges from a domestic socket overnight, so it suits markets where fuel cost rather than charging infrastructure is the constraint — and where duty regimes treat PHEVs favourably against pure petrol.

What warranty does the Tiggo 7 carry on export markets?

Five years or 150,000 km on the vehicle for most export markets. In South Africa, Chery backs the engine with a 10-year/1,000,000 km first-owner warranty — the segment's longest powertrain cover and the strongest retail argument against used-Japanese competition. Fleet buyers elsewhere should negotiate warranty terms into the supply agreement, as regional structures vary.

title: Guangzhou Travel Guide for Canton Fair Week: Hotels, Metro, Payments & SIM Cards
description: A practical Guangzhou travel guide for Canton Fair week: where to stay near Pazhou, how to reach the venue by metro, using Alipay and WeChat Pay, choosing a SIM card or eSIM and a VPN, what to pack, and how to plan a full day at the halls.

content:
A sourcing trip to the Canton Fair is decided as much by logistics as by the halls. Where you sleep, how you reach Pazhou, whether your phone has data and whether you can pay for a taxi at midnight all shape how many suppliers you actually meet. With the 140th session’s Phase 1 running 15–19 October 2026, this Guangzhou travel guide covers the practical layer first-time and returning buyers ask about most — hotels near the Canton Fair, the metro, mobile payments, SIM cards and eSIM, what to pack and how to structure a day at the venue. Get these right and the fair stops being an endurance test and starts being the fastest week of supplier work in your calendar.

Guangzhou for Canton Fair Week: What to Plan First

Four decisions determine how smooth your week goes, and all four are best made before you fly: your hotel area, your metro route, your payment setup and your mobile data. Everything else — food, packing, daily timing — is easier to improvise once those four are locked. The venue is the China Import and Export Fair Complex in the Pazhou area of Haizhu District, and the whole city bends around it during the fair: metro trains run fuller, hotel rates climb, and the roads around the complex slow to a crawl at peak times.

The single most useful habit is to treat the trip as a business week with a travel layer on top. Map your target supplier halls first, then choose a hotel and route that get you to those halls with the least friction. Buyers who book a hotel at a good price but thirty minutes from the wrong entrance spend their week compensating for that choice.

One planning note for Phase 1 specifically: the 15–19 October window covers vehicles, auto parts, new energy vehicles, machinery and hardware. If your sourcing is auto parts and vehicles, this is your phase — there is no need to attend the later phases unless you also buy home goods or textiles.

Getting There: Flights, Airport and the Metro to Pazhou

Most international buyers arrive at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (CAN). From the airport, the metro is the lowest-cost reliable route to the fair area: take Line 3 and transfer to Line 8 for Pazhou. The journey runs roughly 50 minutes and costs around CNY 10. Taxis and ride-hailing work, but during fair week traffic near the complex is heavy, so build in extra time and set your destination to the correct gate for your exhibition area.

The metro itself drops you at the door of the fair, which is why it is the default choice for buyers staying anywhere on the network.

Canton Fair areaMetro station and exitNotes
Area A / DLine 8 → Xingangdong Station, Exit ADirect walk into the halls
Area BLine 8 → Pazhou Station, Exits A / BAlso connects to Line 11
Area CLine 8 → Pazhou Station, Exit CShort walk from the station
Airport arrivalLine 3 → transfer Line 8 → Pazhou~50 minutes, ~CNY 10

Check your area before choosing a station exit — the complex is very large and the areas are internally connected, but walking between halls still takes time. During the fair, allow extra minutes for security checks and queues, and check live crowd levels on a map app before setting off.

Where to Stay: Pazhou, Tianhe and What Fair-Week Rooms Cost

Hotels near Pazhou sell out early and fair-period rates commonly run two to three times their normal price. Book two months or more ahead, or accept whatever remains. The trade-off is always the same: distance buys price.

AreaProsConsTypical fit
Pazhou / Haizhu (walking distance)Walk or short ride to the halls; some hotels connect by skybridgeHighest fair-week rates; books out firstBuyers with back-to-back meetings
TianheMore choice and lower cost; ~30 min by metroDaily commute in and outBuyers balancing fair and city time
Yuexiu / centralBudget-friendly; good metro links; central for diningLonger commute to PazhouLonger stays and first-time visitors

Within Pazhou, hotels range from international brands next to the complex to mid-range and economy options one or two metro stops away. A room within walking distance of Area C, or a hotel with a direct bridge to Areas A, B and C, removes the daily commute almost entirely. Mid-range rooms near Pazhou metro commonly sit in the CNY 550–900 range around fair week, with premium properties well above that. To judge any listing, check two things: the walking distance to the specific area you will visit most, and whether the hotel offers on-site badge printing or a shuttle.

Getting Around: Metro, Taxi, DiDi and the Tram

The metro is the workhorse of fair week: it is fast, cheap, air-conditioned and immune to the traffic that clogs the roads around the complex. Line 8 serves Xingangdong and Pazhou, and Pazhou also connects to Line 11, which eases pressure during peak periods. Buy or top up a metro card or use your phone, and keep your badge handy so you can move between halls and stations quickly.

Taxis and ride-hailing (DiDi) are useful when you carry luggage or travel outside peak hours, but near the fair they face the same congestion as everyone else. For drop-offs, set your destination to the gate for your area and follow staff directions to designated pick-up and drop-off points. Local buses and the Haizhu tram add connections between the venue and nearby districts. The rule that saves the most time: check your area and entrance before you leave the hotel, and plan your day around one or two areas rather than trying to cross the whole complex twice.

Payments in China: Alipay, WeChat Pay, Cards and Cash

China runs on mobile payments, and the good news for visitors is that both major wallets now support international cards. Link your card to Alipay and to WeChat Pay before you arrive, because the moment you want to hail a ride, buy a metro ticket or pay a small vendor, the phone is the fastest option. International cards work at major hotels and larger merchants but less reliably at small shops, stalls and taxis, so do not rely on plastic alone.

MethodWhere it worksSetup
Alipay (linked to international card)Widely accepted, including small vendorsLink your card and verify your passport before arrival
WeChat PayWidely accepted; also your main supplier messaging toolSet up a WeChat account and link a card
International credit cardMajor hotels and larger merchantsCarry as backup; acceptance is uneven elsewhere
Cash (CNY)Universal fallbackKeep roughly CNY 500–1,000 in small notes

Set up both wallets and add a cash buffer. The goal is to never be the buyer stuck at a counter with a card that the terminal will not read while a supplier waits.

Staying Connected: SIM Cards, eSIM, VPN and WeChat

Connectivity is where first-time visitors lose the most time, so decide your route before departure. You have three practical options, and they differ not only in price but in which internet you can reach.

OptionWhat you getBest for
Physical Chinese SIM (China Mobile / Unicom / Telecom)A +86 number; passport registration and facial verification required at the counterBuyers who want a local number and app registrations
Travel eSIM (routed outside the mainland)Data without a +86 number; international apps reachable without extra setupShort-stay buyers who want the fastest setup
International roamingYour home number and data via roaming agreementsVery short trips; usually the priciest option

The nuance that matters: a mainland SIM or mainland eSIM sits behind China’s internet filtering, so services such as Google and WhatsApp will not load without a VPN. A travel eSIM whose traffic is routed outside the mainland, or international roaming, generally reaches those services without extra configuration. Many experienced buyers run both — a physical Chinese SIM in one slot for the +86 number, and a data eSIM for open access. Install WeChat and Alipay before you land, set up your VPN before you fly (it is harder to obtain once you are inside), and save your hotel address in Chinese offline.

Airport telecom counters in the arrivals area can sell and activate a physical SIM with passport registration in around ten minutes, and tourist packages commonly run from roughly CNY 120–300 for 15–30 days with generous data. If your phone supports eSIM and you want to skip the queue, a travel eSIM installed before departure is often the smoother path.

What to Pack and What to Wear for a Full Day of Walking

The complex is vast, and a serious buyer walks 8–15 kilometres a day between halls. Pack for that reality:

  • Comfortable shoes. This is the most important item. Wear the most comfortable pair you own and bring a second pair to rotate.
  • A business card stack. Physical cards remain standard with Chinese suppliers — bring 200 or more, and add a WeChat QR code to speed follow-up.
  • A lightweight bag or small trolley. Samples, catalogues and business cards add up fast; a wheeled trolley helps with larger sample collections.
  • A portable charger and a refillable water bottle. Full days on the phone and on your feet drain both.
  • A caliper and your OE list. The two tools that turn a booth visit from browsing into verification.

Guangzhou in October is warm and can be humid, with occasional rain, so light breathable clothing and a compact umbrella cover most days. Dress smart-casual: comfortable enough for a full day of walking, presentable enough for a supplier meeting.

Food, Water and Energy: Eating Around the Fair

On-site restaurants in the areas around the complex serve Cantonese and international food, but queues between 12:00 and 13:00 can run long. Shift your lunch to about 11:30 or 13:30 and you reclaim half an hour of hall time. Keep hydrated through the day — the air conditioning, the walking and the talking add up — and carry a snack so a missed lunch does not cost you the afternoon.

Outside the venue, Guangzhou rewards a short detour for dinner: the city is famous for Cantonese cuisine, and a proper meal away from the complex is a good way to debrief with a colleague or treat a supplier contact. Because many smaller restaurants run on mobile payment, the Alipay and WeChat Pay setup in section five earns its keep at dinner as much as at the fair.

A Practical Day Plan for Phase 1 at Pazhou

A workable rhythm for a fair day:

  1. 07:30 — breakfast and check. Confirm your badge, your target halls and your metro station for the day.
  2. 09:00 — arrive early. Doors open around 09:30; arriving before the crowd means your first meetings start on time.
  3. 09:30–12:00 — deep meetings. Spend the morning on your top-priority suppliers while you are freshest.
  4. 11:30 or 13:30 — lunch. Eat off-peak to avoid the queue.
  5. 13:30–17:00 — second sweep. Work the next area on your list, collecting samples and quotations.
  6. 17:00–18:00 — wrap and record. Voice-memo each booth and log contacts while the day is fresh.
  7. Evening — follow-up. Send recap messages and rank suppliers before you sleep; the first 48 hours decide who takes you seriously.

The plan is deliberately front-loaded: your most important meetings happen before fatigue sets in, and your notes happen before memory blurs. If you are attending on behalf of a colleague or client, this is also the structure we follow when walking the halls for buyers — our daytime with your OE list, your evening follow-up the same day.

Budget and Safety Tips for First-Time Visitors

A first trip generally lands somewhere between USD 1,200 and 2,500 all-in: flights, fair-week hotel, local transport and meals, with the buyer badge free when pre-registered through the official system. The variable that moves the number most is hotel timing — book early and the same trip costs markedly less.

On safety and small practicalities: keep your passport and a photo of it stored separately, use hotel safes for documents, and keep small notes on hand for the places that will not take a card. Carry the address of your hotel in Chinese so a taxi driver can read it. Keep your badge visible in and around the complex. And pace yourself — a fair week is a marathon, and the buyers who schedule recovery time in the evening still have energy for their best meetings on day four and five.

Coming to Phase 1 (15–19 October 2026)? Send your OE number list and target part categories before you fly — we are based in Guangzhou, a short drive from Pazhou, and can prepare a walking plan, join your supplier meetings, or meet you between halls for sample review. Contact Mr Didi: ucars@global-ucars.com  |  WhatsApp +86 133 0240 8528  |  or reach us via our contact page. Planning what to verify once you arrive? Read how to verify auto parts suppliers at the fair, or check an OE number in our OE parts library.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where should I stay for the Canton Fair?

Pazhou and Haizhu are closest, letting you walk or take a short ride to the halls — ideal if you have back-to-back meetings. Tianhe offers more choice at lower cost, about 30 minutes away by metro, and Yuexiu is a budget-friendly option with good metro links. Fair-period rates run two to three times normal, so book two months or more ahead.

How do I get to the Canton Fair by metro?

Line 8 serves the venue: Xingangdong Station, Exit A for Areas A and D, and Pazhou Station, Exits A or B for Area B and Exit C for Area C. Pazhou also connects to Line 11 to ease peak crowding. From Baiyun Airport, take Line 3 and transfer to Line 8; the journey runs about 50 minutes for roughly CNY 10.

Can I use Alipay and WeChat Pay as a foreign visitor in China?

Yes. Both wallets support international cards for foreign visitors. Link your card and verify your passport before you arrive. They are the fastest way to pay for metro rides, taxis, restaurants and small vendors. International cards work at major hotels and larger merchants but less reliably at small shops and taxis, so carry a cash buffer of roughly CNY 500–1,000 as backup.

Do I need a VPN or a Chinese SIM card for the Canton Fair?

It depends on which internet you need. A mainland SIM or mainland eSIM gives you a +86 number but sits behind China’s internet filtering, so services like Google and WhatsApp need a VPN. A travel eSIM routed outside the mainland, or international roaming, generally reaches those services without extra setup. Many buyers run both and set up their VPN before departure.

How much should I budget for a Canton Fair trip?

A first trip typically lands between USD 1,200 and 2,500 all-in, covering flights, fair-week hotel, local transport and meals. The buyer badge is free when pre-registered through the official system. The biggest variable is hotel timing — booking early can cut the total noticeably, since fair-week rooms run two to three times normal rates.

What should I bring to the Canton Fair?

Comfortable walking shoes above all — you may walk 8–15 kilometres a day. Bring 200 or more business cards with a WeChat QR code, a lightweight bag or small trolley for samples, a portable charger, a refillable water bottle, a caliper, and your OE number list. Keep your passport, badge and a photo of your passport stored separately for security.

content:
Short answer: Overseas buyers register free through the official Canton Fair Buyer Service System, upload passport and company details, apply for the overseas buyer badge, and download the invitation letter from the same portal. The badge gets you into the Pazhou halls; the invitation letter supports a China business (M) visa if your passport needs one. Nationals from about 50 countries can enter visa-free for 30 days until 31 December 2026, but they still need the buyer badge.

1. Who Needs to Register for Canton Fair?

Every overseas visitor who wants to walk the exhibition halls during the 140th Canton Fair needs a buyer badge. The rule applies to first-time buyers and returning buyers alike. Pre-registration is now mandatory for all offline attendees, according to the Ministry of Commerce announcement for the spring session. Once approved, the badge is usually valid for the entire session and can remain valid for future fairs, so returning buyers should keep the physical card safe.

Registration is free when done through the official buyer portal. Third-party agents who charge for a "VIP badge" or "fast-track invitation" are selling something the fair itself gives away. The only official route is the Buyer Service System, and the only costs you should expect are the visa fee at your local Chinese consulate and the 100 RMB on-site service fee if you decide to register at the venue instead of pre-registering.

2. What the Buyer Badge Actually Grants You

The badge is more than entry paper. It carries your name, nationality, company and a QR code that exhibitors scan when they want to record your details. That scan becomes the first record in your post-fair follow-up. Without it, you cannot enter the Canton Fair Complex during Phase 1 (October 15–19), Phase 2 (October 23–27) or Phase 3 (October 31 – November 4).

Beyond hall entry, pre-registered buyers receive fair updates by email, can book badge collection slots at airport and hotel counters, and are eligible for small souvenirs at the registration desks. The practical value is time: pre-registered buyers skip the longest lines at the Pazhou complex on opening morning.

Buyer badge benefits at the 140th Canton Fair
BenefitPre-registered buyerOn-site registered buyer
Hall entry during all phasesYesYes
First badge feeFreeApprox. 100 RMB
Airport / hotel collectionYesNo
Email updates before the fairYesNo
Express lanes at PazhouUsually availableStandard queue

The table shows why pre-registration is the better route for any buyer flying in from the Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia or Latin America. A 30-minute online application saves hours on the ground.

3. Step-by-Step: Canton Fair Buyer Registration

The current registration flow runs through the Canton Fair Buyer Service System. The interface has been consolidated there, so if you see an older invitation-only portal that shows limited functions, switch to the main buyer address. The system asks for the same documents whether you are a garage owner, auto parts distributor or fleet buyer.

  1. Create a buyer account. Use a working email and set a password. The account stays active for future fairs.
  2. Fill in personal details. Upload a passport copy and a passport-style photo. The photo must have a plain background; casual photos are often rejected.
  3. Add company information. Enter your registered business name, address and trade role. This name should match your business card and visa application.
  4. Select attendance intent. Choose the 140th session, your product interests and the phases you plan to attend.
  5. Apply for the overseas buyer badge. Tick the option to generate the invitation letter at the same time.
  6. Download the invitation letter. Once approved, print it for your visa appointment and keep a PDF on your phone.
Required documents for Canton Fair buyer registration

Email and mobile contactRequiredConfirm existing details

Processing times vary, but most buyers receive badge approval within a few business days. Apply at least three weeks before travel to leave time for visa processing and flight booking.

4. Invitation Letter vs. Visa: Do You Need Both?

The invitation letter and the visa are two separate things. The invitation letter proves to the Chinese consulate that you have a commercial reason to visit. The visa is the sticker or stamp that lets you enter China. Whether you need a visa depends on your passport, not on the invitation letter.

About 50 nationalities currently enjoy 30-day visa-free entry to China for business or tourism until the end of 2026. Buyers from those countries do not need an M visa, but they still need the Canton Fair buyer badge to enter the halls. The invitation letter can still be useful as supporting documentation at immigration, but it is not mandatory for visa-free travelers.

Visa pathways for Canton Fair buyers by passport group
Passport groupVisa requirementInvitation letter role
Visa-free countries (UK, EU, Australia, Japan, Korea, etc.)30 days visa-free until 31 Dec 2026Optional supporting document
240-hour transit eligible countriesTransit without visa if flying to a third country/regionHelps explain purpose at border
Countries requiring a visa (USA and others)Apply for M business visaRequired supporting document

Always check the latest policy before booking, because visa rules can change with little notice. The safest approach is to register for the badge and invitation letter first, then decide on the visa route based on your nationality.

5. China Business Visa (M Visa) Checklist

If your passport requires a visa, the M visa is the standard category for commercial activity, including trade fairs. The Canton Fair invitation letter satisfies the invitation-document requirement. Your local Chinese embassy or Visa Application Service Centre decides the final validity, number of entries and stay length.

The most common mistake is mismatching passport numbers. If you apply for the invitation letter in August and renew your passport in September, the numbers will not match the visa application. Re-download the invitation letter after any passport change. Another common error is applying at the wrong mission: the country where you legally reside, not the country of your passport, usually handles the application.

Processing normally takes 4 to 7 working days, with expedited options in major cities. Apply at least one month before the fair to avoid last-minute stress.

6. Where to Collect Your Badge in Guangzhou

Pre-registered buyers can collect the badge before reaching the Pazhou complex. Collection points for the 140th session include Baiyun International Airport, Guangzhou South railway station, the Pazhou Hong Kong and Macao passenger terminal, selected hotels and the fair's Hong Kong office. On-site collection at Pazhou is also available but usually slower.

Bring your original passport and a printed copy of the invitation letter or badge confirmation. Some counters accept the QR code from the official app, but a paper backup removes any language-barrier friction. Airport counters are often the fastest because staff there are used to handling international arrivals.

Canton Fair badge collection points for overseas buyers

Pazhou Complex registration hallLast-minute or on-site registrantsPassport, photo, 100 RMB fee

If your hotel is near Metro Line 8 or Line 11, plan to collect the badge on arrival day and visit the fair fresh the next morning. The metro stations Xingangdong and Pazhou both serve the complex.

7. Visa-Free Entry and the 240-Hour Transit Option

For buyers from visa-free countries, the process is simpler but not automatic. You still need a return ticket, a hotel booking and a clear reason for entry. Carrying the Canton Fair invitation letter, badge confirmation and a short list of suppliers to visit makes the immigration conversation faster.

The 240-hour visa-free transit rule lets eligible travelers pass through China for up to ten days if they are continuing to a third country or region. Hong Kong is about one hour from Guangzhou by high-speed rail, so a routing such as London–Guangzhou–Hong Kong–London can fit the transit rule. This route does not require an M visa, but you must hold confirmed onward tickets and stay within the permitted transit area. Rules can change, so verify the current list of eligible ports and nationalities before relying on this option.

8. Common Registration Mistakes to Avoid

Small errors in the registration phase can cost a buyer the first day of the fair. The registration system is automated, so mismatched data is rejected or delayed without human explanation.

  • Using a trading name instead of the registered company name. The badge name and visa documents should match your business card and company registration.
  • Uploading a low-quality photo. The system compares the image to passport standards. A dark, cropped or filtered photo usually fails.
  • Waiting until arrival to register. On-site queues are longest on October 15. Pre-register and collect the badge at the airport.
  • Ignoring passport expiry. Many countries require six months of validity beyond your planned return date. Check early.
  • Applying at the wrong visa centre. Use the mission that serves your country of legal residence, not necessarily your nationality.

9. How Globalucar Helps During Canton Fair Week

Globalucar is a Guangzhou-based vehicle and auto parts export company. We are not an official Canton Fair exhibitor, but our warehouse and office sit close to the Pazhou complex and Nansha Port. During Phase 1 we help overseas buyers with three practical services.

First, we offer same-day sample viewing for Korean, Japanese and Chinese auto parts that buyers shortlist at the fair. Second, we arrange warehouse visits so buyers can check packing standards, labeling and MOQ before placing an order. Third, we provide FOB Guangzhou and FOB Nansha quotations, container loading plans and documentation support for orders placed during or after the fair.

Our team speaks English and is reachable on WhatsApp at +86 133 0240 8528. If you are in Guangzhou during Canton Fair week, you can also book a meeting at our Baiyun office. The office is a short drive from the Pazhou complex, which makes it easy to combine fair visits with product inspections.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How do I register for Canton Fair as an overseas buyer?

Register free on the official Canton Fair Buyer Service System. Create an account, upload your passport and a passport-style photo, enter your company details, apply for the overseas buyer badge, and generate the invitation letter from the same portal.

Is the Canton Fair invitation letter free?

Yes. The official invitation letter is free for approved overseas buyers when generated through the Buyer Service System. You do not need to pay an agency for it.

Do I need a visa if I have a Canton Fair buyer badge?

The badge gets you into the fair, but it does not replace a visa. Nationals of visa-free countries can enter without a visa until 31 December 2026; others need an M business visa supported by the invitation letter.

Can I register for Canton Fair on the day of the fair?

On-site registration is possible but not recommended. It costs about 100 RMB, requires a paper photo, and involves longer queues than pre-registration.

How long does Canton Fair buyer registration take?

Most buyers receive badge approval within a few business days. Allow at least three weeks before travel so you have time for visa processing and flight booking.

Where can I pick up my Canton Fair badge in Guangzhou?

Pre-registered buyers can collect badges at Baiyun Airport, Guangzhou South railway station, the Pazhou Hong Kong and Macao terminal, selected hotels and the fair's Hong Kong office. Bring your original passport and badge confirmation.

Quick Answer: Cooling, ignition and engine accessory parts for the Hyundai Elantra 1.5L CVT, Sonata 1.5T Turbo, Kia K5 1.5T Turbo and Kia Sportage 1.5L Turbo family wholesale FOB Guangzhou from USD 4-12 per cabin filter, USD 28-95 per radiator assembly, and USD 18-65 per ignition coil. This guide maps the shared 1.5T/1.5L/NU2.0 powertrain across the four vehicles, walks through six high-turnover parts systems, gives an indicative FOB Guangzhou price ladder by tier, and covers the container loading and OE cross-reference arithmetic a parts distributor needs to build a Hyundai/Kia programme.

The 2026 Hyundai and Kia export programme from China and Korea moves four passenger cars that share more under the skin than the showroom placards suggest: the Hyundai Elantra (1.5L MPI naturally-aspirated), the Hyundai Sonata (1.5T Turbo), the Kia K5 (1.5T Turbo) and the Kia Sportage (1.5L Turbo). All four carry variants of the Smartstream 1.5T / 1.5L / Nu 2.0L powertrain family, all four share Hyundai-Kia's Theta II / Nu engine architecture, and all four share the same generation of cooling, ignition and engine accessory parts with only body-specific changes.

This guide is written for parts distributors, fleet suppliers and workshop chains sourcing Hyundai and Kia parts from China. It covers the shared powertrain map, the six high-turnover parts systems (cooling, ignition, engine accessories, sensors, filters, suspension top mounts), the OE number map across the family, FOB Guangzhou pricing by tier, IATF 16949 certification, and container loading arithmetic. For the vehicle-side export programme, see our Elantra 2026 export guide.

01 Why the Hyundai/Kia Family Anchors a Parts Wholesale Programme

The Hyundai-Kia passenger car family is the second-largest in the global aftermarket behind Toyota, and within the export trade it has three structural advantages that keep it anchored in a wholesale parts programme. First, parts commonality: a single OE reference often covers two or three of the four vehicles in this guide, which means a distributor can build a small stock keeping unit (SKU) list and cover a disproportionate share of the channel. Second, the parts are physically accessible: cooling, ignition and engine accessory parts sit in the category band where independent workshops and even owner-mechanics can perform the replacement. Third, the price point: Hyundai and Kia parts typically retail at 60-80% of the equivalent Toyota or Honda reference, which keeps the volume flowing through independent channels.

The 2026 programme specifically strengthens the commonality argument. Hyundai-Kia has converged its 1.5L naturally-aspirated, 1.5L turbo and 2.0L Nu engine architecture onto shared subsystems — cooling hose routing, ignition coil architecture, sensor connector types, filter housing dimensions — across the Elantra, Sonata, K5 and Sportage platforms. A distributor quoting the family can lean on a small common-OE set for the high-turnover items and only needs to maintain body-specific SKUs for trim and accident-repair work.

The other reason this family anchors a programme is the destination market map. Hyundai and Kia stock moves at volume into Russia and Central Asia, the Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia, and Latin America — a corridor wide enough that no single market downturn disturbs the order book. For a Guangzhou-based parts wholesaler, that breadth of demand is what makes a Hyundai/Kia family programme a permanent fixture rather than a market-dependent trade.

02 The 2026 Hyundai/Kia Family Powertrain Map

The four vehicles covered in this guide share more of their powertrain than the model names suggest. The Elantra carries the 1.5L Smartstream naturally-aspirated MPI engine (roughly 115 hp) paired with a CVT. The Sonata carries the 1.5T Turbo-GDi engine (roughly 180 hp) paired with an 8-speed automatic. The K5 carries the same 1.5T Turbo-GDi (the K5 is mechanically close to the Sonata) paired with an 8-speed automatic. The Sportage carries the 1.5L Turbo-GDi engine (roughly 180 hp) paired with a 7-speed DCT.

VehicleEnginePowerTransmissionGeneration
Hyundai Elantra 2023 (still in export catalogue)1.5L MPI NA115 hp / 144 N·mCVTCN7
Hyundai Sonata 20261.5T Turbo-GDi180 hp / 253 N·m8-speed automaticDN8
Kia K5 20261.5T Turbo-GDi180 hp / 253 N·m8-speed automaticDL3
Kia Sportage 20261.5L Turbo-GDi180 hp / 253 N·m7-speed DCTNQ5

Three observations on the map. First, the Sonata and K5 carry the same 1.5T engine with the same 253 N·m torque figure — they differ in body, equipment and brand, not in powertrain. Second, the Sportage 1.5T uses a different transmission (DCT versus automatic) but the engine itself is the same Smartstream 1.5T. Third, the Elantra is the only one in the group running a naturally-aspirated engine, which means its cooling and ignition parts carry a different sub-family of OE references even though they share the same generation of underlying architecture. The shared sub-systems are the reason a distributor can build a family-wide parts programme; the engine-specific items are the reason a careful OE cross-reference still matters.

03 Six High-Turnover Parts Systems

The six parts systems that drive the Hyundai/Kia family wholesale programme are: cooling system (radiator, condenser, cooling fan, thermostat), ignition (ignition coil, spark plug, ignition wires on older applications), engine accessories (alternator, starter, water pump, timing chain), sensors (crankshaft, camshaft, oxygen, MAF), filters (oil, air, cabin, fuel), and suspension top mounts (front strut mount, rear shock mount). Each system carries OE references that vary by vehicle, but the underlying part architecture is largely common across the family.

The table below summarises the OE reference commonality at the system level. The "common" tag means the same OE family series applies across two or more of the four vehicles; "split" means the references diverge by vehicle even though the part function is identical.

SystemOE CommonalityNotes for Wholesale Buyers
Cooling system (radiator, condenser, fan)Split by engine code1.5L MPI radiator ≠ 1.5T radiator; condenser family common on Sonata/K5
Ignition system (coil, plug)Common on 1.5T familySonata/K5/Sportage 1.5T share ignition coil family; Elantra split
Engine accessories (alternator, starter, water pump)Split by engine codeHigher-output 1.5T alternator ≠ 1.5L NA alternator
Sensors (CKP, CMP, O2, MAF)Common on 1.5T familyConnector types harmonised across the 1.5T platform
Filters (oil, air, cabin, fuel)Partially commonCabin filter housing dimensions common on Sonata/K5; oil filter split by engine
Suspension top mounts (strut mount, shock mount)Body-specificBody, not engine, drives the part number — no cross-platform commonality

The pattern across the table: powertrain-driven systems (cooling, ignition, engine accessories, sensors) split by engine code; body-driven systems (suspension top mounts) split by body. Filters sit in between because the housing dimensions are body-driven but the filter element dimensions are engine-driven. For a distributor building a Hyundai/Kia family parts programme, the practical implication is that a small common-OE set covers the high-turnover service items while body-specific SKUs are needed only for trim and accident-repair work.

04 Cooling System: Radiator, Condenser, Cooling Fan Across the Family

The cooling system is the largest single category of high-turnover parts in the Hyundai/Kia family programme. The radiator splits by engine code (1.5L MPI versus 1.5T Turbo-GDi) because the heat load and packaging differ. The condenser is more portable across the family — the Sonata and K5 share a common condenser family, and the Elantra carries a slightly different but cross-referenced condenser. The cooling fan assembly splits by engine and again by vehicle, because the Sonata fan mounts in a different orientation from the Sportage fan.

For a distributor quoting the cooling system across the family, the key OE reference check is the 25310-series radiator. Even within a single vehicle model, the 25310-series splits by production month and market — confirm against the latest Hyundai EPC and the latest Kia EPC at quote stage, and use the chassis (VIN) rather than the model name as the cross-reference key. The Sportage radiator in particular differs from the Sonata radiator (different packaging, different outlet orientation), so do not assume Sonata parts fit Sportage even though both run the same 1.5T engine.

05 Ignition System: Coils, Plugs and the 1.5T Family Commonality

The ignition system is the parts category where the Hyundai/Kia family commonality pays off most clearly. The 1.5T Turbo-GDi engine in the Sonata, K5 and Sportage shares the same ignition coil architecture — typically a pencil-style coil per cylinder — and the same spark plug specification. That means a distributor stocking the 1.5T ignition parts can cover three vehicles from one SKU set. The Elantra 1.5L MPI uses a different ignition coil architecture (and a different spark plug), which is why the Elantra ignition parts sit in their own sub-family.

Indicative OE references for the 1.5T family ignition coil run in the 27301-XXXXX series; for the Elantra 1.5L MPI, the coil reference is in the 27301-XXXXX series but with a different sub-family suffix. Spark plugs cross-reference in the 18841-XXXXX series for the 1.5T family. Always confirm the suffix at quote stage; both Hyundai and Kia publish their EPC regularly, and the references can shift within a single model year.

For workshop owners, the 1.5T ignition coil is the highest-turnover Hyundai/Kia part in the wholesale programme: a misfire under load is the field symptom, the coil replacement is a 30-minute job, and the part is priced at the OEM-grade tier where the margin is right. A distributor building the family programme should lead with the 1.5T ignition coil, then layer in the cooling and engine accessory parts once the volume is established.

06 FOB Guangzhou Price Ladder for Hyundai/Kia Family Parts

Parts pricing from China tiers cleanly with certification, packaging and testing documentation. The figures below are indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges for the three-tier structure most factories quote. Treat them as planning numbers for a wholesale programme, not as a quotation.

Note what drives the jump between tiers. For cooling parts (radiator, condenser, cooling fan), the premium is driven by aluminium core construction versus aluminium-plastic and by pressure testing documentation. For ignition coils, the premium is driven by winding quality, epoxy encapsulation and thermal cycling certification. For filters, the premium is driven by filter media grade (standard paper versus activated carbon versus HEPA-grade). For alternators and starters, the premium is driven by copper-wound stator quality, bearing grade, and voltage regulator calibration. Across all categories, the OEM-grade tier is where the long-term warranty story lives, and where most distributors concentrate their stock.

07 Container Loading and Mixed-SKU Strategy

Hyundai/Kia family parts are mid-weight and mid-volume, which makes them well-suited to mixed-SKU containers. A 40HC container of mixed cooling parts, ignition coils and filters maxes out on volume (roughly 18-22 cubic metres of packed parts) before it maxes out on the 26-tonne working payload. Practical loading numbers: roughly 4,000-5,500 radiator assemblies per 40HC in mixed loading; roughly 25,000-30,000 ignition coils per 40HC in coil-only loading; roughly 80,000-100,000 cabin filters per 40HC in filter-only loading. Pair cooling parts with ignition coils in the same container to balance volume and value density.

Mixed-SKU is the standard first-order pattern for a Hyundai/Kia family programme. A typical trial container pairs the four vehicles' high-turnover parts in ratios that reflect the buyer's market: more radiator assemblies for hot-climate markets, more ignition coils for high-mileage taxi fleets, more filters for high-dust environments, more suspension top mounts for rough-road markets. The trial mix is built around 60% cooling parts, 25% ignition parts, and 15% filters plus engine accessories; the second order adjusts the ratios based on the first container's turn-rate data.

For packaging details that matter on ocean transit: VCI bags inside cooling-part boxes, individual plastic sleeves on alternators and starters, stack-strength cartons for spark plugs and filters (these are the highest-volume items by count), and palletised, shrink-wrapped loading with a packing list that maps SKUs to pallet positions. Ask for photos of a mock pallet before the first order ships; factories that pack well are usually factories that do everything else well too.

08 Certification and Pre-Shipment QC

The single most important certification question for Hyundai/Kia family parts from China is the same as for Toyota: whether the factory holds IATF 16949 (the global automotive quality management standard). For a wholesale programme that is shipping to multiple destination markets, additional certifications matter: ECE R90 for braking components (relevant if the programme expands into brake parts), ISO 9001 as the baseline, and for specific markets GCC conformity for the Gulf, GOST-R for Russia, and INMETRO for Brazil. Document the certification against the destination market's regulatory framework at quote stage, because the same part number may carry different certification for different markets.

Pre-shipment QC for Hyundai/Kia parts should run an application-specific checklist. For radiators: pressure test on a sample basis, brazed joint integrity check, core dimensions against OE drawing, and mounting bracket orientation match. For ignition coils: dwell time and peak voltage test under simulated load, thermal cycling at rated temperature, and connector pin integrity check. For alternators: load test at rated amperage, voltage regulator calibration check, bearing inspection, and 12V output ripple measurement. For filters: media integrity check, frame dimensional check, gasket seal check, and airflow rating verification. None of these tests is exotic; the point is that they happen on your order, with your report, before the container is sealed.

09 Frequently Asked Questions

What is the wholesale price of Hyundai Elantra radiator from China?

Indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges: USD 22-35 for the economical tier (25310-series reference), USD 38-58 for the OEM-grade tier, and USD 65-95 for the premium / private-label tier. MOQs typically start at 50-100 assemblies per reference. Confirm the exact OE number against the chassis (VIN) at quote stage because Hyundai splits references by production month and market.

Are Sonata 1.5T and K5 1.5T parts interchangeable?

For powertrain-driven parts (ignition coil, spark plug, alternator, water pump, sensors), the Sonata 1.5T and K5 1.5T are largely interchangeable — both run the same Smartstream 1.5T Turbo-GDi engine. For body-driven parts (radiator, condenser, fan assembly, suspension top mounts), the references split because the Sonata and K5 carry different body structures and different underbonnet packaging. Always cross-reference by VIN.

Do Sportage 1.5T parts share with Sonata 1.5T parts?

Yes for engine-driven parts (ignition coil, spark plug, sensor family, water pump). No for cooling system parts (the Sportage radiator has different packaging and outlet orientation from the Sonata radiator), and no for suspension top mounts (body-driven). The Sportage uses a 7-speed DCT transmission while the Sonata uses an 8-speed automatic, so transmission-related parts are not interchangeable.

What is the FOB Guangzhou price for Hyundai/Kia ignition coils?

Indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges for the 1.5T family ignition coil (27301-series): USD 5-8 per coil in the economical tier, USD 9-14 per coil in the OEM-grade tier, and USD 16-22 per coil in the premium / private-label tier. A typical order ships in coil sets (4 coils per vehicle, 4-6 vehicles per set), so a 24-coil case is the common wholesale unit.

What certification should I demand from a Hyundai/Kia parts supplier?

Ask for four things: the factory's IATF 16949 certificate (verifiable by number at iatfglobaloversight.org), the ISO 9001 certificate, ECE R90 for any braking components in the shipment, and a recent test report for the specific part family (pressure test for radiators, peak voltage test for ignition coils, load test for alternators). For US-bound shipments, add FMVSS compliance confirmation where applicable.

How many Hyundai/Kia parts fit in a 40-foot container?

A 40HC holds roughly 4,000-5,500 radiator assemblies in mixed loading, 25,000-30,000 ignition coils in coil-only loading, or 80,000-100,000 cabin filters in filter-only loading. Mixed-SKU containers that pair cooling parts, ignition parts and filters in ratios tailored to the buyer's market are the standard pattern for the Hyundai/Kia family programme.
