Read the bands, not the points: the spread is where every real variable lives — friction mix, backing plate source, coating, packaging, and whether the quotation comes from a mould owner or a trader adding one margin. Before comparing any two numbers, ask four things: what Incoterm and port the price assumes, what packaging it includes, what the payment term is, and whether the price survives past the first order. A quotation that only holds for the first container is a promotion, not a price.

Volume arithmetic behaves differently for brake parts than for body panels. Pad sets are dense and small: a 20-foot container commonly absorbs 2,500–4,000 cartoned pad sets, so freight per set is modest. Calipers are the opposite — heavy, bulky, often better bought remanufactured locally. Rotors sit in between, and their weight makes the coating decision a freight decision too: coated costs more per piece but ships safer and retails cleaner.

Markings and Certificates: What R90 Actually Certifies

Brake friction is regulated in more markets than buyers assume, and the markings are checked at borders, not just by end customers. The one that matters most across Africa, the Middle East and Latin America is ECE R90 — the UNECE regulation governing replacement brake linings, drum brakes, discs and pads.

Here is what a booth conversation often gets wrong. An R90 approval is issued against a specific product test, on a specific friction formulation — not against a factory in general. A supplier showing one certificate for one pad family has not thereby certified the forty other applications on the sample board. When a booth claims R90 coverage, ask for the approval number, the test report behind it, and the list of applications it covers; then match your OE list against that list. Our supplier verification guide walks the document chain in detail.

Beyond R90, three documents separate a production factory from a packaging operation: a friction-material data sheet stating the mix classification and performance grade; batch traceability linking a carton code to a production date and mix batch; and, for discs and drums, a metallurgy and hardness report naming the foundry. How fast and how completely those documents arrive is itself a quality signal.

Quality Tiers: Where OEM-Grade Sits on the Shelf

Every supplier describes their product with positive adjectives; almost none volunteer where it sits in the market's own three-tier ladder. Ask directly.

TierWhat it means in production termsPrice position (front pad set)Who buys it
OEM-grade (OE-equivalent build)Formulation and backing plate built to the vehicle maker's specification; full documentation; batch traceabilityUSD 4.5–6.5Dealer networks, insurance repair chains, government fleets
Certified aftermarketOwn-brand production with R90 approval where required; consistent mix; branded or neutral packagingUSD 2.8–4.5Distributors, parts stores, workshops with repeat customers
Economy lineCost-optimized mix and hardware; limited documentation; bulk packagingUSD 1.8–2.8Price-driven retail, temporary fleets, secondary cities

The mistake to avoid is buying tier two and reselling it as tier one — the claim that fails is not the friction but the paperwork, because a dealer-grade customer asks for a document chain you do not have. Kingmay Auto Parts, our parts operation in Guangzhou, works the OEM-grade and certified-aftermarket tiers for Hyundai, Kia and Toyota applications with verified suppliers, and the honest tier conversation is usually the fastest route to a workable order.

Toyota, Hyundai and Kia: Brand-Specific Checks at the Booth

Three brands, three different conversations, and a buyer who treats them identically leaves margin on the table.

Toyota. The parc is enormous and aging — Corolla, Camry, RAV4, Hilux and Hiace running ten to twenty years in most target markets — so application depth matters more than novelty. Ask how far back coverage goes, and confirm which axle variants exist per platform, because one Corolla generation can carry two front pad shapes depending on market and trim.

Hyundai. Korean-platform parts reward suppliers with real mould depth on Elantra, Accent and Tucson applications across a decade of production changes. The practical check is the wear sensor: markets differ on whether it is fitted, and a supplier who asks which sensor variant your market uses knows the product. Coated rotors also move faster in coastal markets, where uncoated discs arrive with surface rust that triggers retail returns.

Kia. Sportage, Cerato and Sorento applications overlap with Hyundai part numbers but not perfectly — several discs and pads share references across the two makes while others do not, and a supplier who claims "Kia same as Hyundai" without checking the crossover table will generate returns. Ask for the crossover list in writing. For calipers, remanufactured units with new seals dominate this side of the trade, and the seal supplier's name is worth knowing.

Samples, the Changeover Break and Factory Visits

Phase 1 closed on 19 October, and the 20–22 October changeover break is now the most valuable sourcing window left in Guangzhou this session. The exhibitors have gone home to their factories — which is the point, because friction production has stages no sample board can show: mix blending, preforming, hot pressing, oven curing, and the grinding and painting lines for rotors.

A practical routine with two or three suppliers shortlisted: request samples against your OE list before leaving the fairground, and ask whether a visit on the 20th, 21st or 22nd fits their production calendar. At the plant, ask to see the mix batching records, the press tonnage per pad line, and where finished goods are photographed and coded. A factory that walks you through those three stations without ceremony will run your orders the same way. Our Phase 1 wrap guide on shortlisting suppliers in 48 hours gives the full routine, and our Guangzhou team can accompany factory visits if your flight schedule is tight.

Packing, Shipping and Getting the Container Right

Brake parts ship well, but three details generate most claims. First, rotor protection: coated discs need edge protection and interleaving, uncoated ones need oil film plus VCI paper inside humidity-sealed cartons — a rotor that arrives with freckled rust is a return even if machining is perfect. Second, carton density: pads travel in small cartons, and a supplier who bulk-packs without inner boxes saves cents and costs you shelf appeal; decide the packaging format at the fair, because changing it later means repacking fees. Third, mixed-container loading: ask for the loading plan in advance — heavy calipers at the bottom, discs on pallets with edge guards, pads filling the crown — and confirm pallet heights fit your destination racking.

Documentation is routine for brake friction in most markets, but confirm two points per destination before booking: whether your market requires any conformity certificate for friction materials, and how carton markings should read for customs — part numbers, quantities and "made in China" markings must match the packing list. Suppliers who already ship to your market have this on file, along with a forwarder at Nansha and consolidation options for your other Guangzhou shipments.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are brake parts available at Canton Fair Phase 2 or Phase 3?

No. Auto parts, vehicles and motorcycles appear only in Phase 1 (15–19 October at the 140th session). Phase 2 (23–27 October) covers consumer goods, gifts and building materials, and Phase 3 (31 October–4 November) covers textiles, toys and food. After Phase 1 closes, the routes back to brake suppliers are the year-round online platform and the April 2027 session.

How do I find brake pad suppliers at the fair efficiently?

Search the official exhibitor database by product category (vehicle parts, brake system) before you arrive, and shortlist by who lists OE-number coverage for your applications. On site, the vehicle-parts sections concentrate friction, disc and caliper makers within a few aisles — our Pazhou halls guide shows where.

What certifications should brake pads from China carry?

For markets that regulate replacement friction, ECE R90 approval per product family is the reference standard — ask for the approval number and the applications it covers, not just the logo. Add a friction data sheet, batch traceability and, for discs, a metallurgy and hardness report.

What MOQ can I expect for brake pads at Canton Fair?

Factories commonly quote 100–500 sets per part number for pads, 100–300 pieces for discs and 50–200 for calipers, with lower figures from trading companies holding stock. Mixed-application orders inside one supplier's catalogue are the practical way to fill a first container without inflating any single SKU.

Semi-metallic or ceramic brake pads for hot climates?

Both are used in Gulf and tropical markets. Semi-metallic carries the fleet volume because it handles sustained heat and costs less per set; ceramic wins at the retail counter for quiet braking, low dust and rotor friendliness. Stock both on your top applications and let warranty data from your own installers settle the mix over two or three containers.

Can I buy Toyota, Hyundai and Kia brake parts with my own brand?

Yes — neutral packing and private-label boxes are standard requests at the brake booths. The usual path is the supplier's standard carton with your brand sleeve, moving to fully custom boxes once volumes justify the print run. Confirm the trademark situation for your destination market and keep the OE reference numbers on the cartons accurate.

description: Toyota brake pads and brake rotors wholesale for Corolla, Camry and RAV4: genuine OE references by generation including 04465-0E060 and 43512-06200, ceramic vs semi-metallic grades, OEM-grade certification (IATF 16949, ECE R90), indicative FOB Guangzhou price ladder, rotor coatings, container loading and the six pre-shipment QC checks.

content:
Quick Answer: Toyota brake pads and brake rotors for the Corolla, Camry and RAV4 are the highest-turnover brake SKUs in the global aftermarket — and China's IATF 16949-certified tier supplies them at FOB Guangzhou prices from roughly $4–9 per ceramic pad set and $9–22 per rotor. This guide maps the genuine OE references by generation, explains what "OEM-grade" means in friction and metallurgy terms, gives an indicative FOB price ladder with MOQ tiers, and covers the QC, packaging and container-loading details that separate a brake program that works from one that generates warranty claims.

Open the service menu of any independent workshop from Dubai to Lima and count the brake jobs. The Corolla, Camry and RAV4 will appear on that list more often than any other nameplates — which is why Toyota brake pads and brake rotors are the anchor SKUs of nearly every parts wholesale program we quote from Guangzhou. Demand is predictable, the applications span twenty years of vehicles, and the OE references are stable enough that a distributor can build a stocking plan around them.

This guide is written for parts distributors, fleet suppliers and workshop chains sourcing Toyota brake parts from China. It covers the OE number map by generation, friction material grades, what "OEM-grade" certification actually requires, indicative wholesale pricing, rotor types and coatings, packaging and container loading, pre-shipment quality control, and the regional buying patterns that decide which grade to stock. For the broader Toyota program, see our Corolla, Camry and RAV4 parts wholesale guide.

Why Corolla, Camry and RAV4 Brake Parts Anchor a Wholesale Program

Brake friction is a consumable: a taxi Corolla in Cairo or a ride-hailing Camry in Riyadh can consume a set of front pads every 25,000–40,000 km. Multiply that by the tens of millions of Corolla, Camry and RAV4 units sold since 2010 and you get a replacement cycle that keeps reordering itself, quarter after quarter, regardless of new-car sales trends. That is the first reason brake SKUs anchor a program: the demand is contractual in nature even when the purchase orders are not.

The second reason is fitment concentration. Three nameplates cover a disproportionate share of Asian-brand brake jobs, and each generation uses a small, well-documented set of OE references. A distributor can cover the majority of demand with roughly 30–40 fast-moving pad and rotor SKUs, which keeps inventory financing manageable. The third reason is margin behaviour: because brake parts are heavy, bulky and certification-sensitive, they are less exposed to cross-border e-commerce price erosion than sensors or electronics. Wholesale buyers who master brake sourcing tend to keep that margin.

The counterweight is quality risk. Brake parts carry safety liability, and the gap between a good and a bad Chinese pad set is invisible on a photo. That is why this guide spends as much space on certification, testing and QC as on price.

The OE Number Map: Pads, Rotors and Shims by Generation

Every serious brake order starts with OE references, not with vehicle names — a "2019 RAV4" can carry three different front pad sets depending on market and production month. The table below lists the genuine Toyota references we cross-check most often. Treat it as a starting map: always confirm the final fitment against the chassis (VIN) before ordering, because Toyota supersedes numbers and splits references by market.

VehicleGeneration / YearsFront Pad Set OEFront Rotor OEShim Kit OE
CorollaE170, 2014–201904465-0241043512-0227004945 series (confirm by VIN)
CorollaE210, 2019–202404465-33471market-split (confirm by VIN)04945 series (confirm by VIN)
CamryXV70, 2018–202404465-0E06043512-0620004945-0E071
RAV4XA40, 2013–201804465-0R03143512-0R02004945-0R030
RAV4XA50, 2019–202404465-0E06043512-06200 (US-built; Japan-built splits)04945-0E071
RAV4 (EU 2.5L)AVA42, 2015–201804465-YZZER43512-48110—

Two cross-reference facts are worth memorising. First, the Camry XV70 and the US-built RAV4 XA50 share not just the front pad set 04465-0E060 but also the front rotor 43512-06200 — one pad-plus-rotor combination covers two of the three highest-volume Toyotas on the road (Japan-built RAV4 units split to their own rotor references, which is exactly why VIN confirmation matters). Second, the Corolla and RAV4 families share the 04465-02220 / 04465-42160 pad lineage across several production years, so a distributor stocking both references covers overlapping demand. You can verify any Toyota, Hyundai or Kia part number in our free OE number lookup tool and browse cross-referenced numbers in the brake system OE library.

Friction Grades: Ceramic, Semi-Metallic and Low-Metallic

Chinese factories producing for export generally offer three friction grades, and choosing between them is a market decision, not a quality decision — each grade is correct for a different duty cycle. The specification that actually defines quality within a grade is the friction coefficient stability and the wear rate, both of which are testable (more on that in the QC section).

GradeTypical CompositionBehaviourBest-Fit Markets
Ceramic (NAO)Ceramic fibres, mineral fillers, copper-freeLow dust, quiet, stable at moderate temperatures, gentle on rotorsMiddle East, Gulf fleets, urban ride-hailing, quality retail
Semi-metallicSteel wool, graphite, friction modifiersHigh fade resistance under load, higher dust and noiseAfrica, mountainous routes, loaded commercial use
Low-metallicOrganic base with 10–20% metal contentBalanced pedal feel and price point between the twoLatin America, Southeast Asia, mixed-duty fleets

For the Camry and RAV4, most wholesale buyers default to ceramic for retail packaging and semi-metallic for fleet contracts. For the Corolla — the world's default taxi — semi-metallic and low-metallic dominate because purchase price per set and durability under continuous duty outweigh dust concerns. Copper-free formulations (meeting the increasingly common environmental requirements in North America and Europe) are available on request from the better factories, usually with a small price premium and a longer lead time.

What "OEM-Grade" Actually Means for Brake Parts from China

"OEM-grade" is used loosely in the trade, so it pays to anchor it to verifiable things. A factory that genuinely supplies or mirrors the OE tier will typically hold IATF 16949 certification for its quality management system, produce friction materials that have passed ECE R90 testing (the European regulatory benchmark for replacement brake components, involving performance, sensitivity and fatigue testing on an approved dyno), and — for US-bound shipments — formulate to FMVSS 135 requirements. Documents are checkable: ask for the IATF certificate number and the ECE R90 approval number for the specific friction family, not just for the factory in general.

Product-level markers of the OEM-grade tier include: positive-moulding or at least consistent press density across the pad face; scorching (the high-temperature treatment that burns off uncured resins and reduces bed-in fade); attached or included shim kits engineered for the specific application rather than universal flat shims; chamfered and slotted friction blocks matched to OE noise-reduction geometry; and printed batch numbers that trace back to a production date and compound lot. When we shortlist brake suppliers for our own wholesale program, a missing batch code or "one shim fits all" packaging is an immediate disqualifier.

For rotors, the OEM-grade tier is defined by metallurgy and machining: G3000-grade grey cast iron (the standard the OE tier uses), balanced casting with dense vent-rib geometry, machined to OE runout and thickness tolerances, dynamic balancing on higher-spec references, and anti-rust protection. A rotor that arrives with visible casting porosity on the friction face or more than ~0.03 mm of runout will generate pedal pulsation complaints within months.

Indicative Wholesale Pricing: The FOB Guangzhou Ladder

Brake parts pricing from China tiers cleanly with certification level and packaging. The figures below are indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges for the three-tier structure most factories quote, based on the price bands we see across our supplier base for Corolla, Camry and RAV4 applications. Treat them as planning numbers for a wholesale program, not as a quotation — final pricing depends on compound, coating, packaging and order volume.

TierPad Set (4 pads, FOB)Rotor (each, FOB)Typical MOQWhat You Get
Economical$4.0–5.5$9–13100–200 setsBasic certification, bulk or plain boxes, semi-metallic standard
OEM-grade$5.5–7.5$13–18100–300 setsECE R90 friction family, scorching, application-specific shims, batch codes
Premium / private label$7.5–9.0$18–22300–500 setsCopper-free ceramic, coated rotors, your branded packaging, barcodes

Note what drives the jump between tiers: it is rarely the raw friction material alone. Packaging (printed boxes, blister packs, barcode labelling), coating (silver-zinc or Geomet-type anti-rust on rotors), and testing documentation account for much of the premium tier. Many distributors start an order in the OEM-grade tier with neutral packaging, then move to private-label premium packaging once the SKUs prove their turn rate.

Rotor Types: Solid, Vented, Coated and Drilled

Corolla rear and some base front applications use solid rotors; the Camry and RAV4 front rotors are vented, with the RAV4 carrying the heaviest section of the three. Within a type, the export-relevant choice is surface treatment. Uncoated rotors carry the lowest purchase price but will show surface rust within weeks in humid climates — fine for dry-market distribution, a complaint generator in coastal or tropical markets. Silver-zinc coated rotors hold appearance for months in transit and on the shelf; Geomet-type waterborne coatings (the OE-preferred technology, recognisable by its matte grey-green finish) offer the best salt-spray performance and are worth specifying for anything shipping to humid or winter-salt markets.

Drilled and slotted rotors exist in the Chinese catalogues but serve a different customer: performance retail, not wholesale replacement. Our advice for a Corolla/Camry/RAV4 program is straightforward — stock plain machined or coated rotors in OE dimensions, and leave the drilled segment to specialists. Drilled rotors crack under fleet duty cycles, and cracked rotors come back as warranty claims with your logo on the box.

Packaging, Boxing and Container Loading

Brake parts are dense and heavy, which makes freight arithmetic a core part of program economics. Pad sets are light (typically 1.5–2 kg per boxed set); rotors are not — a Camry front rotor weighs roughly 8–9 kg each, so a 40-foot high-cube container of mixed brake parts maxes out on weight (about 26–27 tonnes) long before it maxes out on volume. Practical planning numbers from our loading experience: a 40HC holds roughly 4,000–5,500 rotor pieces when palletised with pad cartons filling the voids, or around 8,000–10,000 pad sets if pads only.

Export packaging details that matter: VCI (volatile corrosion inhibitor) paper or bags inside rotor boxes for ocean transit; individual rotor sleeves or waxed wrap to prevent rotor-to-rotor contact; stack-strength cartons rated for palletised ocean freight; and palletised, shrink-wrapped loading with a packing list that maps SKUs to pallet positions so your warehouse can receive the container without re-counting everything. Ask for photos of a mock pallet before the first order ships — factories that pack well are usually factories that do everything else well too.

Quality Control: Six Checks Before Brake Parts Ship

A pre-shipment inspection (PSI) for brake parts should be application-specific, not a generic box-count exercise. The six checks we run or require on brake orders are:

  • Dimensional verification against OE drawing: pad thickness and area, backing plate dimensions, rotor diameter, thickness, and hat height — measured with calipers on an AQL sampling basis.
  • Runout and thickness variation on rotors: dial-indicator check at multiple points on the friction face; reject lots showing pulsation-grade variation.
  • Hardness and material spot checks: Brinell hardness on rotors within the G3000 band; friction coefficient test report for the batch (χ value stability across the temperature range is the number that matters).
  • Surface and coating inspection: machining finish, edge burrs, coating adhesion and salt-spray certificate for coated rotors.
  • Fitment trial: sample pads seated in the caliper bracket and rotor on the hub of the target application where fixtures allow.
  • Packaging and labelling audit: correct OE cross-reference printed, batch codes legible, VCI present, carton markings match the packing list.

None of this is exotic; the point is that it must happen on your order, with your report, before the container is sealed. Third-party inspection agencies can execute this checklist at most Chinese brake factories for a standard man-day fee, and we coordinate such inspections for buyers who order through our Guangzhou program.

Regional Buying Patterns: Which Markets Buy Which Grade

After enough containers, the pattern becomes predictable. Gulf and Middle East buyers — the largest single demand pool for ceramic Corolla and Camry pads — prioritise low dust and quiet operation for retail-branded programs, and order coated rotors for the coastal humidity. African and Central Asian buyers prioritise cost per kilometre: semi-metallic friction, higher MOQs, plain packaging, and uncoated rotors in dry climates. Latin American buyers split between the two, with Brazil's high local tariffs favouring more complete, value-added orders (private label, full kits) shipped less frequently. Russian and CIS buyers in snow-belt regions specify coated rotors and value cold-climate testing documentation, since salted winter roads are the harshest rotor environment a wholesale program will face.

The buying pattern that matters most: almost every experienced distributor starts with a mixed first container — pad sets in two grades for their top ten applications, rotors for the top five — rather than betting the program on one SKU. Turn-rate data from the first container then drives the second order. We structure first orders this way by default; see our Hyundai and Kia brake and suspension sourcing guide for the Korean-nameplate equivalent of the same strategy.

Ordering Process, Lead Times and Mixed SKUs

A standard OEM-grade brake order from a verified Chinese factory runs 20–30 days to production completion for pad sets and 25–35 days for rotors (casting lead time dominates), plus 3–7 days for QC and container loading. Economical-tier stock items can ship in 10–15 days. Mixed-SKU orders — pads, rotors and shim kits for Corolla, Camry and RAV4 in one container — are the norm and are how we quote; braking components combine naturally with the wider Toyota program (mounts, filters, suspension bushings), covered in our engine and transmission mount guide, so one container can carry a full Toyota fast-moving program.

Payment terms for first brake orders typically run 30% deposit with balance against documents; established programs move to more buyer-friendly structures. Ask for the factory's IATF certificate, ECE R90 approval numbers and a recent friction test report with the first quotation — the speed and completeness of that response tells you most of what you need to know about the supplier.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the genuine OE numbers for Toyota Corolla front brake pads?

The 2014–2019 Corolla (E170) uses front pad set 04465-02410, and the 2019–2024 Corolla (E210) uses 04465-33471, with several superseding references in between. Because Toyota splits some references by production month and market, always confirm the exact number against the VIN before placing a wholesale order.

Do Camry and RAV4 use the same front brake pads?

The 2018–2024 Camry (XV70) and 2019–2024 RAV4 (XA50) share the front pad set 04465-0E060, and on US-built units they also share the front rotor 43512-06200 — a single pad-and-rotor combination that covers two of the highest-volume Toyotas on the road. Japan-built RAV4 units split to separate rotor references, so confirm by VIN before ordering rotors for mixed fleets.

How much do Toyota brake pads cost wholesale from China?

Indicative FOB Guangzhou pricing runs $4.0–5.5 per set in the economical tier, $5.5–7.5 in the OEM-grade tier with ECE R90 friction and application-specific shims, and $7.5–9.0 for premium copper-free ceramic with private-label packaging. MOQs typically start at 100–300 sets per reference.

Are Chinese brake rotors reliable for Toyota applications?

Yes, when sourced from the IATF 16949-certified tier with G3000-grade cast iron, OE-tolerance machining and verified runout. The reliability gap between tiers is real: uncoated, loosely-machined rotors will generate pulsation and rust complaints, while OEM-grade coated rotors perform on par with boxed aftermarket brands at a fraction of the landed cost.

What certification should I demand from a brake parts supplier?

Ask for three things: the factory's IATF 16949 certificate (checkable by number), the ECE R90 approval number for the specific friction family, and a batch friction test report showing coefficient stability across the temperature range. For US-bound shipments, add FMVSS 135 formulation compliance.

How many brake rotors fit in a 40-foot container?

A 40HC maxes out on weight before volume with brake parts: roughly 4,000–5,500 rotors when mixed with pad cartons, or around 8,000–10,000 pad sets in a pads-only load. Most wholesale programs ship mixed containers covering pads, rotors and shims across their top ten applications.

Quick Answer: The Toyota Corolla family exported from China in 2026 covers three vehicles on a shared THS-II hybrid platform: the Corolla 2026 Sedan 1.8L Hybrid Pioneer at USD 14,000 FOB Nansha, the Corolla Cross 2026 2.0L Intelligent Hybrid Elite at USD 16,850 FOB Khorgos, and the Frontlander 2026 2.0L Intelligent Hybrid Luxury at USD 18,050 FOB Khorgos. This guide compares the three, walks through the shared 1.8L/2.0L hybrid powertrain, the 60-year Corolla nameplate, the Khorgos-versus-Nansha price arithmetic, and the destination markets where the family still moves at volume in 2026.

Walk into any taxi rank from Lagos to Lima and you will find one car doing most of the work: the Toyota Corolla. Twelve generations, more than 50 million units sold, and a nameplate that has outlived every prediction of its decline. In 2026 Toyota's export programme from China is built around a small family that wears the Corolla badge — the sedan that started it all, plus two crossovers that use the same hybrid drivetrain and ride on the same Toyota New Global Architecture (TNGA) platform.

This guide is written for vehicle distributors, fleet operators and dealer principals who need a single reference for the 2026 Corolla family. We cover the three vehicles we quote most often from Guangzhou, the 1.8L and 2.0L hybrid powertrains, the Khorgos FOB price ladder, the destination markets that move Corolla family stock at volume, and the most common nameplate confusion we see between the three. All prices are FOB tier for LHD units; RHD is available on order for select trims.

01 The Corolla Family in the 2026 Wholesale Trade

The Corolla nameplate entered its 12th generation in 2019 and has carried the E210 platform since. In the 2026 export catalogue Toyota splits the nameplate across three distinct vehicles that share the same THS-II hybrid system and the same TNGA-C architecture, but address different buyers: the sedan for traditional fleet and taxi duty, the Corolla Cross for the compact-crossover segment, and the Frontlander for the slightly larger and more SUV-styled crossover market. For a wholesale buyer this is the year to think of "Corolla" as a family rather than a single car — three vehicles with related but distinct parts programmes and price points.

The unifying thread is the hybrid powertrain. The sedan runs the 1.8L 2ZR-FXE Atkinson-cycle engine paired with THS-II, the Corolla Cross runs the 2.0L M20A-FXS engine on the same THS-II hardware, and the Frontlander is essentially the Corolla Cross with a different body style and equipment list. That shared platform means the parts programme is largely portable across the three — a fact that has made the Corolla family a favourite for distributors building out a Toyota parts book on a single OE map.

The other thing to keep in mind is port routing. The Corolla sedan 1.8L Hybrid Pioneer is the price-entry unit and ships primarily from Nansha for the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. The Cross 2.0L Hybrid Elite and the Frontlander 2.0L Hybrid Luxury are heavier, more equipment-loaded, and ship primarily from Khorgos via the China-Kazakhstan rail corridor to Russia and Central Asia. Understanding that routing logic is what makes the Corolla family economical to stock — one sourcing decision per car, not three.

02 Three Corolla Family Configurations and Their FOB Prices

The 2026 Corolla family export range runs three configurations we quote from Guangzhou in October 2026. The table below sets out indicative FOB pricing, the port of loading, and the wholesale role each vehicle plays.

VehicleEngineIndicative FOBPortWholesale Role

Three observations. First, the price spread across the family is roughly USD 4,050 — between the entry sedan and the top-trim Frontlander — which is narrower than the RAV4 family spread and reflects the shared TNGA-C platform economics. Second, the Corolla Cross and Frontlander sit on the same powertrain and the same FOB-plus-margin pricing logic; what differentiates them at retail is body style, equipment content and the slightly larger boot on the Frontlander. Third, the sedan at USD 14,000 is the price reference that every used-Japanese compacts are benchmarked against — and where a new-vehicle warranty plus hybrid fuel economy wins the comparison shopping.

03 The THS-II Hybrid System: 1.8L and 2.0L Architecture

Both engines in the 2026 Corolla family run Toyota's THS-II (Toyota Hybrid System II) architecture — the planetary gear-set arrangement that has been refined since the Prius launched in 1997. There is no clutch, no torque converter, no multi-speed gearbox; the engine, motor-generators (MG1, MG2) and the planetary gear set manage torque flow through the hybrid control unit. For wholesale buyers this is a stable architecture: the same control logic, the same battery thermal management approach, and the same kind of high-voltage cabling that any Toyota-certified technician can service.

The 1.8L 2ZR-FXE in the sedan produces 90 kW of system output, with combined fuel consumption around 4.2 L/100 km on the NEDC-equivalent cycle. It is the price-entry engine, sized for taxi and ride-hailing duty cycles where fuel cost dominates the operating math. The 2.0L M20A-FXS in the Cross and Frontlander produces 144 kW of system output, with combined fuel consumption around 4.5 L/100 km. Both engines are tuned for 92 RON petrol, both carry a lithium-ion battery pack (rather than the older nickel-metal-hydride), and both share the same cooling and inverter architecture, which is why the parts programme on the hybrid-specific items is essentially one programme across the three vehicles.

04 Khorgos Versus Nansha: Same Hybrid, Different Routes

The Corolla family splits cleanly by destination. The 1.8L Hybrid Pioneer sedan clears at FOB Nansha and ships predominantly by RORO to the Gulf (Jebel Ali, 18-22 days), Africa (Durban, 25-30 days) and Latin America (Santos, 35-42 days). The 2.0L Hybrid Elite Cross and the 2.0L Hybrid Luxury Frontlander clear at FOB Khorgos and move primarily by the China-Kazakhstan rail block train (15-22 days to Almaty, with onward transload to Moscow and other EAEU destinations).

The pricing logic is straightforward: Nansha is the port for the sedan because the sedan is the higher-volume unit and Gulf/Africa buyers want fast RORO economics. Khorgos is the port for the Cross and Frontlander because Russian and Central Asian buyers pay for the equipment content and the rail economics favour heavier, higher-trim vehicles. Container loading runs four units per 40HC for the sedan (the lightest of the three) and three to four units per 40HC for the Cross and Frontlander; RORO from Nansha wins on per-unit cost above eight sedans per sailing, and above six Cross/Frontlander units per sailing.

05 Sixty Years of the Corolla Nameplate

The Corolla nameplate has been in continuous production since 1966 — eleven generations in Japan, the 12th in production for export markets since 2019. In export markets the Corolla family has been Toyota's volume anchor in three distinct phases: the E110/E120 sedans that dominated the taxi trade from the late 1990s to early 2010s, the E140/E170 sedans that carried the fleet and ride-hailing boom of the 2010s, and now the E210 platform that anchors both the sedan and the Cross/Frontlander crossover twins.

For wholesale buyers the generational continuity matters because of one specific commercial fact: the parts channel is exceptionally deep. A distributor stocking filters, brake pads, suspension bushings, lighting and sensors for the current-generation Corolla can cover roughly 80% of the previous-generation aftermarket demand with the same OE references or near-equivalents. That is the depth no other nameplate in the export trade matches, and it is the depth that makes a Corolla family stocking programme economically attractive from the first container.

The crossover expansion is a newer story. The Corolla Cross launched in 2020 and the Frontlander in 2021, both built on TNGA-C with the 2.0L hybrid system; both have moved into the global distribution chain alongside the sedan. For a distributor entering the Corolla family in 2026, the practical mix is two sedans, one Cross, one Frontlander in the trial container — covering fleet duty, retail crossover, and top-trim retail in one shipment.

06 Destination Markets for the Corolla Family 2026

The destination map for the 2026 Corolla family clusters around four corridors. Russia and the EAEU is the largest single market for the Cross and Frontlander, where the 2.0L hybrid's fuel economy and Toyota's dealer network give it a service-network advantage over Chinese compact crossovers priced similarly. Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan) takes mid-trim Corolla Cross units through the Khorgos rail route, with Almaty acting as the regional hub. The Gulf (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait) takes the 1.8L sedan in volume for fleet, taxi and ride-hailing, mostly through Nansha RORO. Latin America (Chile, Peru, Colombia) takes both the sedan and the Corolla Cross, with Chile's zero-duty FTA framework making Santiago the cleanest regional price benchmark.

Three market notes. First, the 1.8L sedan's price point at USD 14,000 FOB Nansha makes it the lowest-priced new-Toyota hybrid in the global export trade — a positioning that wins fleet contracts where operating cost per kilometre is the deciding metric. Second, Russia's 2025-2026 utilization fee has pushed buyers toward higher-trim hybrid units where the fixed fee amortises better against equipment value, which is why the Corolla Cross and Frontlander order book out of Khorgos is growing faster than the sedan order book out of Nansha for Russia specifically. Third, Africa's used-Japanese Corolla replacement cycle continues to feed the new-Corolla pipeline — a Corolla E170 sold in Cairo in 2014 is now at the end of its service life, and the replacement unit is overwhelmingly another Corolla, just newer and with a hybrid drivetrain.

The single biggest operational advantage of stocking the Corolla family is parts commonality. The table below summarises the systems that share OE references across the sedan, Cross and Frontlander.

08 The Same-Name Confusion: Corolla, Corolla Cross and Frontlander

The confusion that matters most: a buyer who orders "a Corolla" expecting the sedan and receives the Cross (or vice versa) creates a return-and-refund problem that no one in the trade wants. The fix is to specify by full model code at quote stage — the sedan's E210 chassis code differs from the Cross's E210G and the Frontlander's slightly different body — and to confirm against the buyer's market homologation rules. For a first-time importer, building a small trial container that pairs the three vehicles is the safest way to gauge which configuration wins the local retail book.

09 Ordering Process, Lead Time and Mixed Loading

A first Corolla family order through our desk follows six steps: vehicle-by-vehicle configuration confirmation, market-spec calibration against your country's homologation rules (Russia EAC, GCC, Latin American type-approval), proforma invoice with FOB Khorgos or FOB Nansha terms, 30% deposit, production slot booking (3-4 weeks for non-stock trims, faster for in-port units), pre-shipment inspection with photo report, and balance against shipping documents. In-port units at Nansha ship within 10 days of deposit; Khorgos rail bookings move on the China-Kazakhstan block-train schedule with 5-7 days from deposit to rail load.

Mixed loading across the family is the standard first-order pattern: two sedans plus one Cross and one Frontlander in the trial container gives a dealer a fleet unit, a compact-crossover retail demonstrator, and a top-trim retail demonstrator in one clearance. For Russia and Central Asia, the mix leans toward the Cross and Frontlander; for the Gulf and Africa, it leans toward the sedan. Add a parts package — filters, brake pads, the high-turnover lighting and sensor items — sized to six months of service demand, and the dealer opens with both sales stock and workshop stock from the first container.

10 Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Toyota Corolla family 2026 wholesale export price from China?

The 2026 Corolla family clears FOB Nansha from USD 14,000 (1.8L Hybrid Pioneer sedan), FOB Khorgos at USD 16,850 (Corolla Cross 2.0L Hybrid Elite), and FOB Khorgos at USD 18,050 (Frontlander 2.0L Hybrid Luxury) — all at container tier for LHD units in mid-October 2026 quotations. Volume discounts of 2-4% apply above ten units per configuration.

What is the difference between the Corolla sedan, Corolla Cross and Frontlander?

Three vehicles on the same TNGA-C platform: the sedan (1.8L hybrid, 2,700 mm wheelbase, 471 L boot, fleet duty); the Corolla Cross (2.0L hybrid, 2,640 mm wheelbase, 440 L boot, compact-crossover retail); the Frontlander (2.0L hybrid, 2,645 mm wheelbase, 458 L boot, premium-crossover retail). The powertrains and most hybrid parts are shared; the body panels, headlamp clusters and trim-specific items are body-specific.

Which Corolla family variant is the volume leader?

The 1.8L Hybrid Pioneer sedan at USD 14,000 FOB Nansha is the single largest volume vehicle in the family, because the price point captures fleet, taxi and ride-hailing buyers across the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. The Corolla Cross at USD 16,850 FOB Khorgos is the fastest-growing variant — driven by Russian and Central Asian retail demand for a compact crossover with hybrid fuel economy.

Do the Corolla family variants share parts?

Yes, partially. The hybrid powertrain (THS-II), TNGA-C platform suspension, cooling system and cabin filter are common across the family. Brake pad sets, body panels, headlamp clusters and tail lamps are body-specific and must be cross-referenced by VIN. A distributor building a Corolla family parts programme can lean on a small common-OE set for the high-turnover items and only needs body-specific SKUs for trim and accident-repair work.

Where do Corolla family cars ship from — Khorgos or Nansha?

The 1.8L Hybrid Pioneer sedan ships primarily from Nansha port for the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. The Corolla Cross 2.0L Hybrid Elite and Frontlander 2.0L Hybrid Luxury ship primarily from Khorgos dry port for Russia and Central Asia via the China-Kazakhstan rail corridor. The split reflects destination logistics, not vehicle quality or specification differences.

Is the Toyota Corolla 2026 family available in RHD?

RHD units are available on order for select trims in the 2026 export programme, primarily for distributor markets in Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Gulf where RHD is required. Lead times run 6-10 weeks beyond the LHD timeline because RHD production slots are scheduled separately. Confirm RHD availability and surcharges at quote stage.

Quick Answer: Cooling and engine parts for the 2026 Toyota RAV4 — radiator, condenser, cooling fan assembly, intercooler, alternator, starter, timing chain, water pump, plus the hybrid-specific inverter, converter, MG1/MG2 motor-generators and battery cooling plate — wholesale FOB Guangzhou from roughly USD 18-65 per radiator assembly and USD 220-480 per hybrid inverter. This guide maps the OE references for the 2026 programme, explains the AWD-specific cooling differences, covers the IATF 16949 / ISO 9001 certification that separates OEM-grade from aftermarket-tier, gives an indicative FOB Guangzhou price ladder, and walks through container loading and pre-shipment inspection.

The 2026 Toyota RAV4 is sold in two cooling contexts: the 2.0L M20A naturally-aspirated petrol with a conventional radiator and mechanical cooling fan, and the 2.0L/2.5L hybrid variants with a closed-loop battery cooling circuit, an inverter cooling radiator, and a higher-spec electric cooling fan assembly. Wholesale distributors stocking RAV4 parts from Guangzhou need to plan for both — and that planning starts with the OE references.

This guide is written for parts distributors, fleet suppliers and workshop chains sourcing Toyota RAV4 cooling and engine parts from China. It covers the cooling system (radiator, condenser, cooling fan, intercooler on AWD variants), engine accessories (alternator, starter, timing chain, water pump), hybrid-specific parts (inverter, converter, MG1/MG2, battery cooling plate), the OE number map for the 2026 programme, FOB Guangzhou pricing by tier, IATF 16949 certification, container loading and pre-shipment QC. For the broader Toyota programme covering Corolla, Camry and RAV4, see our Corolla family wholesale guide and our RAV4 2026 vehicle export guide.

01 Why the RAV4 Anchors a Toyota Parts Wholesale Programme

The RAV4 is the highest-volume Toyota compact crossover in the global aftermarket, which means the cooling and engine parts programme is the largest single category of Toyota-branded parts moving through Guangzhou on any given week. Three reasons reinforce that anchor position. First, the installed base: the RAV4 has been a top-three global SUV since 2017 and the typical owner keeps the vehicle for 8-10 years, which generates a deep replacement cycle on cooling system parts (radiators, condensers, cooling fans) and engine accessories (alternators, starters, water pumps). Second, the technical accessibility: cooling and engine parts sit in the category band where independent workshops and even owner-mechanics can perform the replacement, which multiplies the channel beyond the dealer network. Third, the OE cross-reference stability: the RAV4's OE structure on cooling and engine parts has been remarkably stable across the XA40 (2013-2018), XA50 (2019-2024) and the current 2026 facelift, which means a parts programme built around one generation can cover two with minor additions.

The other reason RAV4 cooling and engine parts anchor a programme is that they are not commoditised in the same way that brake pads or filters are. A faulty radiator or a failed inverter sends the vehicle straight back to the workshop; the buyer does not tolerate "near enough" because the failure mode is overheating, hybrid system fault, or a battery that drops out of its operating temperature window. That reliability requirement pushes the buying decision toward the OEM-grade tier, with its corresponding higher margins and longer reorder cycles.

02 The RAV4 2026 Cooling System: Three Radiators, One Fan

The 2026 RAV4 cooling system architecture varies by powertrain, and the variation matters at the parts counter. The 2.0L M20A petrol carries a single cooling radiator, an AC condenser mounted in front of it, and a mechanical / electric cooling fan assembly. The 2.0L hybrid (THS-II) carries the same primary radiator plus an inverter cooling radiator in the lower front grille area. The 2.5L Dual Engine hybrid (the 2026 addition) carries a third configuration: a larger battery cooling plate with its own low-temperature loop and an additional cooling fan assembly on the rear underbody.

VariantPrimary RadiatorAC CondenserInverter CoolingBattery Cooling PlateCooling Fan Assembly
2.0L M20A petrolStandard OE-seriesStandard OE-series——Electric, single
2.0L THS-II hybridStandard OE-seriesStandard OE-seriesYes (lower grille)—Electric, dual-speed
2.5L Dual Engine hybridReinforced OE-seriesStandard OE-seriesYes (larger)Yes (low-temp loop)Electric, triple-zone
2.5L Dual Engine 4WDReinforced + intercoolerStandard OE-seriesYesYesElectric, triple-zone + rear fan

The AWD variants carry an additional intercooler loop on the rear electric drive unit — this is the most distinctive cooling difference for the 2026 programme. A distributor quoting RAV4 2026 stock should confirm the drive configuration (2WD versus 4WD) at the parts order stage, because the intercooler assembly is not interchangeable between the two and is one of the higher-priced cooling parts on the bill of materials.

03 RAV4 Engine Accessories: Alternator, Starter, Water Pump, Timing Chain

The non-cooling engine accessories follow a more conventional map. The 2.0L M20A petrol carries a 12V alternator (rated roughly 100-130A depending on trim), a starter motor, a timing chain (not a belt) and a mechanical water pump driven by the timing chain. The 2.0L THS-II hybrid runs the same engine but substitutes the starter function for the MG1 motor-generator — meaning there is no conventional starter motor on the hybrid; instead, MG1 (the smaller of the two motor-generators in the THS planetary gear set) handles engine start. The 2.5L Dual Engine hybrid carries the same architecture but with a higher-output MG2 and an upgraded 12V auxiliary battery charger module.

Part2.0L Petrol Application2.0L Hybrid Application2.5L Dual Engine Application

Starter motorConventional starter · OE-seriesMG1 replaces starter functionMG1 replaces starter function
Timing chain kitStandard chain kit · OE-seriesStandard chain kit · OE-seriesReinforced chain kit · OE-series
Water pumpMechanical, chain-drivenMechanical, chain-drivenMechanical, chain-driven (higher flow)
MG2 motor-generator—Hybrid-specific · service-onlyHigher-output MG2

Three operational notes. First, the alternator on the 2.5L Dual Engine carries a higher amperage rating because it supplies the larger hybrid battery pack — a 100A alternator from the 2.0L programme will not run the 2.5L Dual Engine reliably, particularly under continuous accessory load (air conditioning, lighting, infotainment) at idle. Second, the timing chain is not a service interval item in the same way a timing belt is, but it does wear, and a noisy timing chain at cold start is the field symptom that drives the replacement. Third, the water pump is mechanically driven and is typically replaced as part of the timing chain service, not as a stand-alone part — distributors quoting either should bundle them.

04 Hybrid-Specific Parts: Inverter, Converter, MG1, MG2 and Battery Cooling

The hybrid-specific parts are the high-value category on the RAV4 2026 parts bill. The THS-II architecture puts five components on the bench that are unique to the hybrid variants: the inverter (which converts DC from the battery to AC for MG1/MG2 and vice versa), the DC-DC converter (which steps down the high-voltage hybrid battery to 12V for the auxiliary systems), MG1 (the smaller motor-generator that handles engine start and balance), MG2 (the larger motor-generator that provides propulsion assist), and the battery cooling plate (which manages the lithium-ion pack's operating temperature). Each of these carries an indicative OE reference that should be cross-checked against the latest Toyota EPC at quote stage.

Two things to read from the table. First, the OE references are indicative — they must be confirmed against the current Toyota EPC at quote stage because Toyota splits references by ECU part number and by production month, and a "2026 RAV4 hybrid inverter" can carry three different G9200-series numbers depending on whether it is the 2.0L or 2.5L variant and which market it was built for. Second, the FOB Guangzhou ranges above reflect the OEM-grade tier with IATF 16949 documentation; the economical aftermarket tier (functional but without OE-grade testing) typically runs 40-60% lower, while the genuine Toyota tier runs 50-80% higher. For a distributor building a hybrid parts programme, the OEM-grade tier is where the long-term warranty story lives.

05 FOB Guangzhou Price Ladder for RAV4 Cooling and Engine Parts

Cooling and engine parts pricing from China tiers cleanly with certification level, packaging and testing documentation. The figures below are indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges for the three-tier structure most factories quote. Treat them as planning numbers for a wholesale programme, not as a quotation.

Note what drives the jump between tiers. For the cooling parts (radiator, condenser, cooling fan), the premium is driven by aluminium core construction versus aluminium-plastic, by brazed versus mechanical assembly, and by pressure testing documentation. For the engine accessories (alternator, starter, water pump), the premium is driven by copper-wound stator quality, bearing grade, and impeller material. For the hybrid parts (inverter, MG1/MG2), there is essentially no economical tier in current production — the OEM-grade tier is the wholesale entry point, and even there the supply chain is tight because the Toyota tier is more closely held than the cooling tier.

06 Certification: IATF 16949 and What It Actually Means

The single most important certification question for cooling and engine parts from China is whether the factory holds IATF 16949 (the global automotive quality management standard, successor to ISO/TS 16949). IATF 16949 certification means the factory has documented process control, batch traceability, corrective action procedures and customer-specific requirement flows audited to the automotive standard. For cooling and engine parts — where a failure creates a roadside safety event, an engine bay fire, or a hybrid system fault — IATF 16949 is the floor below which a parts programme cannot safely drop.

Ask for the certificate number, not just the claim. The IATF database is publicly searchable at iatfglobaloversight.org, and a current certificate with the right scope (cooling system components, electrical/electronic components, or similar) is verifiable in five minutes. A factory that hesitates to share the certificate number, or that offers a "we are applying for IATF" line, is not in the OEM-grade tier and should not be quoted at OEM-grade prices.

For the hybrid-specific parts (inverter, converter, MG1/MG2, battery cooling plate), additional certification matters: ECE R100 for high-voltage components in European markets, ISO 26262 functional safety alignment for the inverter control software, and UN 38.3 for any battery-adjacent component that ships with lithium content. Document the certification against the destination market's regulatory framework at quote stage, because the same part number may carry different certification for Russia, the GCC and Latin America.

07 Container Loading and Pre-Shipment QC

Cooling and engine parts are denser and heavier than typical aftermarket parts, so freight arithmetic matters. A 40HC container of mixed cooling parts maxes out on volume before it maxes out on weight (roughly 4,000-6,000 radiator assemblies depending on packaging), while a pure inverter shipment maxes out on value per cubic metre. Practical loading: pair cooling parts with hybrid parts in the same container to balance volume and weight; palletise with stack-strength cartons and shrink-wrap; use VCI bags inside boxes for the metal-heavy cooling parts to prevent corrosion in ocean transit.

Pre-shipment QC for cooling and engine parts should run an application-specific checklist. For radiators: pressure test on a sample basis, verify brazed joint integrity, check core dimensions against the OE drawing, and confirm mounting bracket orientation matches the application. For condensers: parallel checks on core integrity, parallel-flow versus serpentine architecture match, and receiver drier / pressure port alignment. For alternators: load test at rated amperage, voltage regulator calibration check, and bearing inspection. For hybrid inverters: high-voltage isolation test, control module communication check, and thermal cycling under load. None of these tests is exotic; the point is that they happen on your order, with your report, before the container is sealed. Third-party inspection agencies can execute the checklist at most Chinese parts factories for a standard man-day fee.

The OE references that anchor the RAV4 2026 cooling and engine parts programme follow the Toyota convention: 16400-series for the primary radiator, 88450-series for the AC condenser, 27060-series for the alternator, 16300-series for the cooling fan assembly, and the hybrid-specific G9200/G92A0/88100/19100/19200 series for the inverter, converter and motor-generators. Second, the G9200-series inverter carries different part numbers for the 2.0L and 2.5L hybrid systems because the inverter capacity calibration differs, even though the physical housing dimensions may look similar. Verify every reference against the latest Toyota EPC before placing the order.

09 Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Toyota RAV4 2026 radiator wholesale price from China?

Indicative FOB Guangzhou ranges: USD 18-28 for the economical tier (2.0L petrol), USD 32-48 for the OEM-grade tier (2.0L petrol), USD 55-75 for the premium / private-label tier. The hybrid radiator (2.0L and 2.5L Dual Engine) carries a 30-50% premium over the petrol equivalent. MOQs typically start at 50-100 assemblies per reference.

Are RAV4 cooling parts different for the 2WD and 4WD variants?

Yes. The 4WD variants (Dual Engine 4WD Luxury and Flagship) carry an additional intercooler loop on the rear electric drive unit and a triple-zone cooling fan assembly with an additional rear fan. The 2WD variants carry the simpler single-fan architecture. Confirm drive configuration at the parts order stage because the intercooler is not interchangeable between 2WD and 4WD.

What is the FOB Guangzhou price for the RAV4 hybrid inverter?

The OEM-grade tier runs USD 220-380 for the 2.0L THS-II inverter and USD 280-480 for the 2.5L Dual Engine inverter, both FOB Guangzhou. The premium / private-label tier runs USD 500-780. There is essentially no economical aftermarket tier for current-generation RAV4 hybrid inverters because Toyota's supply chain is closely held and independent replacements are restricted to IATF 16949-certified factories.

What certification should I demand from a RAV4 parts supplier?

Ask for four things: the factory's IATF 16949 certificate (verifiable by number at iatfglobaloversight.org), the ISO 9001 certificate, ECE R100 for hybrid high-voltage components (for European-market shipments), and a recent pressure-test / load-test report for the specific part family. For US-bound shipments, add FMVSS compliance confirmation where applicable.

How many RAV4 radiators fit in a 40-foot container?

A 40HC holds roughly 4,000-6,000 radiator assemblies in standard export packaging, depending on whether the shipment is pure radiators (volume-limited) or mixed with condensers, cooling fans and other cooling parts. Inverter shipments are typically lower-volume per container (a few hundred units), so they pair well with radiators and condensers to balance volume and value density.

Do RAV4 2026 parts share with the 2025 or 2024 model year?

Yes, partially. The 2.0L M20A cooling system and engine accessories are largely carryover from 2023-2025 production. The 2.5L Dual Engine hybrid is the new addition for 2026 and carries revised inverter, battery cooling and MG2 references that did not exist in the 2025 programme. A distributor stocking the 2023-2025 RAV4 range can extend into the 2026 programme by adding only the 2.5L-specific hybrid parts.

OE references are indicative and must be confirmed at quote stage.

content:
Quick Answer: The 2026 Toyota RAV4 export range from China clears FOB Khorgos from USD 21,880 (Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD Luxury) and FOB Nansha from USD 22,500 (NEW Face 2.0L Gasoline 2WD Deluxe), with the 2.0L Hybrid AWD and 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS bracketing the upper end around USD 25,400-26,200. This guide walks through the five configurations we quote from Guangzhou, the Khorgos-versus-Nansha FOB spread, three powertrains (1.8L/2.0L/2.5L), container loading at four-to-five units per 40HC, and the destination markets where RAV4 2026 stock is moving.

If a wholesale vehicle desk in Guangzhou has a single recurring question from overseas buyers in 2026, it is some version of "is the new RAV4 priced below last year, and which port gives the better FOB". The 2026 RAV4 — the fifth-generation facelift that runs the 1.8L/2.0L/2.5L powertrain family with both a classical Toyota hybrid system and a brand-new "Dual Engine" 2.5L setup — answers both questions. Pricing is more competitive than 2025 at the trim level, and the split between Khorgos dry port (Kazakhstan/China border, rail gateway to Russia and Central Asia) and Nansha port (Guangzhou, deep-water for the Gulf, Africa and Latin America) lets a distributor route stock by destination without paying for two inventories.

This guide is written for vehicle distributors, fleet buyers and trade dealers who need a single reference for the 2026 RAV4 export programme. We cover the five configurations we quote most often, the Khorgos-versus-Nansha price arithmetic, the three powertrains, container loading, the destination market map, and what changed between RAV4 2025 and RAV4 2026. All prices are FOB tier for LHD units; RHD is available on order for select trims.

01 The RAV4 2026 in the Wholesale Export Trade

The RAV4 sits in the segment that drives global SUV volume: five-seat compact crossover, 2,690 mm wheelbase, two-row practicality, and a powertrain family wide enough to span the price spectrum from a fleet taxi to a flagship retail unit. In the 2026 model year Toyota has broadened the export range with the new "Dual Engine" 2.5L hybrid system, refreshed the front face across the line, and kept the 2.0L naturally-aspirated petrol as the entry unit. For wholesale buyers this is the year the RAV4 stops being one product and becomes a small family — five configurations we can quote from stock, each with a defined role in the global distribution chain.

The trade pattern that emerges is unsurprising: Khorgos-bound units tend to be the higher-trim hybrid and the Dual Engine 4WD versions, because Central Asian and Russian buyers pay for the equipment content and the rail economics favour heavier trim; Nansha-bound units are a mix of the 2.0L Deluxe (the price-entry fleet trim), Dual Engine 4WD for Gulf retail, and the 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS for Africa and Latin America, where RORO economics dominate.

Two reference points to keep in mind. First, the 2026 RAV4 still uses Toyota's classical THS-II hybrid architecture on the 2.0L and a higher-output variant on the 2.5L — there is no radical powertrain redesign this year, which means the parts channel built up around the previous three model years carries forward cleanly. Second, container loading has not changed: a 40-foot high-cube holds four units in standard wheel-frame racks (five possible with light trim and frame optimisation). For a first-time importer, that loading arithmetic is the planning number that decides whether container freight or RORO is the right mode.

02 Five 2026 RAV4 Configurations and Their FOB Prices

The 2026 RAV4 export range, as we quote it from Guangzhou in October 2026, runs five configurations. The table below sets out indicative FOB pricing, the port of loading, and the role each trim plays in the wholesale trade.

ConfigurationIndicative FOBPortWholesale Role

Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD FlagshipUSD 22,880KhorgosTop-trim retail, equipment-loaded
NEW Face 2.0L Gasoline 2WD DeluxeUSD 22,500NanshaFleet / ride-hailing / price-entry
2.0L Hybrid AWDUSD 25,400Khorgos (FOB)Mid-trim hybrid, AWD demand markets
2.0 双擎运动 PLUSUSD 26,200KhorgosSport-tuned hybrid retail, top of range

Read the prices as a working guide, not a quotation. The numbers reflect mid-October 2026 quotations at container tier for LHD units; volume, trim mix and market-specific calibration move the final figure, and trim levels split further within each configuration (Luxury versus Flagship, Deluxe versus Deluxe Plus). What the table tells you is the price spread: roughly USD 4,300 between the entry 2.0L Deluxe and the top-spec 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS, with the Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD units clustered in the USD 21,800-22,900 band where most of the wholesale volume actually moves.

03 Three Powertrains: 1.8L, 2.0L and 2.5L Hybrid Architecture

The 2026 RAV4 export programme carries three engine families. The 2.0L M20A naturally-aspirated petrol is the fleet-and-price-entry unit — 127 kW and 203 N·m, paired with a Direct Shift CVT, tuned for 92 RON and inexpensive maintenance. The 2.0L hybrid (the THS-II architecture Toyota has carried since the 2020 model year) layers two electric motors onto a 2.0L Atkinson-cycle engine for 160 kW of system output, with combined fuel consumption around 4.7 L/100 km. The 2.5L Dual Engine hybrid is the new powertrain for 2026 — a 2.5L Dynamic Force engine with a higher-output motor generator set, rated at roughly 160 kW of system output in 2WD form and 168 kW with the rear e-axle engaged (the 4WD variants on the price list). The Dual Engine 2.5L is the configuration most wholesale buyers ask about: the mechanical layout is conventional Toyota hybrid — planetary gear set, no clutch, no torque converter — but the rear electric drive unit on 4WD variants is integrated into the rear subframe for true torque-vectoring behaviour on loose surfaces, which is exactly the capability the Russian and Central Asian order book is paying for.

04 Khorgos Versus Nansha: Port Choice and FOB Spread

The split between Khorgos dry port and Nansha port is the operational decision that defines a RAV4 export programme. Khorgos sits on the Kazakhstan/China border and feeds the China-Europe rail corridor via the Caspian and Russian rail networks — the gateway to Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and the wider Central Asian distribution chain. Nansha is the deep-water port in Guangzhou, with RORO and container services to Vladivostok, the Gulf, Africa and Latin America. The FOB spread between the two reflects inland handling and routing economics, not raw vehicle cost.

RouteTypical loading portLead time to marketBest-fit destination

China-Russia RORONansha port7-12 days to VladivostokRussian Far East, Mongolia
China-Gulf container / RORONansha port18-22 days to Jebel AliUAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait
China-Africa RORONansha port25-30 days to DurbanSouth Africa, East Africa
China-Latin America containerNansha port35-42 days to Santos / BuenaventuraBrazil, Chile, Peru, Colombia

Three operational notes. First, Khorgos rail freight from Guangzhou to Khorgos itself runs roughly USD 1,800-2,400 per vehicle, which is why the FOB price at Khorgos is comparable to FOB Nansha — the rail leg is internalised in the FOB tier at the border. Second, RORO economics from Nansha beat container freight above eight units per sailing on the Russia and Gulf lanes, and beat container above ten on Africa and Latin America. Third, for Russia specifically, the 2025-2026 utilization fee schedule now adds more than the customs duty on sub-2.0-litre petrol units, which has pushed the Russian order book toward higher-trim hybrid units where the fixed fee amortises better against equipment value — exactly why our 2.5L Dual Engine 4WD stock at Khorgos runs hot through the autumn.

05 Container Loading and Container Economics

RAV4 container loading follows the standard wheel-frame rack method used across compact SUVs. The standard count is four units per 40-foot high-cube; five is achievable on lighter trims with frame optimisation but reduces the working load margin. Below eight units per sailing, container freight is the cheaper mode for any port pair; above eight, RORO wins on per-unit cost for the Russia, Gulf and Africa lanes. Khorgos rail bookings are unit-by-unit on the China-Kazakhstan rail block trains; Nansha sailings pair container freight for 1-7-unit orders with RORO for 8+ unit orders.

The average deck-loaded weight per RAV4 unit is roughly 1.6-1.7 tonnes depending on trim, which puts a 40HC close to its 26-tonne working payload on a four-unit load. Distributors who try to squeeze a fifth unit into a 40HC risk axle-weight and stack-height penalties at the loading port, which we have seen delay shipments and trigger reloading fees. Plan the four-unit container as the safe ceiling, the five-unit container as the optimisation that requires supplier-side approval at quote stage.

06 RAV4 2026 Versus RAV4 2025: What Changed

For wholesale buyers the year-on-year changes matter more than the press-release headlines. The 2026 RAV4 carries the new "Dual Engine" 2.5L hybrid system as a fourth powertrain option, the front face refresh across the line, an updated multimedia system with the newer Toyota OS, and revised trim walk — Luxury, Flagship, Deluxe, Deluxe Plus and the new 双擎运动 PLUS at the top. The 2.0L Hybrid AWD carries forward from 2025 with minor calibration updates; the 2.0L petrol Deluxe continues essentially unchanged. The 1.8L hybrid that opened the 2025 line is being phased down in the 2026 export catalogue, with remaining stock in Nansha on order-only.

Top trim2.0L Hybrid AWD Limited2.0 双擎运动 PLUSTop-spec pricing up roughly USD 800-1,200
Parts carryover—~85% carryover from 2025Existing parts programmes continue

The carryover figure is the one that matters to parts distributors. Roughly 85% of 2025 RAV4 service parts — filters, brake components, suspension bushings, sensors, lighting — apply unchanged to the 2026 model year. For a distributor already stocking the 2025 range, the 2026 addition is essentially a vehicle-sales story, not a parts re-tooling story.

07 Key Destination Markets for RAV4 2026

The destination map for 2026 RAV4 stock from Guangzhou clusters around four corridors. Russia and the EAEU (the largest single corridor, cleared under the EAC framework TR CU 018/2011, with SBKTS per-unit approval for commercial lots) takes the bulk of the Dual Engine 4WD Luxury and Flagship units via Khorgos rail. Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan) takes mid-trim hybrid units by the same rail route, with Almaty acting as the regional stocking hub for sub-distribution. The Gulf (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait) takes the Dual Engine 2WD versions and the 2.0L Deluxe for fleet and ride-hailing, mostly through Nansha RORO. Latin America (Chile, Peru, Colombia, Mexico) takes the 2.0L petrol Deluxe and the 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS retail, with the price-entry Deluxe the volume unit under each country's FTA framework.

Chile clears Chinese-built vehicles at zero duty under the China-Chile FTA, which makes Santiago the cleanest regional price benchmark for the 2.0L Deluxe and the 2.0L Hybrid AWD — the landed figure is almost pure FOB plus logistics. The Gulf's 5% import duty and 5% VAT stack makes Dubai the second-most-transparent benchmark; Saudi Arabia's higher ad valorem structure and Saudi specifications on lighting and tyres push the order book toward Nansha RORO with local fitment. Africa's volume buyers (Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana) order the 2.0L petrol Deluxe specifically because the absence of a hybrid battery simplifies field service — a calculation that holds across the continent.

08 OE References and the Parts Pipeline

Wholesale RAV4 buyers should think about parts at the same time they plan the vehicle order. The OE references we cross-check most often for the 2026 export programme cover the high-turnover systems: radiator, condenser, alternator, hybrid inverter (where applicable), brake pads, brake rotors, cabin filter and oil filter. Toyota's OE structure is stable across model years, which means a distributor quoting RAV4 2026 stock can lean on a parts programme built around the 2023-2025 references. A few indicative references, to be confirmed against the current supplier catalogue:

The XXXXX placeholders above indicate reference numbers that must be cross-checked against the latest Toyota EPC at quote stage — Toyota splits references by production month, market and engine code, so a "2026 RAV4" can carry three different brake pad references depending on where it was built. For hybrid-specific parts (inverter, converter, MG1/MG2 motor-generators, battery cooling plate), the Toyota supply chain is tighter than for the petrol equivalents — independent replacement options exist for the OEM-grade tier, but require specialist verification. Our dedicated RAV4 2026 cooling and engine parts wholesale guide covers the full parts programme in detail.

09 Ordering Process, Lead Time and Mixed Loading

A first RAV4 2026 order through our desk follows six steps: configuration and market-spec confirmation against your country's homologation rules (Russia EAC, GCC, Latin American type-approval), proforma invoice with FOB Khorgos or FOB Nansha terms, 30% deposit, production slot booking (3-4 weeks if the configuration is not in port stock, faster for in-stock units), pre-shipment inspection with photo report, and balance against shipping documents. In-stock units at Nansha ship within 10 days of deposit; Khorgos rail bookings move on the China-Kazakhstan block-train schedule, with 5-7 days from deposit to rail load.

Mixed loading keeps first orders low-risk: a typical trial container pairs two or three RAV4 units with a parts package sized to six months of service demand — filters, brake pad sets, suspension bushings, the high-turnover lighting items — so the dealer opens with both sales stock and workshop stock in one clearance. For Russia and Central Asia, we recommend at least one Dual Engine 4WD unit as a flagship demonstrator plus two 2.0L Hybrid AWD units for the volume retail book; for the Gulf and Latin America, the 2.0L Deluxe plus a 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS retail demonstrator is the more common trial mix.

10 Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Toyota RAV4 2026 wholesale export price from China?

The 2026 RAV4 export range clears FOB Khorgos from USD 21,880 (Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD Luxury) and FOB Nansha from USD 22,500 (NEW Face 2.0L Gasoline 2WD Deluxe), with the 2.0L Hybrid AWD at USD 25,400 and the 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS at USD 26,200 — all at container tier for LHD units in mid-October 2026 quotations. Volume discounts of 2-4% apply above ten units per configuration.

Which Toyota RAV4 2026 configuration is the wholesale volume leader?

The Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD Luxury at USD 21,880 FOB Khorgos is the single largest volume configuration we move, because it sits at the price point where Russia's EAEU buyers, Central Asian distributors and Gulf fleet operators all converge. The Dual Engine 4WD Flagship at USD 22,880 carries the retail demonstrator role, while the 2.0L Deluxe at USD 22,500 FOB Nansha dominates the price-entry fleet trade.

How many RAV4 2026 units fit in a 40-foot container?

Standard wheel-frame rack loading carries four units per 40-foot high-cube. Five units is achievable on lighter trims with frame optimisation but reduces the working load margin. RORO from Nansha becomes more economical than container freight above eight units per sailing for the Russia, Gulf and Africa lanes.

What is the difference between Khorgos and Nansha FOB pricing for the RAV4 2026?

Khorgos FOB pricing reflects the China-Kazakhstan rail leg internalised at the border — most Dual Engine 4WD and 2.0L Hybrid AWD stock loads at Khorgos for the Russia and Central Asia corridor. Nansha FOB pricing is the deep-water port quote for the 2.0L Deluxe and the 2.0 双擎运动 PLUS retail trade. The two routes are operationally distinct: rail from Khorgos to Almaty/Moscow transload versus RORO from Nansha to Vladivostok, Jebel Ali, Durban or Santos.

Is the RAV4 2026 available with all-wheel drive?

Yes. The Dual Engine 2.5L 4WD Luxury and Flagship both carry the rear electric drive unit integrated into the rear subframe, giving true torque-vectoring AWD behaviour on loose surfaces. For Russia and Central Asia the AWD variants dominate the order book; for the Gulf and Latin America the 2WD configurations are the volume units.

Does the Toyota RAV4 2026 share parts with the 2025 model year?

Yes, roughly 85% of 2025 RAV4 service parts carry over to 2026. The new Dual Engine 2.5L hybrid system adds a small set of hybrid-specific parts (inverter, battery cooling, MG2 motor-generator) on top of the existing 2.0L programme. Distributors stocking the 2025 range can extend their parts programme into 2026 without re-tooling inventory.
